items.statement: OLX acquisition goodwill on balance sheet; no amortization planned; future M&A only if value-creating
items.quote: The OLX acquisition has been captured in our goodwill. The acquisition will value itself is captured in our goodwill, which is reflecting on our balance sheet. And actually, the objective is to give a return on that capital employed and not write it off because we obviously believe that the acquisition itself is value creating.

items.statement: Buybacks and dividends considered but constrained by regulations; will distribute when permitted
items.quote: We would absolutely look at buybacks and dividends as we think that money can be distributed back. There is regulation today dictating what quantum of buybacks and dividend distribution we can do. So we obviously have to work within the guidelines of the regulation, and we're restricted from doing certain things by regulation itself.

items.statement: ESOP cost ~INR6 crores per quarter expected to continue in FY25
items.quote: We can expect the ESOP cost to be around this range in the next year too.

items.statement: Consumer group revenue split: OEM 65%, dealers 35% in Q4 FY24; repo share 49% for FY24
items.quote: 85%, 15% is new and used, OEM dealers about 65%, 35% in Q4, which is quite stable. In fact, some of the other metrics were repo for the year is about 49%, which is down -- 49% is slightly lower.

items.statement: No further one-off write-offs anticipated after discontinuing C2B business
items.quote: Actually, the only write-off we had was on discontinuing a business, which we had said we're discontinuing. Otherwise, we never had one anyway. So I don't want to talk about the future, but clearly, in the last couple of years, the only thing has really been the one discontinuing business, which is a company, which we acquired and kept the classified as discontinuing C2B, but there are no anticipa

items.statement: OLX traffic ~30 million monthly UVs, steady with marginal growth
items.quote: I think the traffic tends to be about 30-odd million UVs a month. As I said, a large part of it is on an app on a phone, almost all of it is -- I mean, zero of -- net of market -- there's no marketing cost to this revenue to this traffic, sorry, which is making it -- giving the OLX business, strong margins.

items.statement: OLX focus: grow used car classifieds in next 2 quarters, then non-auto segments (homes, jobs, electronics) in 6-12 months
items.quote: So clearly for us in the immediate future, I would say, next two quarters would be focusing on the used classified business, something we understand well as a group. And that would be the big focus for us, I would say, next two quarters. Post the two quarters, we're also extremely optimistic about the non-auto side.

items.statement: Consumer group growth expected well above 2x car industry growth (0-5%) in FY25
items.quote: First, the consumer group. This y ear, at least, it has to go higher than the car industry does because car industry is supposed to be zero to five. So we're hoping that the consumer group growth is much, much stronger than double, the new car industry growth for sure

items.statement: Remarketing business: retail growth focus, repo volumes hoped to have bottomed out
items.quote: Shriram Automall, you're right. I think the two things, one is to keep in the retail business and the fall in repossession is probably we're hoping bottomed out. But yes, it is to keep growing the retail business, and repossession during the year will probably come back and volumes will increase there.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 63% YoY vs 32% revenue growth in FY24; profit growth 1.5-2x revenue growth expected
items.quote: And you also indicated earlier that our profitability tends to grow at a much sharper pace than our revenue growth. It tends to be 1.5 to 2x. I would say more 1.5% if revenue was INR100 and profitably INR150. I think that is by 100%, 150%. So -- or 1% or 1.5%. I think I would take that ratio.

items.statement: OLX is number one used car sales platform in India with strong dealer relevance
items.quote: OLX has reasonable rel evance to the dealers. A large percentage of the dealer sales comes from OLX. It is the number one in used car sales platform in the country

items.statement: One-click financing live on CarWale/BikeWale; expanding to OLX in next 2 quarters; monetization secondary to customer experience
items.quote: In the next two quarters, the financing product will get launch there as well. So the intent is, of course, to take because buying one-click journey across all our platforms, including OLX. And the intent is also to get better customer experience.

items.statement: Buyback/dividend distribution limited by Companies Act regulations
items.quote: There is regulation today dictating what quantum of buybacks and dividend distribution we can do. So we obviously have to work within the guidelines of the regulation, and we're restricted from doing certain things by regulation itself.

items.statement: No one-off costs in Q4 or Q1 FY25; Q4 reflects steady state for OLX
items.quote: No, no, we have not indicated that. And there is no -- everything is done. There's no one-off cost now. We had indicated that in Q3, there were some one-off costs. They're not -- there's no one-off costs in Q4 or Q1 next year.

items.statement: Steel business targets doubling revenue in 5 years; franchisee volume target 68 lakh tonnes by FY29 from 32.5 lakh tonnes in FY24
items.quote: In this year, we achieved around 32.5 lakh metric tonne of steel through the franchisee route. In the next 5 years, we are targeting to make it 68 metric tonne through the franchisee route only.

items.statement: Paint business FY25 revenue target INR380 crores vs INR292 crores in FY24; EBITDA margin target 9.5% vs 8% in FY24
items.quote: We are expecting a turnover of around INR380 crores in FY '25 as against INR292 crores in this year. And we are also expecting EBITDA of 9.5% against the 8% in this year.

items.statement: Steel volume growth target 16-17% annually vs industry 9-10%; royalty per tonne target INR500 in 5 years from INR395 currently
items.quote: Right now, March '24 has ended, and the average royalty per tonne is INR395. And in the next 5 years, our target is to bring it to an average of INR500 per tonne.

items.statement: Raising INR100 crores via convertible warrants over 18 months; INR24.27 crores received; funds for franchisee stake acquisition, new ventures, capex, office premises
items.quote: The company is raising INR100 crores through issue of convertible warrants on preferential basis over the next 18 months. Of this, we have already received INR24.27 crores.

items.statement: Greenfield 2 lakh tonne TMT capacity requires INR70-80 crores plant & machinery plus land; working capital INR30-40 crores
items.quote: For the installation of 2 lakh metric tonnes capacity unit, you need approximately INR70 crores to INR80 crores apart from the land because land is variable, wherever you want, the land is not included in this cost, but the entire plant and machinery requires at least INR70 to INR80 crores.

items.statement: Franchisee capacity to increase to 50 lakh tonnes in FY25 from 40-41 lakh tonnes; focus on expanding existing units not adding new franchisees
items.quote: It would be increased to 50 lakh metric tonnes from the existing 40 lakh metric tonnes, 41 lakh metric tonnes to 50 lakh metric tonnes.

items.statement: Steel industry growth outlook 8-9% annually; paint industry CAGR 8-9% to reach INR125,000 crores by FY29 from INR75,000 crores
items.quote: The Indian paint industry is witnessing rapid growth driven by urbanization, rising disposable income and increased infrastructure projects. The industry is currently valued at INR75,000 crores and is expected to reach a size of INR125,000 crores by FY29 implying a CAGR of 9.4%.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA margin 8.74% in FY24; expected to improve as brand expenses not growing proportionately with volume
items.quote: Ultimately, EBITDA was 8.74% last year. Our Brand expenses are not increasing proportionately. Therefore the EBITDA margin will increase and the PAT will also increase.

items.statement: Paint business EBITDA margin 7.7% in FY24, 8.5% in Q4 FY24; turned EBITDA positive from INR0.4 crores in FY23 to INR23 crores in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR23 crores for FY '24 as compared to INR0.4 crores in FY '23, highlighting a strong turnaround in the business. EBITDA margin stood at 7.7% for full year FY '24.

items.statement: Steel franchisee volumes 32.56 lakh tonnes in FY24, up 9% YoY; royalty income INR129 crores, up 13% YoY; Q4 volumes 8.96 lakh tonnes, up 11% YoY
items.quote: Our steel volume from franchisee route stood at 32.56 lakh metric tonne in FY '24 as compared to 29.82 lakh metric tonne in FY '23 with year-on-year growth of 9%. Royalty income through franchisee stood at INR129 crores in FY '24 as compared to INR114 crores in FY '23, a growth of 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: TMT bar realizations improving; average FY24 INR49,000/tonne vs INR52,000 in FY23; recent improvement INR600-700/tonne; royalty fixed INR400-450/tonne
items.quote: Yes, it is increasing. But right now, last year, average is around INR49,000. INR49,000 was the last year average price, which was INR52,000 in the FY '23.

items.statement: Raw material prices (coking coal, iron ore) impact minimal due to asset-light model; franchisees buy semi-finished goods; royalty on fixed per-tonne basis
items.quote: And our asset-light model of Kamdhenu, because all our franchises purchase semi-finished products and convert them to finished and sell them, the raw material prices do not have much impact on Kamdhenu or our franchisees in terms of profitability.

items.statement: Paint business focusing on value-added premium water-based emulsion products; average selling price INR90/kg in FY24, up 14% YoY
items.quote: Average selling price per kg for FY '24 stood at INR90, higher by 14% compared to last year.

items.statement: Steel dealer network 8,500+ registered active dealers; no internal competition; paint dealer network 4,300+ dealers focusing on Tier 2/3 towns
items.quote: All of them are active and registered. And we keep appointing new dealers wherever we need them. Actually, Kamdhenu has a bit of a marketing USP that I don't make too many dealers. Otherwise, they all compete with each other.

items.statement: Kamdhenu holds 22-23% share in branded organized retail TMT market; unorganized players shifting to Kamdhenu franchisee model for brand premium
items.quote: As per our calculation that we have done the share of Kamdhenu in the branded organized market is around 22% to 23% in the in the retail segment, in this also, particularly in the retail segment, Kamdhenu dominates in this segment with the highest sales share of 22%.

items.statement: NCR construction ban Oct-Dec 2023 for 2-2.5 months due to pollution impacted North India steel sales
items.quote: First, if you look at the whole NCR during October to December, there has been a complete ban on construction for 2, 2.5 months due to pollution. So, due to that, there is a dip in sales, particularly in North India. It has an effect on us.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of 31st March 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain debt free as on 31st March 2024.

items.statement: INR100 crores via convertible warrants on preferential basis over 18 months; INR24.27 crores received; deployment expected in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are expecting to deploy this fund in this quarter. In the Q1, we will deploy that. We are working on that.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR2 per equity share for FY24
items.quote: Lastly, the Board of Directors have approved a dividend of INR2 per equity share, reaffirming our dedication to acknowledge and rewarding the trust placed in us by our shareholders.

items.statement: Steel ROCE 28.5% and ROE 21.1% in FY24; paint business PAT INR14 crores in FY24 vs loss of INR11 crores in FY23
items.quote: ROCE and ROE for FY '24 stood at 28.5% and 21.1%, respectively.

items.statement: NCR pollution-related construction ban caused sales dip in Q3 FY24; steel price volatility and raw material cost fluctuations noted as challenges
items.quote: Despite the challenges we witnessed, including steel price volatility and fluctuating raw material cost, we continue to witness a strong volume growth.

name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Limited
Aptus Value Housing Finance India Limited

items.statement: Revenue growth is a derivative of the overall economy and client earnings; management does not commit to a specific growth rate for the next 2-3 years.
items.quote: On on this front how the economy is likely to behave, your guess is as good as mine, but we are definitely a a derivative of the overall economy and earnings.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin dip to ~18% vs ~21% in H1 attributed to unbilled calls at quarter-end; gross margins remain stable.
items.quote: Okay, I think that has more to do with with the unbilled calls towards the end of the quarter should be broadly similar gross margin is what I would understand.

items.statement: Tech backend completely revamped and launched in first week of April 2024 to meet global standards for international expansion.
items.quote: Third and the most important up, more up, most important regular business update was we re -designed and re -developed the entire tech back -end. So that was , easily the most important update from us I list last year. So , we we just launched it in the first week of April, and, like this is the first week of this financial year.

items.statement: Headcount expanded by ~50 people in Q1 FY24; team now stabilized after recruitment and training phase.
items.quote: So, we did that in June, the first quarter was practically spent on recruitments, trainings, recruitments, trainings, and that is it. So , we expanded the company by almost 50 in in terms of number of people that was absolutely wonderful for us.

items.statement: US expert base expanding with 25-30 people working US hours; meaningful revenue from US clients expected in 1-2 years.
items.quote: On the US front, it is almost an independent team. Now , we have almost 25 -30 people, almost 3 teams working US hours. The business generation is still from India , but our Expert base in US has been expanding considerably, hopefully it should pay, pay us back in a few years.

items.statement: Launched visual mapping tools (Value Chains) out of beta; building expert-led courses (Pex-Panel) with a 3-4 member team under Research Head.
items.quote: Finally, somewhere at the end of last calendar year, we were able to launch it for our clients, and we've got some very good response that , that is fast turning our turning itself into a USB of sorts. We have been making a a lot of hundreds of Value Chains now, and updating them regularly.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~80-85% of revenue; concentration broadly unchanged since IPO, though trending slightly lower.
items.quote: Concentration, while within those 10 things have started stabilizing, but at at a top 10 level there is no significant change. It is, it might be on a lower trend. But it's broadly the same concentration even now.

items.statement: Top 4 industry verticals are IT Services, Healthcare Life Sciences, CPG Retail, and BFSI, representing ~60% of business.
items.quote: Industry basis, the top 4 would be top 4 would be as as it was reflected in the Indian economy, the IT services is top, Healthcare Life Sciences is is also amongst the top, CPG retail is, of course, there, and fourth is BFSI. These 4 together represent about 60% of our business.

items.statement: 70-80% of revenue comes from consulting firms (MBBs, tier-2, in-house strategy) vs financial markets.
items.quote: Most of our business actually comes from the consulting industry than the financial industry. We are more represented in the consulting industry which is the Big 3s, the way, the the MBBs, the Big 3s and tier-2 consulting firms, and maybe in-house strategy teams. Almost 70-80% would be from those set of clients.

items.statement: Business model is predominantly post-paid; financial services clients are more prepaid but smaller teams.
items.quote: Mostly, or mostly on on post, all on post -paid. The financial world is more prepaid where the teams are smaller.

items.statement: Holding ~Rs 30 Cr cash; ~Rs 10-12 Cr is residual IPO proceeds, rest earmarked for international expansion and potential inorganic opportunities.
items.value: Rs 30 Cr cash, Rs 10-12 Cr IPO proceeds
items.quote: Cash. Yes, so so out of that, out of that 30 Crores of sorts, I think somewhere around 10 to 12 Crores is the IPO cash or maybe a little less somewhere around 10, Abhishek would be able to give you the precise number, but the rest of it, we intend to use it for expansion outside the country.

items.statement: No specific acquisition targets identified; open to inorganic opportunities if they arise.
items.quote: Well, never say, never. But have we identified something, no.

items.statement: Abhay Sangal (VP-Operations) to take larger role in US Operations; operations to transition to autopilot mode.
items.quote: Abhay, who has been our offset , as of now in, you know, will likely to take up larger role in the US Operations and slowly we'll transition Ops more into autopilot mode.

items.statement: Repeat business high: 80%+ of calls by empanelled experts; 90%+ revenue from clients engaged 2-3+ years, many 5+ years.
items.quote: Two, repeat business, about 80% plus of our calls are done by Experts who are already empanelled with us in India and almost 90% of our business is by is our clients, which are probably 2, 3 years and more with us. In fact, a very significant percentage would be more than 5 years+.

items.statement: Ticket size in India broadly stable; focus on increasing calls per person via tech rather than raising prices; inflationary increases occur.
items.quote: In India we are broadly at the same ticket size. We try not to increase the prices and we try to maintain the same gross margins. But inflationary increases do happen. We rather focus on increasing the number of per person call by empowering our team with more, with better technological solutions.

items.statement: Differentiation via expert curation, reuse rates (double-digit % vs 2-3% for competitors), value chain maps, and analytics-driven matching.
items.quote: We are far more focused on the res earch side of things and focus more on precision. We try to reuse our Experts as much as possible. We have a lot of value chain maps wh ich are which we have shown in the D RHP, a s well as our videos as well as our previous engagements. So, these are broadly 3 or 4 points where we kind of score above

items.statement: US revenue not yet material; current US expert calls serviced from India client demand; export revenue recognition pending.
items.quote: Are those US calls generated from US clients? No, they are generated more from Indian clients looking to speak to US experts. So, that is our kind of a little lengthier, but slightly less costlier way of building up the network based in US.

items.statement: Scalability constrained by premium pricing; future growth requires moving to lower-value, higher-volume expert segments and peripheral marketplaces.
items.quote: So, as of now we are, we are at a very premium price point. So , at this price point, you cannot have thousands of crores market, or even 100. So , at this price point, it's very difficult to absorb these kinds of experts. Over a period of time, we are likely to move towards low value, high volume experts.

items.statement: UCP segment margin guidance maintained at high-single-digit for FY25
items.quote: we still continue to maintain according to our guidance which we have given to the investor community of high-single-digit margins, and we are within that.

items.statement: Projects segment margin guidance maintained at 4-5% EBIT for FY25
items.quote: For the total project business, our guidance on the project business, I would say domestic as well as international has been between 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Voltbek breakeven at EBITDA level targeted by end of FY25
items.quote: we did talk last time when we spoke about breakeven at EBITDA level we said it will be by the end of the financial year ’25. Yes, of course we still maintain that

items.statement: Voltbek targets 10% market share over time
items.quote: And market share, of course we are saying we plan to take it to 10%.

items.statement: Chennai factory Rs 500 crore capex, half spent in FY24, balance in FY25
items.quote: we had already announced that we will do a CAPEX of Rs. 500 for our Chennai factory. So, you can take that, approximately half of that was capitalized, rather capital work in progress for last year and roughly about half will be within this year FY '25.

items.statement: Additional Rs 200-250 crore capex for Waghodia plants in FY25
items.quote: we are also augmenting our Waghodia plants, both the commercial AC, commercial refrigeration, there also we are spending monies almost to the tune of additional more than Rs. 200 crores, Rs. 250 crores during this year.

items.statement: Chennai plant adding 1 million AC capacity from May-June 2024, targeting 3-3.5 million in 2-3 years
items.quote: Immediately 1 million will catch up from this year itself, will start from May, June onwards of at least 1 million to our production capability. Currently our manufacturing plant at Pantnagar is giving us a capacity between 1.2 million. So, I would be able to reach about 2.2 million.

items.statement: Room AC volume grew 72% in Q4 FY24 and 35% for full year, split AC volumes doubled
items.quote: if you look at the growth which we have spelled out, in the Quarter 4 it's more than 70%, about 72% or so. And even if you look at the annualized or the total YTD financial year growth on the room AC front is more than 35%.

items.statement: UCP segment EBIT margin ~9% for FY24, down from historical 13-15% at lower revenue base
items.quote: For the Full Year '24 the numbers would be down closer to 9%, I would say, which we have already reported.

items.statement: Projects domestic business margin better than international, ROCE over 40% on infrastructure piece
items.quote: if you look at this business, return on capital employed on only the infrastructure piece is about over 40%.

items.statement: Commodity prices accelerating upwards and USD-INR depreciation hurting profitability, offset by value engineering
items.quote: commodity prices have started to accelerate upwards, even USD-INR has depreciated over a period of time. Both of these have been detrimental to the profitability of the business. Nonetheless, various value engineering, and cost austerity drives have kept the profits in balance.

items.statement: Inverter AC share increased to over 80% of split AC sales, premium 4-5 star mix improved
items.quote: The expanded product portfolio of Voltas with newer SKUs designed in-house and competitive pricing has resulted in increased share of the inverter AC category to over 80% during the year.

items.statement: Expanding distribution: 350+ exclusive brand outlets, 26,000+ channel partners, 11,400+ Voltbek partners
items.quote: We have een present in more than 350 exclusive outlets, more than 26,000 channel partners across the length and breadth of the country

items.statement: Commercial mining of coal allowed and FDI norms relaxed in mining sector, positive for M&CE business
items.quote: The recent allowance for commercial mining of coal and the relaxation of FDI norms in the mining sector by the government are positive developments for the business.

items.statement: Domestic projects focus on governance, working capital management and high productivity to convert orders to cash
items.quote: The business continues to focus on governance, working capital management and high productivity to translate the orders into profits and in-turn into better cash inflow.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents Rs 2,835 crore as of March 2024, healthy balance sheet
items.quote: The corporate balance sheet continues to remain healthy with the cash and cash equivalents at Rs. 2,835 crores as at 31st March 2024.

items.statement: International projects risk largely behind, Qatar provisions taken, Saudi and Dubai projects executing well with timely collections
items.quote: we are fairly optimistic to not have further set-backs from the geography and the international business should be on its way to deliver positive results in the next fiscal year.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated net profit was Rs.2,614 crores, the highest ever reported.

items.statement: FY24-25 capacity expected to be more or less the same as FY23-24; no net fleet growth currently planned.

items.quote: Suffice to say that the earning rates and the last contract which have happened are between 50% and 100% higher than the rates at which these vessels are currently earning. And the markets continue to be there at close to 2x what these contracts are running at current.

items.quote: We have recently repriced two of our vessels on time charter itself on two-year time charters and the repricing has happened at a significantly higher rate than previously. So, they are at about 40% higher than the previous rate.

items.statement: Targeting 205,000-210,000 tons annual volume by FY28, implying ~15-20% volume CAGR over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We are confident that as we expand over the next 3 or 4 years, which is I believe we are targeting about 205,000 to 210,000 tons a year -- this year, which translates to around 15% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Awarded contract to Mott MacDonald for engineering consultancy to increase ABS capacity to 210 kt by FY28; debottlenecking to raise ABS from 85 kt to 105 kt and PS from 66 kt to 105 kt
items.quote: We have awarded a contract to M/s. Mott MacDonald Private Limited for engineering consultancy to increase the annual capacity of ABS production capacity to 210 kt by FY'28. We are also progressing as per schedule to increase our ABS capacity from 85 kt to 105 kt and PS capacity from 66 kt to 105 kt by various debottlenecking projects.

items.statement: INR 650 crore capex estimate for expansion is preliminary; detailed cost and timeline clarity expected in next couple of quarters after engineering studies
items.quote: The INR650 crores number was kind of a benchmark or kind of a rule of thumb number, which we have taken to get preliminary board approval to pursue engineering studies for the expansion, which is -- which we are undertaking.

items.statement: EBITDA margins stable at 12.2-12.4% in FY24; management believes current blended spreads are defendable and margins should improve with volume growth, product mix enrichment, and cost optimization
items.quote: Notably, PBITD margins were stable at 12.4% , previous quarter 12.3% for the quarter and 12.2% for the year, which is same as previous year driven by our debottlenecking efforts and an increased share of value -added products and cost optimization products.

items.statement: Specialty ABS grades ~60-65% of ABS volumes; developing value-added PS grades (refrigeration liner, high gloss, tint) and new blends (STYROLOY, ASALAC) to improve mix
items.quote: So it's around 60%-65%. It fluctuates again quarter-on-quarter. But on an annualized basis, you can consider that.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through via formula-based pricing with 1-2 month lag; margins well protected despite styrene monomer price increases
items.quote: Yes, that's right. So like I mentioned in previous calls, now this one is that a lot of our business is driven by fo rmulas as well. And in those formulas, we are able to pass on increases in raw material pricing to our customers fairly straightforward.

items.statement: Steam cost savings of INR 1.5-2 crore in last 5 months at Nandesari plant (~INR 4 crore annualized); similar projects underway at Dahej and Katol; pursuing wind-solar hybrid power PPAs for power cost reduction
items.quote: If you look at power and fuel, for instance, and specifically in fuel, we already have incorporated certain systems in our Nandesari plant wherein in terms of the steam co sts in the last 5 months or so w e have seen a saving of close to INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores, just in the steam cost, which, on an annualized basis, probably is going to be more than INR4 crores, just on fuel cost in one of ou

items.statement: Domestic ABS capacity expected to exceed 400 kt by FY27 and 450 kt by FY28 vs ~300 kt currently; management believes market will remain underserved given 7-10% demand growth
items.quote: Even then we believe that in the next 4 years, the capacity from 300,000 tons which is actually slightly higher than 300,000 tons this year fr om what we have gathered data on, we'll exceed 400,000 tons in year '26-'27 and probably go to 450,000 tons in '27-'28.

items.statement: ABS market share increased from ~26-27% to ~30%; PS market share increased from ~17% to ~20%; focusing on OEM engagement for PS contractual business
items.quote: So last year, I think in ABS, we had about 26% or 27% market share. And in PS, our market share was closer to around 17%.

items.statement: Exports not a priority currently; 50% of ABS demand met by imports, focus on capturing domestic market first; open to selective export opportunities if value-accretive
items.quote: So in terms of overall volume growth, we are still looking first to satisfy our existing customers and only then look at exports as a proposition. We have a strong brand positioning also in the Indian market. So it beh oves us first to look at that as an opportunity and only then pursue other opportunities once we have additional capacity already in place.

items.statement: FY24 sales volume 165 kt (+10.7% YoY); Q4 FY24 volume up 25% QoQ; revenue INR 2,222 crore; PBITDA INR 273 crore
items.quote: Our sales volume grew by 10.7% Y -o-Y to 165 kt for the financial year 2024 and by 25% compared to the preceding quarter.

items.statement: China's ABS self-sufficiency and new Asian capacities already creating pricing pressure; normalized margin environment post-COVID; competitive intensity may increase with domestic capacity additions
items.quote: Post -COVID, China did not come back as strongly as was earlier anticipated. There were also new capacities which have come on in China. So there has been a fair amount of pricing pressure from countries like I mentioned, in the case of ABS would have in Korea, Thailand, Taiwan, etc.

items.statement: Agrawal family management took control in November 2022; strategic focus on capacity augmentation, cost rationalization, new products, sustainability, and culture
items.quote: As you know that our management took over the company only in November '22. So it's been about 16 -odd months that we have had management control over the company. And in this time is when we realized, and we announced plans to go ahead with expansion.

items.statement: Power policy clarity awaited for wind-solar hybrid PPAs; Gujarat policy clauses still pending government clearance; state-level approvals affect power cost savings timeline
items.quote: While it's happened in Gujarat as well, but there are certain clauses which still have to be completely cleared by the government. So in any case, that should be done soon and we believe that will add to our kind of power saving as well.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; focus on cost optimization in logistics expected to yield savings next year
items.quote: There are other projects as well, which are in logistics and other areas, which will also lead to significant savings. But currently, it's hard to exactly estimate. I think, we will see the impact of at least some of these things in specifically in power and fuel in this year, in the full year that we see and more so in the next couple of quarters a nd for logistics, you will see in the following

items.statement: Management expects revenue and profit to improve in FY25 but declines to give specific numeric targets
items.quote: We are working extremely hard, and they have reasons to believe in either case, we will be better off in this election year than what we were later or last to last year.

items.statement: Animal healthcare industry grows at 8-9%; Hester grew 12% standalone and aims to maintain or exceed that rate
items.quote: Animal healthcare industry itself grows at a rate of 8% to 9%. We have grown at a 12% standalone basis. So, I think I mean this is the yardstick which is Hester Biosciences Limited 10 May 2024 there and now we either maintain it or get better, these are the only two options

items.statement: Nepal plant turnover Rs. 13.5 crores in FY24 with capacity to do more than double, potentially three times current turnover
items.quote: We did a turnover of Rs. 13 crores. Now, even at this rate, we still have more than double the capacity, three times rather we can do turnover in our Nepal plant from where we are.

items.statement: Poultry industry on upswing; farmers moving to progressive farming and increasing vaccine uptake

items.quote: The poultry infected by feed prices, right now the ingredient prices are even okay. The demand for overall poultry is okay as our economy is doing good . items.quote: Hester Nepal executed FAO tender for the P PR vaccine and anticipating this to carry forward this year.

items.quote: Our profit margins have increased primarily attributed to a strategic share product mix. Furthermore, both EBITDA and PAT missed a growth closely aligning with our enhanced sales performance.

items.quote: So, to answer your question, I think yes, the margins will sort of shift depending on the product mix, but in the coming years, we definitely want to also focus more on health.

items.statement: Lumpy skin disease vaccine development underway using technology from ICAR; dedicated vaccine expected ready by next year when government starts buying again
items.quote: Our developmental activity hopefully next year, around this time when the government starts again buying the vaccine, we should be ready before that for the dedicated lumpy skin disease vaccine.

items.quote: The global PPR eradication program as you know has been spearheaded by United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. items.quote: I am also pleased to highlight there are cash flows for the current year have shown improvement, marking a positive trajectory.

items.quote: Our debt has gone, now more or less it is a very small debt that in fact we have already started paying income tax over there. This is the first time. So, that shows a sign of progress.

items.statement: Quarterly turnover including GST exceeded Rs.100 crores for Q4 FY24.
items.quote: We are very happy to inform you that quarterly turnover including G ST is more than Rs.100,00,00,000 quarterly more than Rs.100 crores.

items.quote: Yes, Vikram we have just to tell you, for the full year volume in the tonnage , in the tonnage is there of the Rs.57,229 is the tonnage volume for the full year Rs.57,229.

items.quote: In the domestic we are able to increase from Rs.48,447 of the last year to Rs.49,662 that's domestic.

items.quote: Internationally is one of the thing it can trigger up. We are a little bit cautious in case of the domestic for this year, which is expected to improve in future but this year we have been cautious considering the receivables only, we were a little cautious.

items.quote: I can talk about our business where we are not owning the aircraft and there is a EBITDA of generally what we are earning is around near to the 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Variable cost component ATF is passed on to customers in real time; contracts are open, not fixed.
items.quote: We basically have our main component, or the variable cost is aviation turbine fuel , ATF, if ATF prices are increasing or decreasing, we pass on to consumer , customer I mean to say. So, we don't get affected by the variation in the oil prices as you can see in the international.

items.statement: Trade payables credit period is 90 to 120 days per industry practice; receivables insured via SBI Life; no bill discounting due to surplus cash.
items.quote: Yes. So, there is a normal industry practice of let say 90 to 120 days.

items.quote: As a result, the Company had become net debt free and Company is carrying a closing balance of cash and cash equivalent of Rs.17,49,00,000.

items.statement: Sold Chennai land; exploring warehouse development in Pune with proceeds; Bangalore property yields Rs.4-5 lakh monthly rent.
items.value: Rs.4 to Rs.5 lakh per month
items.quote: Rental is around Rs.4 to Rs.5 lakh.

items.statement: Actively exploring both inorganic and organic growth opportunities beyond aviation, including roadways (Patel Roadways legacy).
items.quote: So, we are actively looking for the opportunity both inorganic and organic to grow the business, to expand the Company.

items.statement: Pricing environment hardening due to Red Sea crisis shifting cargo to air routes; expect momentum to continue into FY25.
items.quote: Vikram the prices are getting harder definitely as our Red Sea crises and all the other crises happen. So, definitely because what is happening is ocean routes are not available then people have to go for the air route.

items.statement: Expect to maintain Q4 FY24 quarterly turnover momentum of Rs.101 crores including GST into FY25.
items.quote: We expect to keep the momentum for us as a Company also, the numbers which we have in the quarter gone by . We expect to keep that momentum.

items.quote: the airport authority of India planned capital expenditure of 30,000 crore over five years and the government's target of 1000 UDAN routes, to create 1000 UDAN routes will further boost the expansion of logistic into new territories.

items.statement: Tie-ups with all major airlines (IndiGo, Vistara, Air India, SpiceJet, Akasa) mitigate pilot strike risk; no single airline dependency.
items.quote: We have a tie up starting from Indigo, Vistara, Air India, SpiceJet, whatever name Akasa airline, we have a tie up with all the airlines so our operation don't get affected by this strike.

items.statement: Trade receivables insured with SBI Life to cover unfortunate events; no bill discounting currently.
items.quote: we have taken insurance also for our trade receivable from the SBI life. So, if any unfortunate events happen, then they can get the backup from the insurance Company, that we have done.

items.statement: Promoters fully subscribed and oversubscribed in previous two rights issues demonstrating commitment.
items.quote: promoters have shown their commitment, they have fully contributed, contributed more than what was required of their eligible contributors.

items.statement: Khar property attracting interest from big brand for operation; discussions ongoing, details not disclosed.
items.quote: now good interest from the big brand for operating that property. But further details cannot be shared at this stage and discussion stage.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 volume grew 7% YoY and 30% QoQ; FY24 net sales fell 4.3% to INR 669.4 cr with 2% volume decline
items.quote: These efforts started paying off with a quarter 4 showing a 7% volume growth and a 3.7% value growth. For the full year, your company registered net sales of INR 669.4 crores as against INR 699.6 crores in FY23, a drop of 4.3% and a volume drop of 2%.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 5.9% in Q4 FY24; like-for-like EBITDA margin 8.1% vs 7.1% YoY excluding brand spend
items.quote: EBITDA margins on a like-for-like basis, when I say so, I exclude the additional investments that we continue to support the brand expense which is the new TVC. This was 8.1% versus 7.1% Y-o-Y while the reported EBITDA is obviously a little lower at 5.9% margins.

items.statement: Achieved ~3.5% YoY production cost savings on like-for-like basis; gas prices stable sequentially, raw materials softening
items.quote: We continued the drive to optimize our production costs and we achieved a savings of roughly 3.5% Y-o-Y on a like-for-like basis which is at constant product mix and energy cost.

items.statement: GVT share in sales mix rose to 30% in FY24 from 23% in FY23; vitrified-ceramic split now 50-50
items.quote: On the positive side, gas prices also cooled down and this push on retail market through the year has helped us to grow our share of glazed vitrified tiles in the company's sales mix to 30% versus 23% for FY23.

items.statement: Commissioned Dora GVT line (3.3 msqm/yr) ahead of schedule at 18% lower capex; FY24 capex-to-revenue >10%
items.quote: The company commissioned its Dora plant GVT line, the second GVT line with a capacity of 3.3 million square meter annually ahead of schedule and also at a reduced capex cost of about 18%.

items.statement: Dora GVT line ramping up, full utilization expected in ~1 year; overall GVT utilization 75-80% in FY24; associate Proton adding 5.5 msqm GVT in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our associate company in Morbi will also be launching a new line in quarter two with a 5.5 million square meter capacity which will also be available to us to feed the market.

items.statement: Private project order book healthy; government project order book lower due to elections, expected to pick up from Q2 FY25
items.quote: I think the order book on private projects is healthy. The order book on government projects is lesser than what I would want it to be. But as I said, quarter four has been a bit slow on the government front because of elections and all. And we expect that to start picking up from quarter two onwards.

items.statement: Project sales (orders >3,000 sqm) contributed ~25% of FY24 revenue; retail ~75% (including 12% via dealers)
items.quote: Anything which is more than 3,000 meters single location is what we call a project. This contribution was about 25% for the full year. 25% for the full year was split for project versus what we do directly through the enterprise piece.

items.statement: Core cash conversion cycle maintained at 19 days despite higher credit and inventory to support sales
items.quote: Despite supporting sales via higher credit inventory, we still insured an overall healthy core cash conversion cycle at 19 days.

items.statement: Net debt INR 27.5 cr (lower than Dec 2023); new term loan for Dora GVT line, repayments start FY25
items.quote: The net debt is only INR27.5 crores which is in fact lower than what we had in December '23. The gross debt obviously represents the new term loan that has been drawn to fund the Dora new GVT line and the repayments for this will commence only from next fiscal.

items.statement: Board recommended 5% dividend for FY24
items.quote: The Board has also therefore recommended a 5% dividend for the last fiscal.

items.statement: No formal volume guidance; brand spend to continue at 3-5% of revenue through FY25; TV campaign active till mid-June 2024
items.quote: I think 3% to 5% is on an average what we have been spending now for the past few quarters. And I think that should be the broader thing that would be there for the next few quarters as well.

items.statement: Morbi exports fell from ~INR 2,000 cr/month in H1 to INR 1,500-1,600 cr/month in H2; ~50% of 1,000+ units shut in April; US anti-dumping investigation risk
items.quote: And I think exports within H1 were moving towards almost, you know, moving towards INR 2,000 crores a month kind of a figure. As in H2, my estimate is would have come down to about INR1,500 crores-INR1,600 crores a month kind of a number.

items.statement: US actively considering anti-dumping duty on Indian tiles; investigations ongoing

items.quote: So, the capacity which is functional today, our estimate is that it was 9 crores square meters a month of ceramics and another 9 crores a month of vitrified. This is what the functional capacity we estimated in the month of April.

items.quote: Because of issues in the Red Sea, the sink rates going up, insurance charges going up, plus there is now the news on US actively considering putting a dumping duty on Indian tiles.

items.statement: Added 17 new exclusive display centers (Orient Bell Tile Boutique) in FY24
items.quote: The company has also added 17 new exclusive display centers, the Orient Bell Tile Boutique as we call it, in FY'24.

items.statement: Associate Proton expanding 5.5 msqm GVT capacity in Q2 FY25 funded by internal accruals, no equity support from OBL
items.quote: By the way, just for you and of records, they are doing it out of their own internal accruals. We are not paying out any money to them. So there is no equity support from OBL.

items.statement: Granted first patent for antimicrobial/antiviral tile method; targeting hospital projects in FY25 for differentiation
items.quote: During this year, the company has also been granted a first-ever patent for the unique method of preparing an antimicrobial and antiviral tile. This is something which we will be using in FY'25 to win project orders in the health sector.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY25 and aims to sustain it for the next two to three years.

items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 14%, improved by 188 basis points year-on-year as against 12.1% in FY23.

items.quote: So we can expect like 58%-60% of gross margins going forward, I believe

items.statement: Closed footwear demand was weak due to oversupply; consolidation expected but timing depends on market forces.

items.statement: Optical business utilization at sub-50% in Q4 FY24; break-even at 60-65% utilization
items.quote: We won't give specific numbers Ashish for competitive reasons, but it was sub 50% levels.

items.statement: Open order book at Rs 10,290 crore end of Q4 FY24 with Rs 2,064 crore added in Q4
items.quote: Our open order book at the end of Q4 FY24 is Rs.10,290 crores we are happy to share that robust order book edition amounting to Rs.2,064 crores happened during last quarter.

items.statement: Expect inventory normalization in 1-2 quarters; demand recovery visible from Q3/Q4 FY25 with BEAD contribution meaningful in FY26
items.quote: So that's where we stand today. There are efforts going on locally in the US around how the timing can be fast track but currently, the visibility is probably Q 3/Q4 of our financial year, is where we can see some initial impact or benefit and then meaningfully next year

items.statement: Global Services EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% in Q4 FY24 and 7.6% for full year; target 8-10% sustainable range
items.quote: We have been selective in our intake and execution which has helped us improve our Q 4 EBIT DA to Rs.39 crores and EBITDA margin to healthy 12.1

items.statement: Optical connectivity attach rate increased to 13% from 10% in FY24; first connectivity sales in North America
items.quote: Our optical connectivity attach rates have increased to 13% from 10% last year.

items.statement: Global OFC demand projected at 617M fiber-km by 2026 and 666M by 2028 (4.4% CAGR); ex-China ~8% CAGR
items.quote: As we look at the future projections from CRU, the medium term demand for optical fiber cable volumes is expected to go up to 617 million fiber kilometers by 2026 and 666 million fiber kilometers by 202 8, up from 536 million kilometers in CY2023, this is a healthy 4.4% annual growth rate from 2023 to 2028 and approximately 8% annual growth excluding China

items.statement: Anti-dumping duties on Chinese products in India and Europe expected to benefit non-Chinese players like STL
items.quote: The application of anti-dumping duty on Chinese products in India, Europe is expected to balance out the optical connectivity product supply and help non Chinese players such as STL further standing up our global positioning.

items.statement: Completed capex cycle with operationalization of US facility; now set up to fulfill US-made optic fiber cable demand
items.quote: During the FY24 we also completed our capex cycle with the operationalization of our US facility and we are now fully set up to fulfill demands of US made optic fiber cable products.

items.statement: Reduced permanent employee costs significantly; contract labor costs reported under other expenses; some cost to return as optical interconnect capability builds
items.quote: So, with respect to the e mployee cost, if you see the manpower cost, it's all about the permanent employees. While the labor costs which is generally it's a contract labor, which is not part of the manpower cost, it's getting reported as the other expenses are part of the line

items.statement: No election impact seen in India or US; BEAD funding bipartisan and election-resilient
items.quote: No, we are not seeing any impact of the elections per se whether in India or globally.

items.statement: Realizations reasonably stable in recent quarters; no reduction seen in focus markets; pricing varies by geography
items.quote: I would at least comment that in the last couple of quarters the market has been fairly stable and at least from our focus markets, we don't see any reduction in realization.

items.statement: Focus on right cash profile projects in Services to reduce fund involvement; working capital optimization ongoing
items.quote: We have been very focused on taking on the right kind of projects with the right margins and most importantly right cash profile to reduce our fund involvement so that efforts continue.

items.statement: Market share at 8% global cable demand ex-China in FY24; expected to normalize as fresh demand picks up
items.quote: Basis CRU global consumption data during FY24 we had 8% market share and global cable demand excluding China.

items.statement: Revenue mix diversifying towards North America and Europe as optical demand picks up globally
items.quote: On the back of our global businesses our revenue mix was well diversified during last quarter and we expect this to further improve towards North America and Europe as the demand for the optical products pick up in the global markets.

items.statement: UK services business nearly at breakeven with good order flow
items.quote: And one more thing to add is that we also had in line with what we had promised, we have been able to get our UK services nearly to breakeven so I think that is also something that's positive and we see good order flow up there.

items.statement: Demerger of services business: first NCLT hearing held April 2024; directed to convene shareholder/creditor meetings for scheme approval
items.quote: During the quarter, the first NCLT hearing was conducted in April 2024 NCLT has directed us to convene the meeting of the shareholders secured and unsecured creditors to approve the scheme of demerger and we are working on next steps in the approval process.

items.statement: Management expects ~10% volume growth in coming years and targets value-added product mix >50% of revenue within 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So considering everything put together, we should be in a range of volumes. We should consider 10% around volumes for the coming up, coming years.

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR145 cr in FY25 and INR174 cr in FY26; no new loans planned for FY25
items.quote: Secondly, as far as going forward we are definitely tearing down some of our debt which is a normal repayment of debt of about INR150 crores in the next year. So that will definitely come down.

items.statement: Routine capex INR15-20 cr/year; major expansion capex not yet decided; INR840 cr invested over last 1.5 years (30% to fabric/knitting, rest to spinning)
items.value: INR15-20 cr routine; major capex TBD
items.quote: Normal capex, which is of the routine nature, is about INR15 crores to INR20 crores t hat is happening. That happens every year due to various requirements for debottlenecking and other things. Apart from that, major capex plan has not yet been decided

items.statement: Yarn capacity ~91k tons vs rated 110k tons (max 105k tons); fabric/weaving can improve 7-8%; knitting utilization lower with scope to improve; overall ~10% volume headroom
items.quote: Our rated capacity is around 1,10,000 tons per annum. And we can produce, after giving all efficiencies and others, about 1,05,000 tons. So, we are looking for that kind of capacity utilization which is about 10% more from the present last year's capacity.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 14.52%; management indicates maintaining ~14.5% would be substantial improvement over FY24 average 13%; long-term target 16-20% if export demand and FTAs materialize
items.quote: Basically, we do not give any projections for the margins. But just an indication is that our last quarter margin was 14.5. So, if you are able to maintain that also it should be substantial improvement from the existing levels, yearly levels.

items.statement: Cotton prices stable at INR57-58k/candy (±INR3k) for 6-8 months; expected to remain stable this calendar year; yarn realization FY24 INR274/kg vs FY23 INR338/kg (-19%); fabric realization FY24 INR160/m vs FY23 INR182/m
items.quote: Cotton prices have remained in the range of INR 57,000, INR58,000 plus minus INR3,000 a candy for good last 6 months, 7 months, 8 months which is going to continue going forward as well as we look forward.

items.statement: Export demand improving at normal pace; China re-importing cotton yarn (+35-40% YoY in March); Indian exports improved last 6-8 months, expected stable next 6 months; full demand recovery may take 5-6 more months
items.quote: Demand is definitely improving and it is not a very fast pace. It is a normal pace. If you see the data of imports by various of these countries we are seeing that China has started to re-import large quantities.

items.statement: Export mix targeted at 55-60% of revenue (down from 73% in FY22); domestic and export realizations similar; exports include both yarn and fabric
items.quote: As a strateg y, we would rather keep ourselves limited up to 50 -- in the band of 55 % to 60% on the export side. And that's what we're doing

items.statement: Total debt INR1,339 cr (INR811 cr long-term, INR383 cr WC, INR145 cr current maturities); term debt 5.5% net of subsidies (new loans at full rate pending sanction); WC ~7.5%; debt/equity 1.15-1.16; target interest cost 2.5-3% of revenue
items.quote: As of March 24, the company's debt profile stood at INR1,339 crores comprising INR811 crores in long-term debt, INR383 crores working capital and INR145 crores as current maturities of term loan.

items.statement: Solar capacity increased from 12-13 MW to 23 MW (+10 MW); adding 7-8 MW more in current year; solar generation ~2.7 cr units/yr at lower cost vs grid INR7-7.5/unit; renewables 7-8% of power mix; INR95-100 cr invested in solar over 3 years
items.quote: We have added substantial solar capacity -- solar power capacity. Now our capacity is about 23 megawatts. If you see at the end of the last year this capacity was about 12, 13 megawatts. So we have added more than 10 megawatts of capacity.

items.statement: Value-added products ~38-40% of revenue (fabric 25-26% + value-added yarn 14-15%); target >50% in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So that all put together, it is about 38 % to 40%, where we do a reasonable value addition in comparison to normal commodity yarns. So this proportion slowly is going up. We expect that total, we should be doing it more than 50%.

items.statement: Government schemes (textile parks, PLI, export incentives) delayed due to elections; expected implementation post-elections to aid long-term growth; FTA with EU could benefit >20% of sales (UK only 3-4%)
items.quote: The measures were in active consideration, however held up due to elections. I hope implementation of these schemes post -elections will h elp long-term growth of Indian textile industry

items.statement: Board recommended dividend 25% (INR2.5/share), same as last year
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of 25% i.e. INR2.5 per share, i.e. same as last year.

items.statement: Captive consumption 20% of yarn production; depreciation run-rate INR36 cr/quarter (INR145 cr/yr) on current asset base
items.quote: Yeah, this INR36 crores every quarter will be charged. So the average -- the depreciation next year is expected to be on the current set of fixed assets is about INR145 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Red Sea crisis) increasing freight costs and transit times; margin recovery dependent on export demand pickup and FTA implementation
items.quote: Despite ongoing geopolitical challenges such as Russia-Ukraine conflict, Red Sea crisis, which has resulted in a higher freight cost and extended transit times, our country's cotton textile exports have demonstrated a healthy rebound.

items.quote: In terms of investments, I think our Capex in this business will be anything between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores of Capex, which we are looking to invest in this business.

items.quote: We are now working with a lot of marquee names global names, such as GE, Schneider, Toshiba, Tata Solar.

items.quote: Net debt is around 0 because the long-term borrowing we don't have, and we have the sufficient cash available.

items.quote: We are looking at least about INR 300 crores of revenue at least in both the businesses.

items.quote: The working capital is around 75 days. And I think that will remain in FY '25 also.

items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 0.30 per share, accompanied by the interim dividend of INR 0.30 per share, the combined dividend for financial year 2023-'24 amounts to INR 0.60 per share.

items.quote: But definitely, we are not partnering with them to -- partnering with anybody to bid for the tenders because, again, which we feel that these are very margin negative right now, the pricing is very margin negative.

items.quote: Further, I think there's a significant export potential because one of our significant partners and promoters in Jupiter Wagon, which is Tatravagonka, they are again, very keen to acquire wheel sets from India.

items.quote: Compared to freight per wheel set, both in terms of the pricing and definitely in terms of margins because these are more complicated wheel sets. So it's much better than on the freight business.

items.quote: So, Bharat ji, definitely not. As I mentioned that -- on the wheelset, I think all the Capex is done, that is going to be a significant contributor if we produce about 100,000 wheelsets, we are looking at revenues of upwards of INR 3,000 crore there.

items.statement: Management expects 15-20% topline growth in FY25 and PAT growth of around 1% above FY24 levels
items.quote: We are expecting topline growth of around and I am being very conservative, but we are expecting a topline growth of around 15% to 20% and trying to take up the net profit like it went up by about 1%-1.5% this year. So, maybe another one that is a conservative approach

items.quote: we plan to touch Rs. 500 crores of topline ASAP.

items.quote: And the sales center less, obviously it does improve our operating margin, no doubt. Definitely it helps.

items.quote: In FY24, the company sold 16.06 lakh cotton packets marking a year to year increase of 16.39%.

items.quote: Led by this product, the bajra segment grew by 25.98% in value and 15.51% in volume. The PNS segment has also recorded a good growth with the value and volumes both growing by 35% plus over the last year.

items.quote: Win-Chi-Win continues to perform and delivered a strong growth of 34% during the year.

items.quote: We are not very keen about putting in CAPEX. The godowns, the facilities are available at (Inaudible) 18.58 on rental basis. We go into long term lease with these people and if we don't like it we have a right to change.

items.statement: Focus on bajra, maize, vegetables, supplements with constant focus on paddy and cotton

items.quote: Our working capital position is also improving with stocks and debtors witnessing better controls. This year, we closed with positive operational cash flow of Rs. 74.70 crores.

items.quote: Regarding paddy, the proportion of research to hybrid is 75:25 volume wise, however, the value ratio is 59:41.

items.statement: Sales team headcount growing 8-10%, 80% of increase in Tier 2/smaller cities; Maharashtra+Karnataka share of sales fell 300 bps to 60% in Q4; expanding distribution nationally
