items.statement: Trade receivables up to INR170 crores from INR115 crores due to slow payouts from Telangana corporation market and higher CSD sales (longer credit days); inventory up 10% to INR198 crores due to good harvest
items.quote: See, there is largely on account of the slowdown in payouts being made by certain corporation markets, particularly Telangana. So, that's where some of the collections are outstanding and it's kind of impacting our receivables balance as on 31st of March.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.54x, net debt/EBITDA 1.1x; average borrowing up INR45 crores YoY as WIPs payout received March 31
items.quote: Our prudent financial management is evident in our debt matrix with our debt-to-equity ratio of 0.54 times and our net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1.1 times, reflecting a healthy balance sheet.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR4.5/share, full-year INR8.50/share (same as last year); conserving cash for organic and inorganic expansion
items.quote: Considering the expansion potential in our wine tourism and other inorganic expansion opportunities, company's board has recommended final dividend of INR4.5 per share subject to shareholders' approval. This takes the full-year dividend to INR8.50 per share, almost at the same level as last year.

items.statement: Maharashtra WIPs scheme revived for 8 years (4 retrospective to FY24, 4 prospective to FY28); prospective cap INR20 crores/unit vs no cap earlier; impacts Sula with 3 qualifying units
items.quote: The scheme was revived for eight years, four years which are retrospective until FY24 and another four years after FY24 until the end of FY28. There is a little bit of a difference in the scheme for the prospective four years as a cap has been imposed of INR20 crores per unit as against no cap earlier.

items.statement: Economy segment driven by high discounting, race to bottom; Sula not competing there; gained market share in new institutions via elevated S&D spend in Q3-mid Q4, now moderating S&D
items.quote: On the economy side, yes, we do expect volume growth there to be in the range of 5% to 6% or mid-single digits. Mid-single digits, you can say. And we do see this as a segment that is sort of driven by high discounting and becoming a race to the bottom.

items.statement: Onboarded VFX Supervisor Dan Levitan with 30+ years experience and 85 feature films, and COO Zameer with 20+ years at ILM, MPC, DNEG
items.quote: We are excited to update you about the onboarding of two exceptional individuals who will enhance our creative and operational capabilities. VFX Supervisor, Mr. Dan Levitan. With over 30 years of experience, this esteemed VFX Supervisor brings a rich depth of knowledge to BFS.

items.statement: Launched upskilling program to convert 2D VFX artists into 3D concept artists with 100% employee participation
items.quote: Basilic Fly Studio proactively upskills its workforce through upskilling technical programs. This initiative focuses on equipping employees coming from 2D digital VFX background with cutting-edge proficiencies and nurturing their talent to grow as 3D concept artists.

items.statement: Expanding project portfolio into emerging markets Italy, Spain, France and seeing surge from North America post writers' strike resolution
items.quote: BFS is expanding its project portfolio with new ventures originating from emerging markets such as Italy, Spain, and France, as well as experiencing assertive projects from the established markets of North America post the resolution of the writers' strike.

items.statement: Visible pipeline before September 2024 includes previs for video game cinematics (INR25M, 10 months), blockbuster sequel (INR180M, 10-11 months), exclusive vendor project (INR340M, 8-10 months), June 24 project (INR200M, ~500 shots), produc
items.quote: Previs for video game cinematics commencing in the coming days, this project spans for 10 months. Coming from AAA level gaming company showcasing our commitment to long-term engagement and creative excellence this shall bring an expected revenue of INR25 million. A blockbuster sequel anticipated to generate significant revenue of INR180 million over the next 10 to 11 months.

items.statement: Confirmed order book visibility for H1 FY25 is roughly INR75 crores
items.quote: Total order book would be roughly around INR75 crores. This is the visibility of the first half.

items.statement: Expecting ~30% revenue growth each for FY25 and FY26, with surge from August/September 2024 based on confirmed movie release dates
items.quote: Currently, we are estimating a growth of around 30% each for FY25 and also from September onwards, from August, September onwards we do see a surge in the market based upon the confirmed release dates of the movie project that has been announced by the major production networks.

items.statement: Aim to maintain FY24 EBITDA margin (~50%) and PAT margin (~35%) in FY25
items.quote: Yes EBITDA margin is something that would be able to maintain what the EBITDA margin that we have maintained for the previous year.

items.statement: Currently balancing margins: ~75% of India work at discounted rates, ~25% overseas work at better margins
items.quote: If you look into maybe 75% of what we work in India is discounted, but 25% what it comes out of these overseas locations would add to our margin. So that is where we've been balancing out this current situation.

items.statement: Direct studio work increased from 30% to 35%; targeting 45-50% by Q1 FY25 (March 2025)
items.quote: In terms of direct production initially were around 30% and we have increased to 35% now. And from the studios it's around 65%.

items.statement: Revenue split by service: ~30% Roto, 20-25% Paint, ~45% Compositing and other
items.quote: Approximately, I think percentage 30% for Roto and 20%, 25% for Paint and rest are just Composting and other was 45% each.

items.statement: Standalone receivables INR63 crores: INR15 crores >180 days (on declining trend, installment arrangements), INR48 crores <180 days; net working capital cycle ~60 days normalized
items.quote: Net working capital I would say 60 days.

items.statement: Other current assets include WIP ~INR19 crores and GST refund ~INR5+ crores
items.quote: Work in progress is roughly INR19 crores, GST refund is INR5 crores plus.

items.statement: Timing recruitment for June-July 2024 ahead of expected August/September surge; also pursuing strategic partnerships in incentive locations and technology-driven companies
items.quote: We are timing our recruitment closer to that, that is by June, July. It's what we would not be recruiting around August, but by June, July is what we've been planning and apart from that we're also working towards strategic partnerships as well.

items.statement: Appointed advisor for inorganic opportunities; in close discussions with potential partners, may materialize soon
items.quote: Yes, very much, Pranav and we've been working on that as well and we also have appointed an advisor who's working on that and we are very much closer in terms of discussing with few potential partnerships.

items.statement: Government VFX incentive: 30% of minimum project expenditure (capped at INR300M/project) for foreign content; 5% bonus for Indian content; applying for fresh projects
items.quote: So one thing is, it is more promising and encouraging where the government has announced 30% of minimum project expenditure based off for the VFX studios that would be working on foreign content, international content. And likewise, the minimum cap at, sorry, not minimum cap, maximum cap at INR300 million for each project.

items.statement: FICCI EY report: India VFX industry revenue ~INR5,400 crores last year, expected to grow to INR6,300 crores this year; animation & VFX CAGR 17.5% to INR185B by 2026
items.quote: Overall media industry, for example, based on FICCI EY report of the revenue for the VFX industry it looks like it's around INR5,400 crores for the overall for India VFX industry, around INR5,400 crores for the last year, but it's expected to grow to INR6,300 crores for this year.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated: Revenue INR105.79 crores (+33.75%), EBITDA INR52.18 crores (+34.35%), PBT INR50.61 crores (+34.95%), EPS INR17.85 (+9.38%)
items.quote: Consolidated financial. Total revenue surged by 33.75% amounting to INR105.79 driven by strong operational efficiency, EBITDA and profit before tax increased by 34.35% and 34.95% respectively reaching INR 52.18 crores and INR50.61 crores.

items.statement: FY24 standalone: Revenue INR103.19 crores (+46.34%), EBITDA INR51.68 crores (+40.69%), PBT INR50.18 crores (+41.64%), PAT INR26.44 crores, EPS INR17.69
items.quote: In our standalone financials for fiscal year 24 total revenue impressively increased by 46.34% to INR103.19 crores underpinned by strong operational efficiency, EBITDA rose by 40.69% to INR51.68 crores And profit before tax increased by 41.64% to INR50.18 crores.

items.statement: Wrong consolidated financials uploaded to NSE on April 30, 2024 due to clerical error (UK subsidiary numbers); correct financials were board-approved; informed NSE May 1; added internal controls
items.quote: On behalf of BFS, I wish to apologize to the investors for unforeseen inconvenience caused due to typographical errors present in the uploaded documents of consolidated financial statements as of 31st March 2024, which we submitted on National Stock Exchange on April 30, 2024.

items.statement: Workforce ~500 as of March 2024 (up from 400+ post-IPO); operating from Chennai, Pune, London, Vancouver
items.quote: As of March 2024, we employ around 500 individuals. A robust team dedicated to driving success following our IPO, we've experienced significant growth expanding our employee count.

items.statement: Global footprint with HQ in Chennai and offices in Canada, UK; executives based overseas to capture direct international work
items.quote: Established in 2016, Basilic Fly has emerged as a leading force in VFX innovation with our headquarters based in Chennai and a global footprint extending to Canada and the UK.

items.statement: India cost advantage: ~USD150/day vs USD500-600/day in UK/US for high-end work; targeting streaming platforms (Netflix, Amazon) cutting costs but demanding quality
items.quote: For example, if you take USD500 to USD600 per day there, and if you take USD150 per day here is much better margin. So that is something we will be working towards and getting those kinds of projects.

items.statement: Diversifying into gaming cinematics (previs), corporate films, real-time 3D content creation (Unreal), advertising VFX (5-10% of revenue)
items.quote: We've been working on these kinds of projects and working on a short and real-time projects for corporate films and likewise for gaming cinematics and likewise diversified into other markets as well.

items.statement: JLR expects EBIT margin around FY24 level (8.5%) for FY25, investment spend ~GBP 3.5bn, targets net debt zero by end FY25, Q1 cash flow broadly breakeven
items.quote: we expect EBIT margin for this year to be around the level of FY 2024. We do expect to have to spend a little bit more in terms of demand generation, and we will oﬀset that operationally with cost reduction. We expect investment spend to be around GBP 3.5 billion, and we are holding our target to be net debt zero by the end of this ﬁnancial year

items.statement: Tata Motors consolidated capex for next year broadly similar to FY24 at ~Rs 8,300 Cr, JLR capex ~GBP 3.5bn
items.quote: is well funded by the operating cash, and nothing abnormal there. And the investment spending, we ended the year at Rs. 8,300 Cr. There are some sure questions, I already see what is likely to be JLR's investment and what is ours - about GBP 3.5 billion in JLR and broadly similar lines for Tata Motors

items.statement: CV business achieved double-digit EBITDA for FY24, Q4 EBITDA ~12%, PBT ~Rs 6,000 Cr, $1bn EBITDA new high
items.quote: Overall numbers, it's been again a very strong year, there's a highest ever revenues, highest ever proﬁts as far as this business is concerned as well. And we ended at Rs. 78,800 Cr revenue with a double -digit EBITDA that we had co mmitted. And for the quarter the EBITDA came in stronger at about 12

items.statement: PV industry growth expected <5% in FY25 due to high base, channel inventory, elections, heatwave; secular growth 6-8%
items.quote: after triangulating the projections from multiple places, we clearly see that the industry will moderate and grow less than 5%, given that the pent -up demand has got exhausted, the channel inventory is high a nd in the ﬁrst quarter, we will face certain factors like that of elections, heat wave which might dampen the demand temporarily for quarter one

items.statement: JLR order book 133k units (excl. 33k Range Rover BEV waitlist), above normalized 110k; Europe/UK soft, NA/Overseas/China strong
items.quote: We did end the year with an order book of 133,000 units, that includes orders for SV vehicles that does not include the 33,000 people I mentioned to have signed up to the waiting list on Range Rover BEV. Pre-COVID, our order bank sort of averaged a normalized level, of around 110,000 units.

items.statement: JLR Range Rover/RR Sport production capacity ramped up; Solihull plant at record 201k Range Rover sales, Defender 115k record
items.quote: Range Rover is up 27%, that's driven by progressive improvements in both our production system and those of our suppliers, allowing us to move up capacity levels in our Solihull plant. That level of 201,000 units is a record sales for the Range Rover brand.

items.statement: PV Sanand EV facility ramp: Jan <1k, last month 6,500, targeting 10k soon, then 15-16k/month
items.quote: Sanand facility, we started in Jan, we did about less than 1,000 production in Jan, but we have progressively ramped up. And last month we crossed 6,000, to be speciﬁc, 6,500. And soon the production ramp-up is going to attain a level of 10,000. And going forward then, you know, further improvement up to 15,000 to 16,000 numbers

items.statement: JLR VME increased from 0.5% to 3% YoY, offset by material cost improvements (GBP 267m, half raw materials, half non-repeat of semi/supplier costs)
items.quote: price is now a negative in this walk, whereas historically for the last few quarters, it's been positive. That is due to slow increases in our VME rates from 0.5% a year ago to 3%, that 3% is still very light in comparison to many others in the market. Those increases in VME have however been more than oﬀset by material cost improvements versus a year ago

items.statement: CV commodities: ferrous metals softened, aluminum up, other non-ferrous stable; Q1 seeing increases in castings, forgings, aluminum, tires, forex; will pass through price increases
items.quote: In Q1 itself, we are seeing some increase in casting , forgings, aluminum, tires. Fore x will also have some impact. So, yes, Balaji, I think we will have some impact due to commodities, which we will pass through appropriate price increases at the right time

items.statement: PV battery costs still declining, secured best costs from supplier; further reduction expected but nearing floor; better realizations from this quarter
items.quote: So far, you know, we have been seeing the battery prices still coming down. We have secured the best possible battery costs from our supplier. Going forward, I think this is going to still go down to some extent, but I think this would be more or less reaching the level of what we can think as the best possible reduction of sale prices.

items.statement: PV multi-powertrain mix: petrol 58%, diesel 13%, EV 13%, CNG 16%; CAFE headroom substantial, prepared for CAFE III/IV
items.quote: With petrol at 58%, diesel at 13%, 13% EVs, and 16% CNGs, so we are playing all the powertrains and it's coming through very nicely. And that has ensured those green emissions friendly vehicles also mean that our CAFE headroom that we have is substantial at this point in time.

items.statement: Tata Motors Finance GNPA 5.6%, NNPA 3.2%, collection efficiency improving, early delinquency healthy, capital adequacy and liquidity adequate
items.quote: Collection eﬃciency continues to improve and that's why GNPA has now reduced to 5.6% and NNPA is 3.2%. So from that perspective, the portfolio is back under control

items.statement: Consolidated automotive debt Rs 16,000 Cr (Rs 7,300 Cr external, Rs 8,700 Cr finance leases); India business Rs 1,000 Cr net cash; JLR net debt GBP 732m (from GBP 3bn), repaid >GBP 1.8bn from operating cash flow
items.quote: automotive debt is now Rs. 16,000 Cr, of it Rs. 7,300 Cr is the external debt a nd Rs. 8,700 Cr is ﬁnancial leases. And split diﬀerently, the India business is now Rs. 1,000 Cr positive cash. JLR and Singapore are the two places where we have the debt to be knocked out, and the plan is to ensure this year we take that out completely

items.statement: JLR no immediate plans to access bond markets; will fund in due course
items.quote: At the moment there are no plans to access the bond markets, but in due course, we will of course do funding again, but no direct, no immediate plans.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend: Rs 3 ordinary + Rs 3 special = Rs 6/share; DVR Rs 3.1 + Rs 3.1 = Rs 6.2/share; total payout ~Rs 2,300 Cr (highest ever)
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3 for the ordinary shareholders, Rs. 3.1 for the DVR shareholders, which is the normal dividend and there is also a special dividend in lieu of the successful TTL IPO of Rs. 3 per share for Ordinary and Rs. 3.1 for the DVR holders . So together is about Rs. 6 and Rs. 6.2 resulting in a cash ﬂow of almost Rs. 2,300 Cr, the highest ever dividend that Tata

items.statement: PV PLI: certificate for Tiago EV received, SOP for disbursement being finalized, expect disbursement H2 FY25; applying for 2 more products in Q1, 1 in Q2
items.quote: PLI, so far we have got the cer tiﬁcate for Tiago EV. And right now the SOP for disbursement is being ﬁnalized. And we are hoping that in the second half of this ﬁnancial year, we may start getting the disbursement. We are also going to apply for additi onal two products in Q1 and for the additional one product in Q2 also

items.statement: Management expects FY25 volume growth of around 10% and EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: we have always been optimistic, and we always feel that 10% to 15% growth rate has been our norm. There have been a few years like last year where we have dropped below that. But otherwise, 10% is, I think, what we expect.

items.statement: FY24 capex was INR120 crores; FY25 capex planned at INR60-80 crores plus potential INR75-200 crores for new products over 2 years
items.quote: this year, our total capital expenditure is about INR120 crores. In that INR120 crores is also some expenditure for routine maintenance capex and the solar plant to supply electricity to our Dahej facility.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant (100 TPD, INR375 cr capitalized) commissioned and running well; utilization ~60% in H2 FY24
items.quote: the ethylamines plant, which we had been constructing over the last 2, 2.5 years has been commissioned and has been running very well much better than our expectations. And it is now probably the largest ethylamine plant in the world.

items.statement: Acetonitrile plant utilization ~55-60% in H2 FY24 due to Chinese competition
items.quote: The second half was not as good as the first half because the Chinese pressure continued in terms of price and aggressive selling in the Indian market. So -- we were at about half our capacity 55%, a little better than half.

items.statement: Pharma demand stable and growing; agrochemical destocking ending but Chinese competition increasing
items.quote: the market demand for pharma is quite stable now and growing. And we have managed to increase our sales in terms of tonnage.

items.statement: Ethylamine margins improved in last 3-4 months due to lower ethanol prices and stable selling prices; methylamine margins stable; MIPA margins pressured after anti-dumping duty expiry
items.quote: But as far as pricing is concerned, yes, it has improved on both the selling side as well as the raw material side, the ethyl alcohol has softened. compared to what it was, say, 6 months, | year ago.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22%; FY24 average selling price dropped ~20%, top line down ~14%
items.quote: I would say that 20% EBITDA margin is what we hope to achieve between 20% and 22%.

items.statement: FY24 volume growth under 10% (just short of 1 lakh tons); H2 weaker due to acetonitrile and MIPA pressure
items.quote: Yes, total volume growth for the whole year is under 10%. Second half was much -- I mean, it was disappointing largely under pressure from Acetonitrile, as I said earlier, to Nilesh.

items.statement: Acetonitrile prices stabilized around INR145-160/kg; ethylamine prices INR150-160/kg; raw materials: ammonia INR50-52/kg, acetic acid <INR40/kg, methanol <INR30/kg
items.quote: About INR150 or so. For the larger people INR145, for the smaller people INR160 that kind.

items.statement: Chinese competition across products (acetonitrile, MIPA, methylamine); Balaji adding 40k ton methylamine plant; Chinese methylamine capacity announcement noted
items.quote: it's not just acetonitrile, it's across the board, they have too much capacity in most of their chemical industry. And in fact, we recently saw an announcement by one of their companies for a huge methylamines plant.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty investigation on acetonitrile initiated March 2024; interim relief possible Q4 FY25; injury estimated 15-20%
items.quote: we have filed antidumping in December and in March '24, the investigation has been initiated, hearings are going on right now and we are planning for filing interim relief also in that. But it will take time. Maybe in Q4 of '24-'25, we expect that to come, if it is favorable on our side. Injury is in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY24 sales mix: ~40-50% amines, ~25% derivatives, ~20-25% specialty (mainly acetonitrile)
items.quote: It's still, I think, in the region of 40% to 50% is the main Amines about 25% is derivatives and about 20% to 25% is specialty, which is the main one being Acetonitrile.

items.statement: Other expenses up INR15 crores QoQ due to CSR provision, Patalganga asset impairment, higher power/fuel from increased production
items.quote: So mainly CSR expenses, which we could not spend, we had to make provision for that, and there was one asset at Patalganga, which was not being used, so we had to impair that. and since there is increase in production, the power and fuel expenses have increased.

items.statement: Solar capacity 8.5 MW total (3.5 MW added in Jan FY24); saves INR3-4 crores/year vs grid; power cost lower in FY24 due to lower coal prices
items.quote: Yes, about -- my estimate would be these 8 megawatts would be giving you about INR3 crores to INR4 crores of savings in view of if you were buying from the grid, right?

items.statement: Old ethylamine plant at Patalganga (15k tons) to be converted to methylamine over ~2 years; Dahej methylamine plant at 80-85% utilization (45k tons/yr)
items.quote: No, we are having plans to convert it into methylamines. The engineering has just started. It would take a little time to convert it but_we are preparing for 2 years down the line when the demand has grown to a level where we will need it.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market size 30-35k tons; 50-55% imported in FY24
items.quote: Market size would be in the range of 30,000 to 35,000 tons. And I would say about 50% of that estimated is imported last year. 50% to 55% was imported.

items.statement: Targets FY26 revenue of about 4,000 crores with steady EBITDA margin around 12.5%
items.quote: we aim to achieve a top line of about 4,000 crores while maintaining a steady EBITDA margins at around Sangam (India) Limited 13 th May 2024 12.5% for FY26

items.statement: Denim and Phase 1 synthetic fabric capex completed, yielding benefits from Q1 FY25; Phase 2 synthetic fabric underway; Phase 3 yarn on track for Q1 FY26 completion
items.quote: Denim and Phase 1 of synthetic fabric CAPEX has been successfully completed within the expected timeline and will be yielding benefits from Q1 Financial year 25 and this quarter onwards. Phase 2 of synthetic fabric is currently under way and is progressing as per schedule. Phase 3 of yarn segment is also scheduled and it is on track for completion by Q1 FY26

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved across all segments in Q4 FY24; running at broadly full utilization currently
items.quote: During this quarter, there has been an improvement in capacity utilization under all the segments of the company

items.statement: Exported approximately 160 lakh meters of denim fabric in FY20-23; won Texprocil award for highest denim exports
items.quote: During the year, we exported approximately 160 lakhs meter denim fabric across the world

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 1.7% QoQ to 10%; targets 12.5% by FY26 driven by value-added mix shift
items.quote: EBITDA margin is at 10%, which is expanded about 1.7% quarter on quarter again

items.statement: Value-added (fabric & garment) share at 53% of revenue in FY24; targets ~60% in 2 years, yarn share to fall from 47% to ~40%
items.quote: Currently, 53% of our product mix comprises of value-added products, and going forward, we are committed to increase this further

items.statement: Slight uptake in demand as sector headwinds reduce; improved price relations across all product segments
items.quote: As the sector headwinds have reduced a little, we are witnessing a slight uptake in demand, reflected in improved price relations across all our product segments

items.statement: Exports 33-40% of revenue across 60+ countries; key markets: Bangladesh, South America, Europe, Turkey, Africa, Egypt, Middle East; expects export share to remain in similar range
items.quote: currently about one third of the business in the company comes from the export market and two third comes from the domestic market

items.statement: Cotton prices at Rs 57-58k per candy, 2% cheaper than international; grid power blended cost Rs 7.25/unit; 10% energy from renewables
items.quote: And it is around 57 to 58,000 rupees is the prices per candy. So it is in the reasonable market

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity comfortable; at 85-90% of peak debt levels; undrawn long-term debt Rs 150-200 cr; peak interest cost in Q4 FY24, expected to decline
items.quote: We can safely say that we are at least about 85-90% at the peak debt levels

items.statement: Working capital borrowing cost blended at around 8%
items.quote: Working capital is between around 8%. Blended

items.statement: Last fundraise Rs 100 cr (60% promoter, 40% non-promoter); no further equity infusion foreseen; well capitalized
items.quote: Last fundraising was about 100 crores where 60% was funded by the promoter and 40% was from a non-promoter entity

items.statement: Maintained 20% dividend for continuity; will work on codified dividend policy
items.quote: So we just tried to maintain continuity. Last year, it could have been a higher number, but since we could see that, you know, margins are going to be under pressure in the future. So we tried to be conservative last year and this year we try to maintain some continuity there

items.statement: FTA talks with UK and Australia advanced; expected to progress after new government forms in a couple of months
items.quote: the very advanced talk with the UK and Australia, but it will take some time with the new government will come into power, right? Probably it will happen in a couple of months time

items.statement: Dyes and chemicals cost (classified in other expenses) rises with fabric turnover increase
items.quote: For example dyes and chemicals used in processing. When our fabric turnover increases the raw material on the processing division is dyes and chemicals but that is classified in other expenses

items.statement: Garment segment ~3% of total revenue; substantial growth expected in FY25 as garment capex completed
items.quote: Currently, Garment consists of about 3% of the total business

items.statement: Interest rates at global peak; any further rate hikes could increase finance cost beyond current peak
items.quote: we are at the peak of the interest rates across the globe. So now that is beyond our control. So whatever easing will happen there, that can contribute

items.statement: 30-40 major clients across segments; details in investor presentation
items.quote: there are about 30-40 big clients that we put on the presentation

items.statement: Competitive advantage from diversified portfolio across cotton/synthetic yarn, denim, synthetic fabric, garment; ability to supply multiple products to brands
items.quote: we are better placed in terms of the varied product ranges and when we are entering some markets where you know we're dealing with brands so we are able to supply various products versus just doing one product there

items.statement: ESOP/Sweat equity issued 2 years ago amortized over 5 years; exceptional item relates to this non-cash cost
items.quote: this is with regards to the the ESOPs and SWEAT equities that that were issued to various company, company officials, I think 2 years back. So that is that that is going to be amortised over 5 years

items.statement: Guided minimum 10% standalone volume growth for FY25 without considering expansions
items.quote: Minimum 10%, I'm telling you. I'm telling you very conservatively, but minimum 10% without considering any expansions.

items.statement: Guided EBITDA margin range of 21% to 24% for FY25
items.quote: It should be between 21% to 24%. Minimum 21%, maximum 24% should be there.

items.statement: Methylamine plant commissioning expected around end of December 2024
items.quote: The project is likely to be commissioned around the end of December 2024.

items.statement: Electronic grade DMC plant set to commission in FY25 with 15,000 MT per annum capacity
items.quote: Electronic grade DMC plant set to commission in FY '24 -'25 holds promising prospectus in India EV batter y market due to its exclusive production status and a robust installed capacity of 15,000 MT per annum

items.statement: Dimethyl ether manufacturing project at Unit IV set to launch by March 2025 with 100,000 tons capacity
items.quote: At Unit IV, we are currently working on a DME manufacturing project set to be launched by March 2025 along with being a substitute of LP G, DME is used in Aerosols plus Bureau of Indian Standards is eyeing a 20% DME blend with LPG recognizing its benefits

items.statement: Proposed N-Methyl Morpholine 3,000 tons per annum and NBPT 2,500 tons per annum projects
items.value: 3,000 tons per annum; and N-(n-butyl) Thiopho sphoric Triamide, which is called NBPT, 2,500 tons per annum
items.quote: The Company has proposed to set up the following projects. Number one, N-Methyl Morpholine Company, 3,000 tons per annum; and N-(n-butyl) Thiopho sphoric Triamide, which is called NBPT, 2,500 tons per annum.

items.statement: Isopropylamine to be manufactured in existing Ethylamine plant at Unit I by modification
items.quote: Isopropylamine, the Company has proposed to manufacture Isopropylamine, Mono and Di, in the existing plant of Ethylamine at Unit I by modifying the existing Ethylamine plant, which is not in operations as we have set up a new and high output plant for manufacturing of Ethylamines at Unit IV.

items.quote: The ETR across the globe will be 23%, for India it's 25% so we'll optimize it to 23% at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Winning core banking deals in Europe through architectural rigor (OTP, VakifBank); US embedded finance traction with 3-4 deals; fintechs struggling on enterprise-grade security
items.quote: We closed over eight core banking transformation deals in the previous year. And as I look at the pipeline, it c ontinues to be very good. It's a deep pipeline. We are in multiple stages, and what we are also seeing from a core banking perspective, we talked about this as eMACH.ai. We are now getting called by large tier -one players, regional players, etc

items.statement: Platform revenue target $50-75M in 3 years (currently ~$5-6M/qtr ex-GeM)
items.quote: This business has to be a 50 to 75 -million-dollar business in platfor m revenue and should be there comfortably. So we are targeting 100 million, but 50 to 75 million dollars should be the platform revenue in 3 years' time.

items.statement: 300 global leaders from 31 countries attended eMACH.ai Summit with AI and iTurmeric boot camps
items.quote: 300 l eaders from 31 countries, 2 Boot Camps, 1 purpose it's the largest congregation. For nine days, the leadership team started beginning the year with a new agenda of eMACH.ai to become the disruptive platform for the world

items.statement: Customer canvas strategy: Magnificent 7, Expand 18, Focus 36 accounts; 11 countries for deepened coverage
items.quote: Today, we have a rich set of top 50 accounts on which we have focused our attention to gr owing those accounts. They are the leaders in their geography. Magnificent 7, Expand 18, and Focus 36 are the three agenda points we are driving on Customer Canvas

items.statement: RBI actions on Kotak/Paytm driving legacy modernization demand; security architecture becoming key differentiator
items.quote: I would say another 12 to 18 months to understand that legacy core and legacy lending platforms are fundamentally built on the technology by hollowing the code, by doing patchworks. It's not going to solve the problem; you need to go to the first principle thinking.

items.statement: North America momentum: 8 deal wins in Q4 (6 AI); Europe core banking traction; APAC/ANZ wins; Middle East DTB leadership
items.quote: Eight deal wins out of which six deal wins are in AI business is a credible performance of North America. It has both areas, so one is on the CBX deal around digital Contextual Ba nking eXperience deals and AI deals.

items.statement: GeM cost reduced from Rs 67 Cr (Q3) to Rs 27 Cr (Q4); Rs 40 Cr differential due to third-party costs ending mid-Dec and provisions
items.quote: In Q3, we also had GeM in the sense the GeM got ended only by mid of December so until such time we had GeM cost we had third party cost related to GeM and all so in Q4 we conservatively made some provisions for some of the cost.

items.statement: 1,000 R&D personnel invested annually (~$200M equivalent cost) building enterprise-grade platform with 42 cloud mgmt and 40+ security elements
items.quote: We are investing close to a thousand people in R&D each year. A thousand people in R&D, I am mentioning to some US person, is at $100K per R&D cost, it's a $200 Million per year cost compared to any other vendor in America or Europe.

items.statement: SI partnership channel rotating in Intellect's favor; CEOs of SIs now approaching Intellect; indirect distribution to add significantly in 12-18 months
items.quote: I'm meeting the CEOs of all the SIs. So now they're coming to us, which was the reverse way. So that wheel has rotated. How it will translate into numbers? Sinc e this investor conference is not a business plan conference, we are cautious about it

items.statement: Sustainability: Zero-discharge campus for 1 year; 15 initiatives under GRI/BRSR frameworks; 5,000 employees took sustainability pledge
items.quote: Our campus has been a zero -discharge campus for the last one year. No single waste item is going out of the campus as a waste. We recycle or reuse all our water, food, and other waste. And there are almost 15 initiatives in sustainability that are happening.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY25 and FY26, with I&C expected to grow at low double-digits
items.quote: For this 2024-25 and next financial year, we expect growth to be slightly better than 5.4% -- 5.5%, maybe in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at INR 9-11 per SCM for the long term
items.quote: So even if we expect some cost increase and gas costs going up, we are still comfortable with the range of 9% to 11% in the long-term, I mean.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 900-1,000 crore for FY25 standalone, plus INR 150-200 crore for UEPL, targeting group capex of INR 1,000 crore+
items.quote: As far as our CapEx guidance is concerned, we target and have an internal budget approval in the range of INR900 crores to 1,000 crores, at least in the next year.

items.statement: CBG plant capex estimated at INR 550-600 crore for two phases of 500 TPD each
items.quote: It will be around INR550 crores to INR600 crores for -- there will be 2 phases, one, 500 tons per day of waste handling in Phase 1 and 500 tons per day of waste handling in phase 2.

items.statement: Targeting 50+ new CNG stations in FY25 and 40-50 in FY26, up from 36 in FY24
items.quote: But this year, FY 2025, we expect to do much better in terms of CNG stations. Maybe more than 50 stations we are targeting to be completing this year and maybe around 40 to 50, around that number will be for FY 2026.

items.statement: 1 lakh SCMD of new I&C contracts signed under 10% FO discount scheme, another 1 lakh SCMD to be connected in coming year
items.quote: Now that guaranteed 10% discount enabled us to sign up more than 1 lakh SCMD worth of new contracts, and many of those have now come on stream.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA up 56% to INR 1,843 crore, PAT up 63% to INR 1,289 crore; Q4 PAT INR 265 crore vs Q3 INR 317 crore
items.quote: EBITDA for the financial year is INR 1,843 crores compared to previous financial year of EBITDA of INR 1,184 crores, which is an increase of 56%.

items.statement: Q4 opex increased to INR 192 crore from INR 168 crore due to INR 25 crore marketing scheme spend, deemed one-time
items.quote: Mainly, there is an increase on account of the marketing scheme we introduced for promotion of CNG vehicles. So almost more than INR25 crores has been spent during the quarter on account of these marketing schemes.

items.statement: Priority gas allocation at ~74% of sales; weighted average gas cost ~$7.25-7.3/MMBtu with HPHT blending
items.quote: In this quarter, on an average, we have been able to get around 74% APM compared to our sales in the priority sector. But with the availability of HPHT, I think still the weighted average has remained well under control, in the range of around, l et's say, $7.25 or $7.3 per

items.statement: Term contracts: 0.75 mmscmd Henry Hub (60% take-or-pay), 0.1 mmscmd Brent-linked, 0.49-0.5 mmscmd HPHT
items.quote: So I just mentioned 0.75 is Henry Hub, around 0.1 is our Brent link, okay. And roughly 0.49 or 0.5 is HPHT term contracts.

items.statement: CNG vehicle additions in Q4: ~20,000 total (13,000 private cars, 5,400 autos, 1,400 small commercial); MSRTC added 300 CNG buses, expects 100 more in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: The CNG vehicle addition in Q4 was slightly more than 20,000 numbers, out of which about 13,000 were private cars. About 5,400 were autorickshaws, and about 1,400 were small commercial vehicles.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle CNG adoption accelerating: 67 trucks added in Q3, 97 in Q4; scheme continues for commercial segment but paused for passenger cars
items.quote: Just to give you an example of trucks, etc., I mean, we were doing a negligible amount of additional trucks every quarter, but then Q3, we managed to do 67; Q4, 97. So traction is coming.

items.statement: FY24 sales mix: CNG 2.549 mmscmd (70.6%), Domestic PNG 0.52 mmscmd (14.4%), I&C 0.499 mmscmd (13.8%); I&C grew 12.3% YoY
items.quote: Average sales volume for the year ended 31st March '24 of 3.609 consists of CNG volume of 2.549, domestic volume of 0.52 and industrial and commercial volume of 0.499 mmscmd.

items.statement: I&C customer base: 4,769 total (4,300 commercial, 460 industrial); added 108 in Q4
items.quote: Roughly, slightly more than 4,000 would be commercial. Industrial should be about 300 -400.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Unison Enviro (UEPL) in Feb 2024; UEPL Q4 volume 0.14 mmscmd, EBITDA ~INR 60 crore/yr; targeting 1.2 mmscmd terminal volume in 7-8 years
items.quote: We have completed acquisition of 100% stake in Unison Enviro Private Limited and is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mahanagar Gas.

items.statement: Formed 51:49 JV Mahanagar LNG with Baidyanath LNG for LNG corridor; first station expected in 1 month, 4 more in FY25
items.quote: We have started the JV company, Mahanagar LNG Private Limited, with 51% equity holding, for supplying LNG to vehicles and a step towards developing the supply-side LNG corridor ecosystem.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 18/share proposed, total FY24 dividend INR 30/share (300% of face value), up 40% from INR 26 in FY23
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board of Directors has proposed a final dividend of INR18 per equity share for the financial year '23-'24. Thus, total dividend for the year, including interim dividend already paid is INR30 per share.

items.statement: Surplus cash ~INR 1,400-1,500 crore after INR 560 crore UEPL acquisition, INR 50 crore 3EV investment, JV equity infusion; open to further acquisitions/diversification
items.quote: If you look at this year full year, our surplus would have been in the range of INR2,000 crores plus. But today, my surplus is in the range of INR1,400 crores, INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Repaid UEPL borrowings via INR 200 crore unsecured loan from MGL; will fund UEPL capex for 2-3 years (INR 150-200 crore) until cash flow positive
items.quote: Going forward also, in the case of UEPL, currently also what we have done is we have repaid their borrowing by giving unsecured loan from MGL to the extent of INR200 crores.

items.statement: OMC trade margins: INR 5.41/kg (metro), 4.68 (Thane/class A), 4.38 (class B), 3.70 (class C/rural); interim settlements pending but provided for
items.quote: Yes, it is 5.41 for metro, that is Mumbai main. Then, 4.68 for Thane and otherwise. And below that, it is 4.38 or something, and then, 3.7 for rural and small areas.

items.statement: UEPL consolidation includes provisional intangible assets (INR 520 crore) mainly for license authorization; final valuation within 1 year; non-cash amortization impacts consolidated PAT
items.quote: So major intangible asset in case of a CGD entity is basically valuation of the authorization, okay. Apart from that, it is a normal case with any other business which we acquire.

items.statement: FY24 volume 3.609 mmscmd (+5.45% YoY); Q4 volume 3.779 mmscmd; CNG 2.666, Domestic 0.563, I&C 0.55 mmscmd in Q4
items.quote: We have achieved highest volume of sales, which is 3.609 mmscmd.

items.statement: Pipeline network: 6,968 km total (226 km added in Q4); Raigad GA: 416 km pipeline, 80,041 domestic connections, 47 CNG stations
items.quote: We have also laid 226.04 kilometers of steel and PE pipeline during this quarter, thereby taking the aggregated pipeline length to 6,968 kilometers.

items.statement: CNG stations: 347 total (28 added in Q4, 36 in FY24, 45 upgraded); highest ever in company history
items.quote: We have commissioned 36 new CNG stations and upgraded 45 existing CNG stations, which is the highest number achieved in the history of the company.

items.statement: Domestic PNG connections: 3,20,125 added in FY24 (highest in country by any CGD); total ~2.49 million households connected across 3 GAs
items.quote: We have provided 3,20,125 domestic PNG connections. And along with our subsidiary, Unison Enviro, we have completed 3,30,000, which is highest in the country by any CGD entity.

items.statement: Equity investment in 3EV Industries (3-wheeler EV manufacturing) and MoU with MCGM for CBG plant in Mumbai
items.quote: We have also made equity investments in 3EV Industries Private Limited, a start-up in the business of manufacturing 3-wheeler cargo and passenger electric vehicles.

items.statement: Management expects 10-11 hubs over next 2 years, 4-5 in Pune, rest in East and core geographies; 6 leases already signed, 2 more in pipeline.
items.quote: Over the next 2 years, we have a clear visibility of 10 hub centers and a few spokes, out of which, 4 to 5 would be in Pune and the rest in the east and our core geographies. We have already finalized locations and signed leases for 6 hubs and would be closing a few more in a couple of months to come.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR200-220 crores for next 2 years for new centres, with INR120 crores for Pune region; replacement capex of INR10-15 crores additional.
items.quote: So considering these 10 hubs and also adding new modalities in the existing centers because of the higher footfall, we expect the total capex to be in the range of around INR220 crores for the next 2 years, out of which INR120 crores, we expect to be for the Pune region.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margins expected to remain at 40%; new hub ramp-up may cause 1-2% dilution in near term, improving by FY28.
items.quote: Currently, if you look at the P&L, the EBITDA margins are at 40% level. If you see, okay, consistently, we have been achieving at 39% to 40% level. And as you know, as ma'am explained in the next couple of years, we are planning to add at least like 10 hubs, out of which, at least like 5 hubs, we'll be planning in the Pune region. So considering this expansion plan, as you know, it takes some time

items.statement: Q4 FY24 saw 28.3% YoY revenue growth (18.5% organic), driven by 17% volume and 15% footfall growth; wellness segment contributed 14% of revenue.
items.quote: I'm delighted to announce that this quarter, too, witnessed robust business performance with a remarkable year-on-year growth of 28.3%. Of which, an impressive 18.5% growth was achieved organically. This growth was primarily fueled by both footfall and debt volume. This quarter also marked a notable milestone with the wellness segment contributing 14% of the revenue.

items.statement: Mahabubnagar hub breakeven in 2 quarters; Kolkata hub expected breakeven in next 2 months; 5 Pune hubs expected breakeven within 1 year; Gulbarga hub expected breakeven in next 2 quarters.
items.quote: Completing 6 months of successful business operations, our hub center in Tier 2 geography, Mahabubnagar, has gained significant traction, achieving breakeven within 2 quarters. Once again, this emphasizes the need of a quality-oriented, integrated diagnostic chain and also validates our brand's ability to earn the trust and loyalty of our customers over time, empowering us to thrive in new markets

items.statement: Radiology 37%, pathology 63% of revenue; B2C 93%; PH Pune mix 60% pathology, 40% radiology vs Vijaya 65% pathology, 35% radiology.

The B2C revenue stood healthy again at 93%. Our radiology business stood at 37%, slightly higher than 36% in Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Wellness segment grew to 14% of revenue (13.5% core + 0.5% PH), driven by new corporate partnerships for employee health checks.
items.quote: This quarter also marked a notable milestone with the wellness segment contributing 14% of the revenue. This is partly attributed to the recent partnerships with a few large corporates for the employee health checks.

items.statement: No debt needed for next 2 years capex; INR184 crores surplus cash, generating INR170-190 crores free cash flow annually; debt only if inorganic acquisition pursued.
items.quote: So as I mentioned, currently, we're having a treasury of almost close to INR185 crore and currently, the cash back is going to be at a 28% - 29% level. So you will be generating almost close to INR170 crores to INR190 crores of free cash flows every year. And so I don't think we need to take any debt because the next 2 years, the capex requirement is almost close to like INR220 crores for the new

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR1 per equity share (100% dividend) for FY24, subject to AGM approval.
items.quote: I'm happy to inform you that the Board has recommended a dividend of INR1 per equity share of INR1 each. That is 100% dividend for this financial year FY '24, subject to approval of the shareholders in the coming AGM.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities if right fit, asset, valuation found; core interest in South and East, West (Pune) hands full, may consider Mumbai, not looking North.
items.quote: Inorganic is always a question mark. So I think what I can only say is that if we find suitable opportunities, we will look at them. And the balance sheet supports us, I think. As you know and as you mentioned, the capex that Raju just mentioned is probably taken care of even by internal accruals. So inorganic growth is always depending on whether we find the right fit, right asset, right valuatio

items.quote: We normally -- like we said, the founder's vision was trying to keep prices affordable and get growth through volume and new customers. Until and unless, we see a significant increase in price and input costs, we do not pass it on to the customers. And for probably the volume and the growth, even we haven't seen a significant increase being asked by some of the vendors, and it's mostly been in ver

items.quote: The revenue per test was INR462. And the revenue per footfall was INR1,589 during this current quarter. And we reached a key milestone of 1 million patient footfall in this current quarter.

items.quote: It's also finding the right talent with the right wavelength, right, Girish. It's skilled manpower. 70% of our ops run on skilled manpower. As we speak, we do different things. That's why we got from 4 to 6, 6 to 10. And

items.quote: currently, the cash back is going to be at a 28% - 29% level. So you will be generating almost close to INR170 crores to INR190 crores of free cash flows every year.

items.statement: Point-of-care testing not a threat; PCR is confirmatory gold standard, POC is screening only; Vijaya focused on high accuracy/sensitivity technologies.
items.quote: So basically, point-of-care is not new. It has been around for a long time. And you have to differentiate between POC and PCR. Where PCR is considered as confirmatory gold standard kind of a test, whereas point-of-care is usually done more from a screening point of view. So whether it is in COVID or in other indication, the market is very different for both. Somebody who gets a point-of-care will

items.statement: Aspiration to grow revenue 25% YoY, EBITDA 30% YoY and double store count over 3-4 years from Dec 2021
items.value: revenue 25% YoY, EBITDA 30% YoY, double store count
items.quote: In December '21, after we listed, we have guided that, our aspiration is to grow revenues by 25% year -on-year, grow EBITDA by 30% year-on-year and double the store count over a 3 to 4-year period.

items.statement: KFC long-term restaurant EBITDA margin target around 20%
items.quote: the overall long -term guidance on KFC margins we have called out that we would like to be in that 20% zone.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India expansion will be extremely cautious; markers for acceleration are SSSG recovery, ADS towards INR 50,000-55,000, restaurant EBITDA 8-10%
items.quote: The markers, I would say, 3 markers which we'll track internally. One is certainly looking at can the SSSG come back on the brand. That's the first. Reasonable ADS at a store. So moving towards INR50,000 ADS level marks again gives us some comfort, which helps us to manage costs more efficiently and deliver some sensible level of profitability. And the third would be the profit itself. I think mov

items.quote: For Sri Lanka, actually it's getting it back into those -- hitting those mid-teens level, I think, will be key. So being at 15%, I think -- in and around that 15% would be good place to again look at expanding aggressively.

items.statement: Demand across consumer categories remains constrained; private final consumption expenditure worst in 2 decades over last 6 quarters
items.quote: And really, the story as we indicated even in February was that demand across all consumer product categories remains constrained. And now we've got the private final consumption expenditure metrics released by the government over the last 6 quarters. It's been the worst it has been over the last 2 decades.

items.statement: KFC Q1 FY25 trends: April impacted by Chhota Navratri; May significantly better than Jan-Mar but in line with YoY improvement; no further improvement seen
items.quote: May has -- May is significantly better than either Jan, Feb, March quarter. But I mean, it is more or less in line with the improvement that we see on a year -on-year basis. Sequentially, this quarter -- so sequentially, this quarter is a better quarter if I remove Navratri, and we are seeing trends along those lines. We are not seeing even further -- or we are not seeing further improvement in --

items.statement: Pizza Hut seeing improvement vs last year but brand still fragile; need more quarters to confirm turnaround
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, we are seeing improvement compared to what we saw last year. But because the brand is -- has undergone a fragile few quarters, I'm still wanting to see how it pans out. And perhaps before the next -- or during the next quarterly results, we s hould give you concrete evidence that indeed we are starting to turn the corner on the brand

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin 13.6% in Q4 FY24, down 260 bps YoY; adjusted EBITDA margin 8.6%, down 3% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA declined 5% year -on-year and margin was 13.6%, down 260 basis points. Consolidated EBITDA at INR 110 crores, 17.5%, grew Y -on-Y by 7%. Adjusted EBITDA, that is pre-Ind AS 116, at INR54 crores in the quarter, 8.6%, declined by 3% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA -2.7%; excluding additional marketing spend, brand broke even at restaurant EBITDA level
items.quote: And while gross margins improved year -on-year by 120 bps, the impact of negative SSSG and higher marketing spends meant that the restaurant EBITDA came at negative 2.7%. If we exclude the additional marketing spend done during the year -- during the quarter, the brand broke even at the restaurant EBITDA level.

items.statement: Sri Lanka Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA 12.3%, impacted by store operating cost inflation despite gross margin improvement of 90 bps QoQ
items.quote: And while gross margin saw also an improvement even in Lanka business by -- up by 90 basis points quarter-on-quarter, restaurant EBITDA came at 12.3%, impacted by, as Sanjay mentioned, the cost inflation which we experienced on the operating expense side of the store.

items.statement: Pizza Hut added 33 stores in FY24; Q4 FY24 net-zero additions; expansion to remain extremely cautious
items.quote: Last -- with the year gone by, we added 33 restaurants for Pizza Hut. Yes, for the quarter, 0 additions. And for the previous quarter, it was 8. As we called out, the expansion will be c autious. We are not saying we are going to be 0 or pausing completely. It will be extremely cautious, suffice to say

items.statement: Sri Lanka store additions to remain single-digit in FY25 until margins recover to mid-teens
items.quote: You could see it as single digit in terms of a store count addition for the financial year.

items.statement: FY24 capex ~INR 385 crores; KFC capex ~INR 2 cr/store (1,500-1,600 sq ft); Pizza Hut capex ~INR 1.42-1.45 cr/store
items.quote: As I called out previously, if you look at the CapEx per store per format, so KFC CapEx is generally in the ra nge of INR 2 crores per store for around 1,500 to 1,600 square feet. Pizza Hut, we are seeing it in the range of INR 1.42 crores to 1.45 crores per store on Pizza Hut.

items.statement: Gross margins improved 150 bps YoY for KFC and 120 bps for Pizza Hut in Q4 FY24; expect gross margins to range +/- 2 bps sequentially going forward; no material price increases expected
items.quote: So whatever benefit had to come in into the P&L in terms of gross margin improvement, I think that's locked largely starting Q3 of last year. And if you see sequential gross margin, we had called out that it will be ranged from plus/minus 2 basis points. I think going forward, we expect that the gross margins would be ranged about plus/minus 2 basis points. And we don't see any price increase -- m

items.statement: KFC launched 5 new burgers (American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian veg/non-veg) and relaunched Chizza LTO and paneer Zinger in Q4 FY24
items.quote: And this quarter, we've taken our burger game to the next level by launching 5 new burgers: American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian and Indian veg and Indian nonveg. We've re launched also, which you will discover only at the store, the Indian veg option, a paneer Zinger.

items.statement: New fried chicken entrants (Popeyes, Wow Chicken) create positive category noise; KFC's scale and sourcing economies protect margins; unlikely competitors can sustain price leadership
items.quote: So in that sense, competition is only good. Now the second part to that question is that however, at the scale that KFC operates, we undoubtedly have economies of scale also. So it is difficult for any competitor to come in and be a cost leader and, therefore, impair margins. So I don't think that should happen, point number two.

items.statement: KFC SSSG -3% in Q4 FY24; ADS INR 114,000 (impacted by ~25% new store additions which operate at 70-80% of brand average in year 1)
items.quote: SSSG came at minus 3%. Our ADS is at INR114,000. Just to clarify, the ADS is also impacted by new store additions, which we're, over the year almost at 25% restaurant additions. And as we called out, generally, the new stores take time to scale up. And their ADS are generally lower initially the first year compared to the brand average.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; consolidated PBT INR 80 lakhs (0.1%), adjusted PBT INR 8.3 cr (1.3%) in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Consolidated PBT of INR8 million or INR80 lakhs, or 0.1%. Adjusted PBT was INR8.3 crores or 1.3%.

items.statement: Demand environment soft; seasonal calendar shifts (Navratri, Adhik Maas, Shravan) make quarterly trends noisy; annual view preferred for KFC

As a result the trends, which are sequential trends or year -on-year trends, some quarters where it gives out a good picture, some quarters, they are not strictly comparable.

items.statement: Ranked top 3 franchisee by Yum! on customer metrics and operating standards for both KFC and Pizza Hut; #1 QSR in India on ESG (Dow Jones Sustainability Index), 95th percentile globally; best-ever employee engagement score at 88th percentil
items.quote: We are ranked among the top 3 franchisees by Yum! on -- in both KFC as well as Pizza Hut on our customer metrics and our operating standards. We also achieved -- this is an internal metric, but I'd like to share with you.

items.statement: Target loan book growth of 22-24% for FY25 and 22-25% CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: we are looking for a growth for FY '25, a growth of 22% to 24% on the advanced book si de. And going forward also, we want to look to increase our loan growth on a CAGR of 22% to 25% over the next three to five years

items.statement: Target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY25 with continuous improvement thereafter
items.quote: We target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY'25 and continuous ROTA expansion going forward.

items.statement: Opex ratio expected to remain around current FY24 level of 2.95% in FY25

items.statement: Plan to add 25+ branches in FY25 to cross 200 total branches

items.quote: a couple of thousands of crores now we are spending on the IT side on an ongoing basis. We need to again spend much higher in terms of making the system much more robust than what it is now.

items.statement: Plan to hire more IT staff; reviving Baroda Sun Technology subsidiary
items.quote: we are thinking of something completely different to augment our human resources on the IT side and both in terms of spend and the hiring, both would continue

items.statement: Nainital Bank divestment process ongoing; actively pursuing completion
items.quote: as far as Nainital Bank is concerned, the process is on. So as the process is on, I will not be in a position to make any speculation here. But let me tell you, we are actively pursuing on the process to complete, right?

items.statement: No equity capital raise planned short term; CRAR 16.31% sufficient; may replace maturing AT1/Tier II bonds
items.quote: As of today, I mean I don't think we require any capital other than maybe replacing my maturing AT-1, Tier II bonds.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guidance of INR 100 crores excluding Panoli plant contribution
items.quote: This year, I mean, ex -Panoli because we have not factored in operations of Panoli till it comes and we put our budget and production plan for Panoli, but ex-Panoli I could say that EBITDA would be about INR100 crores in this year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target of 18% to 20% without Panoli plant
items.quote: 25% to 30% was probably including Panoli this year we should do between 18% to 20% without considering Panoli.

items.statement: No additional debt planned for capex; internal cash flows sufficient for next year
items.quote: I don't think we intend to take any debt for capex. And we are not looking at very heavy capex in next one year.

items.statement: Panoli API plant environmental clearance expected by June; commercial production to commence in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Panoli we are expecting approval in the month of June and after trial production etc in another 2 months, 3 months and proper commercial production should be in Q3.

items.statement: R&D center at Panoli already established; full-scale activity to start after environmental clearance
items.quote: The R&D center has already been established and trials are already on over there. As soon as we get the EC, which we expect next month, the R&D activity will start full scale.

items.statement: API gross margins historically range 30-35%; Q4 FY24 dip due to sales exceeding production and March price pressure
items.quote: If I take an average, it should range about 35%. This particular quarter, the gross margins were lower due to two, three things. One was, it was a reverse case where sales were higher than the production.

items.statement: Expect average API margins of 32-37% as international approvals for new products come through in 6-8 months
items.quote: As [Sanjay 0:16:42] rightly said, we work in a table of between 32% to 37% margins. It may fluctuate in a quarter, but that's the average we are trying to work on.

items.statement: New API products Faropenem and Ertapenem launched; Ticagrelor, Rivaroxaban, Empagliflozin commercialized domestically; DMFs under submission for international markets
items.quote: However, new products like Faropenem and Ertapenem were successfully launched in the last quarter and this has added to the Penem business. General products like Ticagrelor , Rivaroxaban and Empagliflozin have now been commercialized and are marketed to various customers in India.

items.statement: R&D completed development of Edoxaban, Lacosamide, Macitentan; expect commercialization in current financial year
items.quote: Our R&D has been working actively and new products like Edoxaban, Lacosamide and Macitentan development has been over completed and we expect commercialization in the current financial year.

items.statement: Formulation development focused on integrating new API molecules like Rivaroxaban, Apixaban, Empagliflozin for regulated markets
items.quote: As a strategy, new formulation development is focused on integrating the new molecules which we are manufact uring and developing in our active pharmaceutical ingredient business. For example, products like Rivaroxaban , Apixaban, Empagliflozin are already developed even in the formulations.

items.statement: CEP applications for European market filed; Amlodipine and Lymecycline CEPs expected in current or next quarter
items.quote: We have also made various applications for CEPs for the European market and some CEPs like Amlodipine and Lymecycline are expected in the curren t or next quarter.

items.statement: CEP for linear cycling filed; approval expected by end of May or beginning of June
items.quote: we have filed a CEP for linear cycling and I mean the date which has been given by the authorities is in the month of May. So we are expecting by end of May or beginning of June, hopefully we should be getting this.

items.statement: Panoli plant environmental clearance delayed due to jurisdictional confusion between Gujarat and Central pollution authorities; hearing completed, clarification submitted
items.quote: Earlier, there was a confusion between Gujarat Board and Central Pollution Control authorities that who has the authority to allow us, give us permission. And initially as far as we had applied to Gujarat government and later on when they said, I mean now Central has said that they only will do it.

items.statement: US ethanol validation batches supplied to large MNC; commercial orders expected in 3-6 months after NDA approval
items.quote: They have already taken validation batches with our product. They have filed their NDA with the FDA there and we expect the regular commercial business to start in the next 3 months to 6 months.

items.statement: Nitroxylin commercial sales starting in Europe this quarter; US ethanol trial material sent
items.quote: Nitroxylin in Europe is now starting in this quarter and US ethanol trial material has gone and we expect that commercial orders will come in the next 3 months to 6 months.

items.statement: CDMO business currently negligible; expect increase after 1-2 years post regulatory approvals
items.quote: Currently there is no CDMO projects till the time we get our approval. But going forward after a year or two, you can expect an increase in CDMO business.

items.statement: Developing synthetic KSMs in-house to replace Chinese imports; cost lower than China but Chinese price dumping remains a risk
items.quote: The whole purpose of where we are developing the KSMs, we are developing those KSMs where our cost is lower than China. But as you rightly said, China has a habit of reducing prices wherever India develops better than them.

items.statement: Fermentation-based KSMs (penicillins, statins) remain Chinese-dominated; India competitive only in synthesis-based intermediates
items.quote: In fermentation based the Chinese will always be more competitive. Kopran Limited May 17, 2024 But wherever there's only purely synthesis based, I think that's where India is actually catching up

items.statement: March quarter margin dip partly due to domestic selling pressure as companies reduce inventory for balance sheet reasons
items.quote: March in India particularly, not in international market. But domestic market, there is always some selling for all companies to meet their targets or whatever. So there is a tendency of prices going down temporarily for the month of March.

items.statement: R&D headcount exceeds 100 across three centers (Mahad, Panoli, formulations); more hiring planned after Panoli execution
items.quote: Maybe more if you put both there are three centers now, Mahad, Panoli and our formulations. So it will be more than 100.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing shipment timing delays for Latin American business and some imports; no forex impact as rupee stable
items.quote: I think Red Sea has some impact in terms of shipment timings too [inaudible 3 8:50 and Latin American business and some of our imports].

items.statement: Chinese price dumping risk remains for synthetic KSMs; company retains option to buy from China when prices low
items.quote: China has a habit of reducing prices wherever India develops better than them. And I mean that scenario is going to remain. But developing these KSMs gives us security in case, I mean wherever China is dumping, we always have a choice to buy from China.

items.statement: Panoli plant revenue contribution not factored into FY25 guidance; visibility on EBITDA breakeven to be assessed after commercial production starts
items.quote: At the moment, we have not factored into Panoli working at all in whatever we are saying.

items.statement: Insurance broking margin expected at 3-4% sustainable range
items.quote: We are expecting, I think margin range of 3 to 4% sustainable.

items.statement: NBFC AUM growth momentum of ~35% expected to continue
items.quote: So, we expect the momentum to continue in the coming years.

items.statement: NBFC leverage capacity up to 3-3.5x equity, targeting 2000+ crore AUM
items.quote: we believe that we can grow up to like 2000 plus crores of the AUM with the growth, profit also coming in.

items.statement: StoxKart targets doubling revenue and exponential demat account growth in 3 years
items.quote: So next three years, we basically we plan to grow, you know like 100% from here. Like we can say we plan to double our revenue.

items.statement: Industry seeing surge in retail participation with 50%+ new demat accounts from Tier 2-4 cities
items.quote: over 50% of new dema t accounts are bein g opened . M oreover youth engagement is significant. With 55% to 60% of this account opened by individuals below 35 years

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM at Rs 3801 crore
items.quote: our mutual fund AUM stands at Indian Rupees 3801 crores.

items.statement: Insurance sold 9,96,000 policies in FY24
items.quote: We sold 9,96,000 policies solidifying our market presence.

items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at around 27%. Net profit after tax reported rupees 66.2 crores while PAT margin stood at 13%.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 26%, PAT margin 11.5%
items.quote: EBITDA margin is stood at 26%. Net profit after tax was reported approximately rupees 188.3 crores, while the PAT margin percentage is stood at around 11.5%.

items.quote: In F Y24 EBIT contributions from our broking , distribution and trading business constituted 62% financing with contributed 34% to EBIT while insurance broking business contributed 4% to EBIT

items.quote: So currently we have around 2.5 lakh demat accounts in StoxKart. Shikhar Mundra: OK. Pranay Aggarwal: If that is your question. If you talk about downloads of our mobile app, our downloads are around 8,45,000

items.quote: We are adding like almost 1.25 to 1.5 l akh demat and trading account every year currently

items.quote: in all proprietary trading, we earned Rs. 45.8 Crores in this quarter.

items.statement: NBFC equity base ~Rs 445 crore, current leverage 1.84x, capacity to 3-3.5x

items.quote: we definitely have identified certain sectors as a negative sector wherein we don't lend, for example, the real estat e developer is one of the examples where we don't lend to or somebody who is in like infrastructure kind of business where the cash flows are long

items.quote: our total expense is around 19,00,00,000 and we earn 19.76 crores as revenue. OK, so we did a PBT of 78,00,000.

items.quote: Last year we did around same revenue. The revenue growth is you can say is muted. The reason being as I told you that last year our focus was on product development and now, we feel our product is upgraded to ou r satisfaction

items.quote: the last disbursing in that portfolio happened sometime in June 2022. And after that we have not disbursed any further loan.

items.quote: even today we have a tie up with Stockal the essence of the tie up is to allow trading in U.S. Securities so that is there.

items.quote: We are not like policy bazaar. We are increasing our efficiency to make it more productive and we are growing organically, right.

items.quote: We feel that we should be launching more close to about two projects every quarter.

items.quote: Our investment in new developments during this year has also been doubled to INR389 crores.

items.quote: Given our strong collections, the company has generated an OCF, an operating cash flow, of INR643 crores in FY 2024.

items.statement: Digital strategy shift to full-funnel approach drove 60% increase in walk-ins
items.quote: Our digital strategy changed to a full -funnel approach at top mid and bottom resulted in an increase of 60% in our walk-ins.

items.statement: Ajmera JV commercial project in Bandra: 6-8 months from RERA approval and launch
items.quote: On the approval front, I would like to state that we are at least about six to eight months away from any meaningful approval where we will go in for a RERA approval and then launch it.

items.statement: Labour shortages seen due to migration to Gaza/Israel/Ukraine; skilling initiatives underway
items.quote: In between, there was a huge move away of our labour to go and rebuild Gaza, Israel, the Ukraine. And we did see some amount of shortages.

items.statement: Crown project liquidation target: sell remaining inventory within 1.5-2 years driven by OC receipts and word-of-mouth
items.quote: We are seeing a lot more repeat customers that is encouraging us to believe that we should be able to liquidate all the inventory we have over there within the next year and a half or two.

items.statement: Redevelopment tender delays due to resident expectations; company avoids overbidding, lets high-bid projects go
items.quote: Sometimes we also see that projects go at unbelievably, high, I would say returns to the existing members. We will wait and watch to see how those projects perform.

items.statement: No geographical expansion outside MMR; exploring plotted developments and data centers within MMR
items.quote: We will continue to explore everything in this market and we continue to explore the potential of the other segments that are available in this market and try and focus our energies to serve all segments of the real estate requirements of our MMR area.

items.quote: We anticipate the upcoming year to be yet another extraordinary period for our organization and we are poised to achieve a 35%-40% increase in both our revenue and profits in FY25 with expectations to maintain this rate of growth going into FY26 as well.

items.quote: So, based on our expectations, we are looking at a 2.5-3 years payback period for our stores.

items.quote: So, last year, we did 190 in FY'22. In FY23, we did 210-220. And this year, we did 230-240 in terms of the realization.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected stable; margin improvement from product value not cost reduction
items.quote: We don't see a lot of movement in the raw material prices happening. It will be mainly driven by value in our products.

items.statement: No increase in debt planned for FY25; EBO expansion funded through internal profits
items.quote: No. As of now, we will not be increasing the debt this year. Most of the EB Os will be funded through our own profits, through the

items.quote: Reflecting on our growth trajectory from FY20 to FY24, we have achieved a revenue CAGR of 19% and EBITDA CAGR of 18% and a PAT CAGR of 33%.

items.quote: Once we achieve these two growths, we look at somewhere around 20% to 25% after that year. But we are very, very optimistic in the growth figures for the upcoming two years.

items.quote: Margins for the quarter stood at 10% as agains t 6% in Q4FY23 and 13% in previous quarter. Margins for the quarter could have been even higher but for the muted realisations mentioned earlier

items.quote: We expect the margin trajectory and EBITDA/ton improvement to sustain going forward as well on the back of our investment towards cost rationalization and commitment towards increasing the share of green energy in the overall mix.
