items.statement: Andhra Cement EBITDA breakeven expected by end Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are hopeful that it should have been in the current financial year. We should do the same thing by Q1, same time next year end of Q1 next year, we believe that we should reach to that point.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 18% for FY25, with ~16% from brand sales and ~2% from Dahej technical sales
items.quote: The revenue forecast given of 18%, around 16% is from the brand sales and about 2% is some technical sales from Dahej and the number includes both the businesses.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of ~18% for FY25, with gross margin expected at 38%
items.quote: You see we are of the opinion 38% gross margin appears to be sustainable. As against 39%, we are expecting 39% -- 38% gross margin because of which we are expecting EBITDA at around 18% this year.

items.statement: Volume growth expected at 15% for FY25 vs 9.07% in FY24
items.quote: And with La Nifia, we are expecting the volume growth to be in the range of 15

items.statement: Dahej plant incremental revenue target of INR40 crores for FY25
items.quote: It's around INR40 crores incremental?

items.statement: Normal capex for FY25 around INR20-25 crores; planning new herbicide plant at Dahej in H2 FY25, amount not finalized
items.quote: You see as far as the incremental capex for '24-'25, normal capex could be around in the range of INR20 crores. This year, the major capex was pertaining to the Dahej. And other than Dahej, it was around INR20 crores, INR25 crores.

items.statement: Further capex planned for new herbicide plant at Dahej in H2 FY25, amount not yet finalized
items.quote: Yes, Mr. Hussain. This FY '25, we are planning further capex for a new herbicide plant, and it will come in H2.

items.statement: Launched 3 new products (LaNevo, Purge, MYCORe Super) with LaNevo having market potential over INR1,000 crores
items.quote: Firstly, LaNevo , a powerful broad spectrum insecticide that effectively controls both sucking and chewing pests. This product is launched in collaboration with Nissan Chemicals, Japan. As you would have seen in the slide deck shared by us, this product has a huge market potential of over INR1,000 crores, which has developed only in last 2 years with only 3 products competing for market share and

items.statement: New products expected to contribute ~5% of overall revenue in FY25, with LaNevo alone targeting ~3%
items.quote: Our new product sales are included in the revenue growth target of 18%. The products which we have launched is LaNevo, which we are expecting around 3% growth in the total sales of the company. Overall, we are expecting around 5% growth from the new products.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit market share for new 9(3) products over 3-5 years
items.quote: Mr. Gandhi, I would just like to share these 3 products are very promising. We have launched them right now. Already, the products will be in the market within this first quarter. So in terms of market share, we are targeting at least a double-digit market share in these segments.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded ~400 bps in FY24; ~100-150 bps from low-cost inventory, ~300 bps from product mix
items.quote: I think, around 100 to 150 basis points because of the low cost of inventory and around 300 basis points because of the product mix.

items.statement: Dahej plant EBITDA loss of INR15 crores in FY24; expected loss of INR20 crores in FY25 due to full-year operations and R&D investment; breakeven expected in FY26
items.quote: You see in the current financial year, which is '23-'24, the EBITDA loss was around INR15 crores. And in the current financial '24-'25, we are expecting EBITDA loss of around INR20 crores.

items.statement: Above-normal monsoon (106% per IMD/Skymet) and La Nina conditions expected to drive strong demand in FY25
items.quote: The major weather forecasters have predicted above 100% rainfall this year on the back of developing La Nifia conditions. Therefore, this year, the demand for all our products are expected to be very good

items.statement: Generic molecule prices bottomed out; some products seeing price increases due to raw material shortages; branded specialty prices stable
items.quote: I think it is very unpredictable to comment on the prices. Right now, we already see that most of the generic products have bottomed out and few products, the increase is already seen due to unavailability of raw materials or increase in the prices of raw materials.

items.statement: Passing on raw material price changes to customers monthly; branded product prices increased where technical prices rose
items.quote: Wherever the technical prices have increased, we have also increased the prices of our branded products. We are passing on the increase as well as the decrease of raw material prices to the ultimate customers on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Dahej chemical synthesis plant commenced operations in FY24; new herbicide plant planned in H2 FY25
items.quote: Also in FY '24, Dhanuka has commenced operations at our Dahej chemical synthesis plant, and we are working to create breakthroughs in chemical synthesis with our new R&D laboratory with 30 chemists for research and chemical processes.

items.statement: New chemical R&D lab with 30 chemists established at Sanand to support Dahej manufacturing and contract manufacturing
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that we have established a new chemical R&D lab with 30 chemists to build speed in our product and process development capabilities at Sanand. This will help us in developing new products for manufacturing in Dahej and capture contract manufacturing opportunities.

items.statement: Generic:specialty revenue mix expected at 1/3:2/3 in FY25 vs 60:40 in FY24
items.quote: This year, generic and specialties, we are expecting around 1/3, 2/3.

items.statement: Launched 2 new 9(3) products in first 45 days of FY25; expecting 1 more in Q1; total 8 planned over 2 years, all in-licensed
items.quote: So the 9(3) products are the registration by Dhanuka. And we have already launched 2 products in the first 45 days and expecting to launch 1 more 9(3) plus in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing discussions ongoing with Japanese and other international companies; positive interest but nothing matured yet
items.quote: Yes. There are -- discussions are going on. We will come back to you when something matures.

items.statement: Channel inventories at higher levels in March; slow uptake in current quarter; expecting faster movement from June with monsoon onset
items.quote: The channel inventory for the industry in the month of March has again gone up to some extent. However, in the current quarter, we see a little slow uptake. And I think once the rains arrive from the month of June onwards, we should see faster movement.

items.statement: Dahej plant revenue INR7.5 crores in FY24; full-year operations in FY25
items.quote: It's around INR7.5 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend 400% (INR8/share) paid in FY24; final dividend 300% (INR6/share) recommended for AGM on 21 Aug 2024
items.quote: The company has already rewarded its members by paying an interim dividend at a rate of 400%. That is INR8 per equity share, having face value of INR? per share, which has absorbed INR36.47 crores. The Board of Directors has further recommended 300% final dividend that is INR6 per equity share.

items.statement: Marketing spend at 6-7% of revenue; increasing ~1% in FY25; employee cost ~20% of revenue with ~15% increase expected
items.quote: You see our marketing spend is in the range of around 6% to 7%. And this year, it will be around 1% higher than the previous year.

items.statement: Industry volume growth low single digits in FY24; Dhanuka volume growth 9.07%
items.quote: For Dhanuka, volume growth was 9.07%. For the industry, it was low single digits.

items.statement: Global agrochemical demand muted; US/Brazil destocking continuing; China supply ample; current Indian price increases may be temporary
items.quote: Yes, Rohanji, you're absolutely correct. And the general understanding in the industry is globally, the demand remains muted. And in my interactions with the companies in China also there is no dearth of supply right now. I think the current trend that we are seeing in the price increase is due to the momentary factor as Dhanukaji said around low inventory of technical and intermediates with India

items.statement: Kimitec collaboration at LOI stage only; no significant developments or launches expected in FY25
items.quote: So that is Mr. Shivam not a joint venture. It actually is right now only a letter of intent. And the idea is for research, development, marketing and manufacturing of the product. And right now, it is under work and it will take some time for it to commercialize.

items.statement: Guided FY25 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP in low-to-mid teens range and aim for high teens over 3 years
items.quote: we do expect next year our EBITDA margins to be the low to mid-teen range in terms of what we will exit. And we hope that we're able to do better. But that's, of course, what is the band in which we would like to give the guidance right now.

items.statement: Target double-digit top-line growth over next 3 years on organic basis
items.quote: we would like to grow our top line in double digits for the next -- on a 3-year basis. That's what as far as our top line and our margin line is concerned.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP at 11.4%, up 220 bps QoQ and 790 bps YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, our EBITDA margin pre-ESOP cost have expanded by 220 bps quarter-on-quarter to 11.4% and 790 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 660 bps YoY to 46.1% in Q4 FY24 driven by mix, cost optimization and price increases
items.quote: I'm happy to share that our gross margin ha s improved by 660 basis points t hat is from 39.5% in quarter 4 financial year '23 to 46.1% in quarter 4 financial year '24

items.statement: Expect Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin level to be sustainable in FY25 with quarterly fluctuations
items.quote: We believe, based on the projects that we are undertaking and the structural changes we had done, the margin of Q4 should be sustainable next year as well.

items.statement: API order book strong with regulated market orders allowing selectivity in price-sensitive markets
items.quote: I'm optimistic, looking at our current order book and our stable regulated market orders coming in through also allow us to be selective while participating in growth opportunities in some of the more price-sensitive markets.

items.statement: API capacity utilization at 70-75%; capacity sufficient for at least another year with plans to reshape mix
items.quote: We are today at about 70% to 75% is what we use. And that -- we have capacity with us, as for our current portfolio, is something that we largely have at least for another year.

items.statement: Turkey pricing actions fully compensating 60% inflation; price increases executed in June and January
items.quote: we are able to take our pricing increases to completely compensate for any inflation. And therefore, that helps us keep the margin in place as well as the top line.

items.statement: Portfolio reshaping toward higher-margin regulated markets and companion animal APIs; discontinued less attractive segments
items.quote: We have driven business growth with -- on portfolio, which are high growth, higher margins, and at the same time, we have also discontinued less attractive segments that we participate in.

items.statement: Expanding API customer base with new customers and commercialization of older contracts; 70% API revenue from regulated markets
items.quote: we are a very strong regulated markets player nearly 70% of our business comes from markets which have -- which are from Europe or the US a nd in these kinds of customers tend to give a lot of premium and reference for suppliers who are quality suppliers

items.statement: Leveraging regulated market strength to compete in emerging markets on margin-accretive basis
items.quote: when you have a leverage because of your regulated market supplies, you can be competitive in the emerging markets as well. So it's not a market that we're going to ignore. It's just that we will not be selling at any kind of price and compete just for that.

items.statement: Successfully completed WHO and global customer audits enhancing credibility as preferred supplier
items.quote: We have, also, successfully completed audits from WHO and many other global customers. This will enhance our credibility as a preferred supplier.

items.statement: Turkey hyperinflation accounting continues under IndAS 29; early signs of currency stabilization
items.quote: Net monetary loss on hyperinflation economy which is Turkey is shown under IndAS 29 adjustment which continues because the situation in Turkey. Turkey is amongst one of the 3 or 4 countries in hyperinflation as of now, so that still continues.

items.statement: Working capital improved to INR4,201 million from INR4,354 million YoY
items.quote: Our working capital stands at INR4,201 million as on March '24 as compared to INR4,354 million as of March '23.

items.statement: Net debt INR3,789 million; net debt/EBITDA improved to 3.55x from 4.70x; debt level expected stable but ratio to decline with EBITDA growth
items.quote: Net debt as on date, as on March 31, '24, is INR3,789 million against INR3,654 million in March '23. Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio has seen an improvement and which stands at 3.55 as on March '24 versus 4.70 in March '23.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A targets in formulations and API for R&D and manufacturing synergies; supported by promoter
items.quote: M&A is part of our growth plan. We are constantly evaluating targets, including some in India. And as far as the nature of targets are concerned, we are open both to targets and formulations as well as any opportunity on the API side

items.statement: API quarterly run rate targeting INR100 crore consistently in next 12-24 months; FY24 API revenue INR325 crore
items.quote: a three-digit number per quarter is what we certainly aspire to have consistently in the next 12 to 24 months. But beyond that, it would, of course, depend on how fast we are able to commercialize some of the new products

items.statement: Emerging markets mixed: Turkey stabilizing but Brazil tender volatility and MENA currency/repatriation challenges persist
items.quote: emerging markets will be a mix for a while. And the fact that the larger market sector, Turkey etcetera, for us are growing, we'll make sure that at an aggregate level, we will do well.

items.statement: U.S. formulation entry on hold; focusing on organic growth; M&A would be incremental if accretive
items.quote: I think the U.S. formulation piece, as we have said before, is on hold for us. We will look at our strategic priorities. As I said earlier, we are looking at M&A. We are looking at business development.

items.statement: ESOP cost declining trend expected to continue; may increase if leadership hires made
items.quote: ESOP generally, the impact is very high in initial few years, which we have seen in the last couple of years. And since last two quarters, the trend has already, if you see, has started going down. We believe that based on our current calculation, yes, the trend continues and our ESOP cost keeps on coming down.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guidance maintained at Rs 1,450-1,700 crore
items.quote: With commissioning of several ongoing projects and anticipated volume ramp-ups in existing products, we continue to maintain our expected EBITDA guidance of Rs. 1,450-1,700 crore for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guidance raised to 20-30% from 20-25%
items.quote: Yes. Actually, our earlier guidance was 20% to 25% in the last con-call, so that we have increased to 20% to 30% as a range.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA split expected 40-45% in H1 and 55-60% in H2
items.quote: Yes, I think it will be more 40%-45% and 55%-60%.

items.statement: FY24 capex over Rs 1,280 crore; FY25 capex planned at Rs 1,500-1,800 crore
items.quote: We entailed a CAPEX of over Rs 1,280 crore in FY24 on project expansions, and plan to spend another Rs 1,500-1,800 crore in FY25.

items.statement: FY26 capex upward of Rs 1,000 crore, not yet finalized
items.quote: FY'26, no, we have not yet fully finalized the numbers. I think that will be maybe in the next couple of quarters, where we'll be able to give a clearer guidance on the capex for FY'26.

items.statement: Nitro Toluene and ethylation blocks commissioning in Q2 FY25
items.quote: That will be looking at Q2 of FY'25, the commissioning for both Nitro Toluene and the downstream.

items.statement: Chloro Toluene project initial phase projected to commence by FY26
items.quote: Our Chloro Toluene project is also advancing well, with the initial phase projected to commence by FY26.

items.statement: Agrochemical segment under pressure; discretionary segments (dyes, pigments, specialty polymers, additives) seeing recovery
items.quote: This agrochemical segment is under pressure. So volumes in that segment are getting impacted. Whereas on the discretionary side, dyes, pigments, and other segments, there we are seeing good traction as far as demand is concerned.

items.statement: Agrochemical recovery expected in H2 FY25; calendar year 2025 near normal
items.quote: Yes. Agrochemical first half will be challenging. But I think in the second half, I think we should see a good recovery in agrochemical.

items.statement: Value-added downstream products expected to deliver 25-30% EBITDA margin on average
items.quote: No, we have a basket of products. So some of the products, there may be pressure. So on an average, this value-added product will give you a 25%, 30% range as EBITDA margin in that.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to structurally improve from FY26-27 with Chloro Toluene range
items.quote: As we had mentioned earlier that Chloro Toluene range these are more value-added products, so structurally, there the EBITDA margin is higher. So with those products coming in line on a weighted average basis, combined EBITDA also as a percentage will increase from FY '26-'27 onwards.

items.statement: First long-term contract (agro intermediate) contributed below Rs 100 crore in FY24; expected ~Rs 250 crore in FY25
items.quote: FY'24, I think it was below INR100 crore as some agrochemical impact had taken place. But this year, we expect more around INR250 crore or so.

items.statement: MMA contract revenue expected to grow 50-60% YoY in FY25
items.quote: Y-o-Y, this is 50% to 60% at least.

items.statement: FY24 revenue split: agro/pharma ~35%, discretionary ~65%
items.quote: This agro and pharma were around 35% and discretionary around 65%, and 35%, 65% kind of a number was there between discretionary and non-discretionary.

items.statement: Long-term contracts on raw-material-plus pricing; short-term contracts quarterly with price movement
items.quote: Certainly, in all the long-term contract we have structured pricing in place, whereas contracts which are more of a quarterly; orders which are more on a quarterly basis, there the prices may have some inherent movement also, up and downside.

items.statement: Absolute debt not expected to reduce due to ongoing capex; working capital optimization efforts continue
items.quote: So on an absolute basis, I'm not expecting debt numbers to reduce, but there will be efforts in terms of optimizing the working capital days, which could pot entially provide some optimization of debt, but the debt will be a bit higher than what it is currently right

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 1 per share (20%) for FY24
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs 1/- share (i.e 20%) for FY24.

items.statement: R&D centre at Navi Mumbai driving in-house development for Chloro Toluene range and sunrise sectors
items.quote: Yes, this entire Chloro Toluene range that is all in-house because we'll be adding a lot of new chemistry in that photochemistry, ni trilation, hydrolysis and grignard chemistry. So a lot of different chemistries, the products will be coming up in this entire Chloro Toluene range and also in a multipurpose plant

items.statement: Peak EBITDA from existing assets (excl. Chloro Toluene/MPP) estimated ~Rs 2,000 crore (10-15% above FY25 guidance high end)
items.quote: Yes. I think another additional 10% to 15% should be possible. So more towards INR 2,000 crores kind of a number should be possible from ongoing existing location expansion.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand recovery product-specific; some products may normalize only by calendar 2025
items.quote: Basically, it will be generally, this will be always product specifics. So somewhere the demand will pick up in this quarter, next quarter, and all. And some of them which are annual bases, where the demand pickup will be more happening in calendar year '25.

items.statement: Export geography mix: ~11% North America, 6% Europe, 4% China, 3% Japan, 28% rest of world
items.quote: But overall, on an an nualized basis, we had about 11% North America, 6% Europe and 4% in China, 3% Japan and rest of the world, 28

items.statement: Tax rate for FY25-26 expected around 12-16%
items.quote: Our tax rate for FY'25, FY'26, I believe it should be around 15%, maybe around 12% to 15% or 12% to 16%.

items.statement: Cable division guided at 25% year-on-year growth for FY25
items.quote: our guidance has been that we are expecting 25% year-on-year growth. Last year, the growth was lower than 25% because we had a big drop in Cable exports to the U.S. market.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 350-400 crores per year remains on track, focused on conductor rod making, alloying, CTC, bus bars, rods
items.quote: We were talking about doing INR350 crores to INR400 crores capex year-on-year. So that program still remains pretty much on track.

items.statement: Conductor order book INR 6,885 crores (premium 44.8%, export 37%); Q4 order inflow INR 3,018 crores (premium mix 57.5%); Cable order book INR 1,436 crores (export ~20%)
items.quote: Overall, our order book stands at about INR 6,885 crores, with the premium basket contributing to 44.8% and the export mix contributing to 37%. New order inflow for the quarter came in at INR 3,018 crores, of which the premium product mix is 57.5%.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across conductors, cables, transformer oil; Export demand weak from US (deinventorising, high rates, elections); Global sales ex-US grew 29.8% (Q4) and 51.8% (Cables Q4)
items.quote: Domestic demand continues to be strong, offsetting the weaker export demand that has been coming, especially from the U.S. market, where customers had been deinventorizing. Global sales growth, ex the U.S., actually grew at 29.8% in Q4.

items.statement: US market share fell from 26% (FY23 peak) to 12-13% (FY24); Australia third largest export market, growing; Indian Railways, solar, wind, renewables driving domestic cable growth
items.quote: Anand, it was at 26%. And today, at its peak, I mean in FY '23, it was at 26% of the revenues of that year. Today, it's about half of that, about 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Chinese competition intensifying in conductors and cables, especially building wires and solar cables in US, Asia, Africa, Latin America; US authorities cracking down on illegal routing; Sterlite Power main premium conductor competitor; GSK
items.quote: we see increased competition coming from Chinese exporters in most of the markets. Even in the U.S. market, they have been trying to skirt around the tariffs by illegally routing products through alternate geographies.

items.statement: CEA mandate: copper transposed conductors required for transformers >400 amps, driving CTC growth; RDSS scheme EPC portion ~35-40%, metering large allocation; MVCC projects under RDSS for safety
items.quote: There is a new requirement that has come in from Central Electricity Authority, which requires you to use copper transposed conductors for all transformers that exceed 400 amps.

items.statement: Full back-to-back hedging on copper/aluminum; margins per unit unchanged by raw material price moves; higher commodity prices may delay customer projects
items.quote: our margin will not change depending on the prices of copper or aluminum going up and down because we run a full hedge book. There is complete back-to-back hedging that happens on all the orders.

items.statement: QIP funds deployed in working capital reducing interest-bearing LC; No new debt details discussed
items.quote: because of the QIP funds coming in and getting deployed in working capital, our interest-bearing LC has come down.

items.statement: India transmission line addition: 14,203 ckm (FY24) vs 16,602 ckm target; FY25-27 target 17,500 ckm/yr and 80,000 MVA/yr transformation capacity; Renewable capacity addition 18.48 GW (FY24) vs 15.27 GW (FY23); Solar 81% of RE addition
items.quote: On a 12-month basis, 14,203 circuit kilometers of transmission lines were added, which has fallen short of the planned addition of 16,602. However, looking ahead in the next 3 years, it is targeted to add about 17,500 circuit kilometers of transmission lines per year and about 80,000 MVA of transformation capacity per annum.

items.statement: US market softness to continue near term (high rates, elections); Chinese export aggression; Short-term tender slowdown due to Indian elections; Red Sea freight costs hurting Europe exports
items.quote: We are also seeing a short-term slowdown in demand from tenders and some of the new conducting work, at least for this period given the fact that decision-making is reasonably paralyzed due to the ongoing elections

items.statement: Full capacity revenue potential Rs 350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 18%
items.quote: On a full-fledged capacity, the turnover will be around Rs. 350 crore. And the margins will be at the same level or maybe 18% somewhere.

items.statement: Target PAT margin 7-8%
items.quote: We are aiming around 7% to 8% PAT margin.

items.statement: FY25 incremental capex negligible at Rs 4-5 crore
items.quote: Negligible, not much, maybe maximum Rs. 4 to Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: Bulletproof/fireproof product attachments may cost Rs 5-7 crore
items.quote: certain attachments or the additional equipments which are not costing more than Rs. 5 to Rs. 7 crores.

items.statement: UAE plant capacity 28.5 lakh sqm at 34% utilisation; Silvassa 10.68 lakh sqm at 67%
items.quote: Our plant, Silvassa is having a capacity of 10.68 lakh square meter of architectural glass and currently operating on an average 67% of its capacity, whereas our UAE plant is having a capacity of 28.50 lakh square meter of architectural glass and currently operating on an average 34% of the capacity.

items.statement: India utilisation to cross 80-85% in FY25
items.quote: And secondly, India this year also we will cross 80%-85%.

items.statement: UAE order book 60 mn AED with 8-10 month execution; India Rs 30 crore annual order book
items.quote: Particularly related to this current year's performance , we have around 60 million order book position at UAE. And secondly, in India, we have around Rs. 30 crores order book position a year

items.statement: Portfolio mix target: 30-35% commodity, 30-35% mid-margin, 20-25% niche (bulletproof, fireproof, voice control)
items.quote: 30 % to 35% product portfolio of the commodity, 30% to 35% for the medium size margin product and around 25% to 20% for the niche product where we aligned our margins.

items.statement: India real estate demand growing with metro expansion, SRA schemes, and premium housing; visibility 5-10 years
items.quote: The demand, particularly in real estate in India will be growing year-on-year and with the housing requirement in India and particularly all metro stations , there is a very good demand and secondly visibility of the demand and the changing scenario of the real estate that all big corporates are now in the real estate.

items.statement: UAE market expanding across Dubai, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman, Muscat; growth-driven opportunity
items.quote: UAE , Dubai is expanding, Sharja is expanding, Ras Al Khaimah and Marjan area is also expanding. Ajman is also expanding and nearby country also expanding, Muscat and all. So, there is a growth in the market, so that growth, we will have a space in the growth market.

items.statement: UAE key competitors: White Aluminum, Gulf Glass, Emirates Glass; India: Fishfa, FG Glass, Glasstech, Fuso, Sapphire, Asahi
items.quote: major competitor in UAE is White Aluminum, Gulf Glass and Emirates Glass. Pranay Jain: And in India? Amrut Gada: India, we have here Fishfa Glass, FG Glass, Glasstech, Fuso and Sapphire and little bit of Ashai glass

items.statement: Promoter loans (quasi-equity) may convert to equity in 1-2 years
items.quote: Only thing that promoter funding, which has been infused as in loan, which we call it as quasi equity also, so that we can convert it into an equity , but not at this stage maybe in a couple of years.

items.statement: Post MPS compliance, may consider QIP to replace promoter loans or fund India expansion
items.quote: We can think about it. So, right now, whatever the promoters are selling is just to bring that the holding at 25% of the public as per the required norms of L ODR. So, post that, we can think about any QIP or anything for replacing this, the promoter loan or something like that or for the expansions, what we plan in India.

items.statement: In mid-stage discussions for acquisition/expansion in India; clarity in 1-2 months
items.quote: Yes, we are in discussion with some potential buyer, some expansion. It is mid stage, not early stage, also not on mature stage, but within one or two months it will be more clear.

items.statement: Promoter holding 77.45%; MPS compliance to 75% in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: In one or two quarter.

items.statement: UAE revenue FY25 target 80-90 mn AED (~Rs 180-200 crore); India Rs 92 crore
items.quote: India is around Rs. 92 crores and Dubai is around 80 to 90 million

items.statement: Float glass capacity additions by Saint-Gobain, Guardian aligned with demand growth per PwC survey; no oversupply expected
items.quote: So, that expansion is from Saint -Gobain and the Guardian and other players for manufacturing the float glass. So, we have also done one survey recently from P WC. So, there is a gap in between demand . Demand is increasing so that exp ansion and whatever is coming in future that is aligned with the growth of the demand.

items.statement: Solar glass market surveyed; no investment decision yet; focus remains architectural
items.quote: We are also working on solar requirement as this capacity is also increasing, solar glass, green energy glass. And we recently did a survey of the market that solar demand , solar glass demand and architectural glass demand and automobile demand. Right now, we are totally focused on architectur al, but at the same time, we are also working on the solar market. If everything works, then management

items.statement: Targeting 6-7% same-store sales growth for FY25 to return EBITDA margins to 28-30% range
items.quote: we are focusing on 6% to 7% and considering the trend of March and April, the 6% to 7% SSG we are focusing to achieve those coming back to that EBITDA margin of 28% to 30% range.

items.statement: Expect to cross Rs 1,000 crore revenue by mid-FY27, maintaining ~20% CAGR plan
items.quote: Broadly it is same. There 20% CAGR we have been planned , so not exactly by end of FY2 6 but mid of FY27 or FY27, we are definitely going to cross Rs. 1,000 crores revenue

items.statement: Targeting online sales of Rs 50 crore in FY25, around 6-7% of total revenue
items.quote: This year we are targeting the net sales of around Rs. 50 crores. So, this would be something around 6% to 7% of the overall company sales.

items.statement: Committed to maintaining 55-56% gross margin going forward

items.statement: Final dividend INR4 per share announced (subject to AGM approval) plus INR58 interim dividend paid in Jan'24; INR100 crores investable surplus for growth and shareholder rewards

This is subject to the approval of the shareholders at the Annual General Meeting. And this is in addition to the interim dividend of INR58 per share paid in January '24.

items.statement: Michel Pauli joined as new MD of Estima AG; leadership team changes made to improve capacity utilization and technical capabilities
items.quote: We are happy to announce that Mr. Michel Pauli, a very experienced technology and business leader has joined as the new Managing Director of Estima. In addition, we have made several chan ges in the operating and leadership team at Estima.

items.statement: Impairment loss taken on Estima via Kamla International Holdings and Pylania SA due to continuous losses
items.quote: Due to continuous losses in Estima, we have made a provision by impairing the value of investment in these entities in our financials.

items.statement: Estima turnaround delayed by ~1 year due to unexpected slowing in Swiss watch business
items.quote: But, because of the unexpected slowing down in the Swiss watch business, this turnaround will probably be delayed by about a year.

items.statement: Silvercity Brands global launch of Favre-Leuba scheduled for last quarter of current year; brand establishment expected to take 3-5 years
items.quote: This current increase in the capital of Silvercity Brand s is essentially for the requirements of working capital and to be able to launch the brand globally, which is scheduled to be done in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: KDDL maintains ~54% stake in Ethos; committed to majority ownership but further stake sales possible
items.quote: KDDL and my input together, we currently have about 54% of Ethos. It is our articulated thing that our position that KDDL will continue to maintain a majority stake in Ethos, there is no question. Whether there will be some more stake sale, we cannot say right now. But we will continue to maintain majority.

items.statement: Management prefers factory visits over frequent calls; plans 2-3 factory visit events per year for serious analysts
items.quote: We would like to organize at least twice a year, maybe more visits to our factories, where we have a full day of discussion analysis after you have seen the factory, you've got a feel for what is our business.

items.statement: FY2024 was an elevated and peak capex year; clear moderation expected in FY2025
items.quote: We have always mentioned that FY2024 will be an elevated and peak level of capex and I expect to see clear moderation going into FY2025.

items.statement: Wireless capex to moderate meaningfully in FY2025; transport, enterprise, data center, and homes capex to continue
items.quote: I think where the moderation will happen is really on wireless capex which accounts by the way for a large part of the capex so to that extent we do see moderation going ahead into next year.

items.statement: B2B capex had one-off fiber and data center spends in Q4; submarine cable investments are lumpy
items.quote: our B2B business had a bit of one -off this quarter which is primarily related to fiberi zation so we bought some fibers and some spends o n the data center business

items.statement: Rolled out ~43,100 network sites and ~55,982 km of fiber in FY2024; 5G available nationwide
items.quote: We rolled out about 43,100 network sites and 55,982 kilometers of fiber. Our bet on NSA which is a non-standalone technology paid off it just not only saved us capex it also delivered superior experience.

items.statement: Plan to roll out over 25,000 rural sites in next couple of quarters, lower than last year
items.quote: We have commenced another round of expan sion here to plug this gap. We expect to rollout over 25000 sites lower than last year in the next couple of quarters

items.statement: Industry customer additions in low single digits annually over last 12 quarters
items.quote: You are seei ng that customer addition in the low single digits at the aggregate level

items.statement: India RoCE 9.5% in FY2024, extremely low; tariff repair needed to improve returns
items.quote: Our RoCE for India is 9.5%, which is extremely low for a business that is so essential to the digital spine of this country. Clearly tariff repair is needed to set this right.

items.statement: Tariff repair essential; current ARPU ~Rs 209, right level ~Rs 300; industry needs substantial repair
items.quote: We are already at just over Rs. 200 ARPU. I think the right level of ARPU even at Rs. 300 would still be one of the lowest in the world so there is substantial repair to be had in the industry.

items.statement: Tariff hikes will occur in multiple rounds, not one shot; SIM consolidation modest; digital essentiality supports absorption
items.quote: Obviously it will not go in one shot from 200 to 300 that is not going to happen but it will have a couple of rounds to actually get there.

items.statement: 5G base ~72 million as of March 2024, growing 2-2.5M/month; free 5G doubles data usage vs 4G
items.quote: We have roughly 72 million 5G customers as of March 2024. This is growing currently at the rate of 2 to 2.5 million every month.

items.statement: DTH customer base grew 9,000 in Q4 and 200,000+ in FY2024, only operator to grow; moderate price hike due to broadcaster increases
items.quote: On an annual basis after two years of decline we grew our customer base by over 200,000 net adds the only operator in the industry to grow customers during this year.

items.statement: Mobile churn reduced from 2.9% in Q3 to 2.4% in Q4 via structural grid-based experience program
items.quote: This was also supported by our structural efforts to fix the network experience which saw mobile churn reducing from 2.9% in Q3 to 2.4% in Q4.

items.statement: Welcome VI fundraising; three strong private operators good for India; market remains brutally competitive
items.quote: I am glad to see that VI has raised money a nd I really wish them well. I think India will be we ll served if it has three good private operators working there

items.statement: Rights issue guidance of three years has 6-8 months left; formal revised guidance expected in 3-5 months
items.quote: Our understanding is more a guidance and we will have to chew on what is the outlook for the free cash flows so maybe by the next three to five months we will come out with a more formal either a revised guidance or whatever commentary that we have to provide.

items.statement: India net debt/EBITDA at 2.86x; paid Rs 16,350 Cr debt in FY2024; expect further reduction
items.quote: India net debt to EBITDA is n ow at a comfortable level of 2.86. We expect further debt reduction going forward

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom repaid Rs 1,500 Cr in Q4; net debt/EBITDA 2.14x at year-end
items.quote: I am happy to report we have repaid about Rs. 1500 Crores of debt in Q4 and ended the year with a net debt to EBITDA of about 2.14.

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom IPO completed; investor confidence reflects brand, execution, integrity, governance
items.quote: I want to start by th anking our investors for showing confidence in us through the recently concluded Bharti Hexacom IPO. This speaks well about the brand Airtel, about our execution capabilities, high standards of integrity and corporate governance

items.statement: Dividend policy premature; combination of deleveraging and dividend as cash generation improves
items.quote: Obviously as we generate more cash a combination of deleveraging and dividend will happen. I think it is too premature for us to comment on any dividend policy.

items.statement: All 20,000 employees spent a day with frontline staff in March; ongoing ritual to improve experience
items.quote: We think of Airtel as having only two types of people those who serve customers and those who serve those who serve customers. It is with this in mind that we had every one of our 20,000 people get out into the market and spend a whole day with our frontline people in March.

items.statement: Airtel Business domestic revenue growing 18-20% annually; global wholesale business under pressure from OTT cutbacks
items.quote: The domestic business is on a strong footing and continues to grow at 18 to 20%.

items.statement: Payments Bank MTU 67M; annualized revenue run rate >Rs 2,100 Cr; deposits ~Rs 2,800 Cr, up ~50% YoY
items.value: 67M MTU; Rs 2,100 Cr revenue run rate
items.quote: Monthly transacting users under 67 million. The annualized revenue run rate is now over 2100 Crores; deposits remain robust at around 2,800 Crores growing nearly 50% year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets FY25 disbursements of INR3,600-3,800 crores and AUM of INR15,000 crores by March 2025
items.quote: the company is confident of reaching a disbursement of INR3,600 crores to INR3,800 crores, an AUM of INR15,000 crores, stage 2 numbers between 7% and 9% and GNPA below 3% by March '25.

items.statement: Targets FY25 PAT of INR450-475 crores implying 20-25% profit growth
items.quote: Anywhere between INR450 crores to INR475 crores.

items.statement: Expects FY25 NIM of 4.8-5.2% versus 5.23% in FY24 due to aggressive pricing for salaried home loans
items.quote: As far as NIM is concerned, yes, we now have a NIM of around 5.2%. But going forward, it may not be 5.2%. It may be a nywhere between 4.8% to 5.2

items.statement: Expects FY25 net credit cost to be minimal with potential negative provisions of INR20-40 crores from NPA recoveries
items.quote: The credit cost for this year is expected to be minimal.

items.statement: Targets FY25 ROA around 3% and ROE around 15.8%
items.quote: ROA should be anywhere around 3%. And ROE should be around the same. We were around 15.8%. Hopefully, we should be able to maintain around the same range.

items.statement: Targets FY25 cost-to-income ratio around 24%
items.quote: cost -to-income ratio is around 24% for the w hole year. Hopefully, with the likely increase in the income because of our recovery -- sorry, because of our expansion as well as the recovery that is going to give us income, I think this cost to the income ratio should be -- we should be able to maintain around 24

items.statement: Plans to add 40 outlets in FY25 to reach 250 total touch points
items.quote: We will be adding another 40 outlets in FY '25 to make the number of outlets to 250.

items.statement: Expects FY25 employee expense growth of 10-12% over FY24's INR102 crores
items.quote: last year, we were around INR102 crores. So maybe this time, there may be a 10% to 12% increase, that is for FY '24-25.

items.statement: Expects Phase 2 IT project to cost additional INR15-16 crores in FY25
items.quote: maybe another INR15 crores to INR16 crores will be there for Phase 2.

items.statement: Reduced GNPA from INR618 crores in Q3 FY24 to INR552 crores (4.1% of AUM) in Q4 FY24; Net NPA at 1.5%
items.quote: We were able to reduce the GNPA from INR618 crores in Q3 FY '24 to INR552 crores, which is 4.1% of the AUM. Net NPA stood at INR192 crores at 1.5%.

items.statement: FY24 full-year NPA reduction of INR168 crores; total provisions INR518 crores with 65.2% Stage 3 coverage
items.quote: We have reduced the NPA by INR168 crores for the full year. For the NPAs, we have a total provision of INR518 crores with a provision coverage ratio of 65.2% for Stage 3 assets.

items.statement: Restructured portfolio of INR528 crores as of March 2024, with INR158 crores in Stage 3
items.quote: As of March 31, 2024, we hold INR528 crores of restructured portfolio outstanding in our book, of which approximately INR158 crores are in Stage 3 and remaining in Stage 1 and 2.

items.statement: FY24 slippages INR150 crores, recoveries INR316 crores; Q4 slippages INR37 crores, recoveries INR101 crores
items.quote: INR150 crores was the slippage for the whole year, INR360 crores for the -- INR316 crores was the recoveries for the whole year. For the last quarter alone, if you want, one minute -- it is INR37 crores of slippages and INR101 crores of recovery.

items.statement: Targets FY25 net NPA reduction of INR60-100 crores and provision release of INR40-50 crores
items.quote: Going forward we expect a reduction of aro und max minimum of INR60 crores up to INR100 crores of NPA reduction. So this will help us in releasing a provision anywhere between INR40 crores to INR50

items.statement: ~INR300 crores of NPA over 1000 days old; plans simplified settlement scheme for vintage borrowers
items.quote: out of around INR500 odd crores, INR300 odd crores, I do not have the exact number, around INR300 crores is more than 1000 days old.

items.statement: New loans disbursed since Jan 2022 (INR5,700 crores) show 0.24% NPA and 1.8% Stage 2
items.quote: we have disbursed something around INR5,700 crores from January'22, which means in 27 months, we have disbursed out side of INR5,700 crores. Our NPA in this book is only INR24 crores, it is 0.24%.

items.statement: FY24 NIM 5.23% up from 4.84% in FY23; spread maintained at 3.38% with yields at 11.75%
items.quote: Our NIM for FY '24 was at 5.23%, up from 4.84% in FY '23. The company has been able to maintain a spread of 3.38% for FY '24 by raising yields to 11.75% despite facing stiff competition at our pricing levels.

items.statement: FY24 disbursements INR3,135 crores (12.7% growth ex-DA pool); sanctions INR3,340 crores (7.9% growth ex-DA pool)
items.quote: Our disbursements for FY '24 was a record high of INR3,135 crores as against INR2,919 crores of FY '23. On a comparative basis, we have registered a growth of 12.7%, excluding the DA pool buyouts done in FY '23 for INR136 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 disbursements INR895 crores, sanctions INR978 crores; 9% and 16% Y-o-Y growth ex-DA pool
items.quote: We were able to achieve disbursements of INR895 crores against INR835 crores in Q4 '23. Our sanctions stood at INR978 crores as compared to INR966 crores in Q4 '23. Excluding the DA pool buyout transaction we did in Q4 '23, the growth in sanctions and disbursements are 9% and 16% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: AUM INR13,513 crores as of March 2024, up 9% Y-o-Y after INR168 crore GNPA reduction
items.quote: After taking into account GNPA reduction of INR168 crores, our AUM stands at INR13,513 crores, an increase of 9% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Plans to maintain ~75:25 housing to non-housing mix; salaried share may rise from 52% to 53-54%
items.quote: See, as of now, the ratio between home loan and non -home loan is 75% and 25%. Under non home loan, LAP constitutes only around 15%. So going forward as well, we will be maintaining the same ratios.

items.statement: 56% of loan book from Tamil Nadu; plans to increase exposure in Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra; Tamil Nadu share may decline to 50-54%
items.quote: Gradually, of course, 56% of our loan book is from Tamil Nadu because of the effect -- base effect. So Tamil Nadu may slow -- may come down slightly, maybe from 56% it may come to 55% or 54%. We will be increasing our exposure in non-Tamil Nadu especially in the southern regions of Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra and all, that is our plan of action.

items.statement: No immediate plans for Northern India expansion; focus on existing geographies for FY25
items.quote: At least for FY '24-25, I do not want to venture into new geographies because the existing geographies itself, there are so many new places to venture into.

items.statement: Spent INR24 crores on IT transformation (LLMS, EGL); INR13.5 crores capitalized; Phase 2 underway for back-office ops
items.quote: Phase one of the project comprising of LLMS and EGL are completely integrated and fully functional. Applications planned for Phase 2 are under progress. We have so far spent INR24 crores, of these, INR13.5 crores have already been capitalized.

items.statement: Total IT project cost ~INR40 crores excluding security; INR22 crores spent; INR15-16 crores remaining for Phase 2
items.quote: the total project cost, excluding any security -related expenses is around INR40 crores. We have already spent around INR22 crores. So it will be -- maybe another INR15 crores to INR16 crores will be there for Phase 2.

items.statement: NHB funding eligibility restored as Net NPA below threshold; can access post-AGM; NHB cheaper than bank funding but allocation uncertain
items.quote: It's definitely possible because now that our net NPA has come down we become definitely eligible for our NHB funding. Of course, that can happen only post the AGM because NHB normally expects the AGM to be over.

items.statement: Plans to double collection team from ~80 to ~150 people in FY25; focus on 1-90 day overdue bucket
items.quote: We had around 80 -- 80-odd people for collection. Now we want to almost double it to around 150 for this current year. Our focus this particular year will be more on collection s, especially 1 to 90 days

items.statement: Sales force to increase from ~200 to ~300 foot-on-street personnel in FY25 (excluding branch heads)
items.quote: Last year, we had around 200 salespeople. This year, our foot-on-street sales persons will be around 300. This will be excluding the branch head, okay?

items.statement: Added Chief Business Officer; plans middle-level hires in sales, collection, underwriting; no senior-level additions
items.quote: we have already informed one CBO, Chief Business Officer, Mr. Raja has already joined and we may induct some people at the middle level under all verticals whether it is sales, collection or even in underwriting, at middle level, but not at the senior level, perhaps, but definitely at the middle level.

items.statement: FY24 PAT INR395 crores up 32% Y-o-Y; Q4 PAT INR108 crores up 32% Y-o-Y and 8.7% Q-o-Q
items.quote: For the whole year, we have earned a net profit of INR395 crores against INR296 crores for FY '23. Our ROA and ROE stood at 3% and 15.8%, respectively, for FY '24 as against the respective figures for FY '23 at 2.5% and 13.5%.

items.statement: Average ticket size for new book ~INR20 lakhs vs ~INR12-13 lakhs two years ago; overall book average ~INR12 lakhs
items.quote: Yes. Today, my average ticket size is around INR20 lakhs. 2 years back, it was only around INR12 lakhs to, INR13 lakhs. So my average ticket size for the new book is around INR20 lakhs. But for the entire book it's around INR12 lakhs.

items.statement: Expects Q1 FY25 disbursements to be dull due to branch transfers and new openings; Q2 and Q4 are peak quarters
items.quote: First quarter will be slightly dull let me admit, but going forward, yes, it will pick up. Normally for this company second and fourth quarters are peak quarters.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 13-16%
items.quote: the top line as you said, between 13% to 16% somewhere around there.

items.statement: US business expected to maintain at least 10% growth
items.quote: We should at least maintain a 10%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 400 bps to 33% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 400 basis points while PA T margins by 300 basis points.

items.statement: US EBITDA margin 37% vs India 29%
items.quote: So, we have EBITDA margin of 37% in USA and in India it is about 29%.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin expected around 33% with improvement as revenue grows
items.quote: if you look at on annual numbers from 29% to 33%, this is what we can expect.

items.statement: US demand visibility better after Q4 pressure
items.quote: The overall demand situation is as such I think Q4 there was some pressure on that. But apart from that, the visibility is better.

items.statement: Human nutrition growth driven by US recovery and biocatalyst
items.quote: Human nutrition we're talking some growth has to come up from the US going forward and some has to come up from the biocatalyst area in the coming few years.

items.statement: No formal order book; business is order-to-order
items.quote: So, in our business, there is no contract as such or the order book kind of things, generally order- to-order which you know the customers and you know the pains and that is where it's always difficult to predict exact numbers of re venue what it will be and exactly how it will be and quarter-and-quarter how they will

items.statement: ₹30-40 crore R&D center investment over next two years
items.quote: maybe about somewhere around ₹30-40 crores developing this R&D centers.

items.statement: Capacity utilization ~65%; expansion triggered at 80%
items.quote: The capacity should be about 65% utilization, difficult to say because it's always a cat and mouse game, at the same time when there will be the 80% utilization, probably we will go for it for the expansion, we will build up slowly, slowly small areas so that we can build it up with very fast.

items.statement: Pricing stationary; input costs stable and expected to continue
items.quote: It is more stationary, Nikhil.

items.statement: Input costs stable; logistics higher due to Red Sea but manageable
items.quote: Input cost more or less is stable in terms of raw material prices and other prices, and we expect the same to continue.

items.statement: Human nutrition mix expected 65-70% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, we expect it to grow, but in terms of percentage probabl y it will be between 65 % to 70% because there are some other businesses as well

items.statement: Top 10 customers 26% of revenue; top customer 4-5%
items.quote: Top 10 customers sale is about 26% as compared to 24% in FY '23.

items.statement: Pricing pressure exists in competitive segments; Serratio faces competition
items.quote: bit is always there on this side. When there is a competition, pricing pressures are always there. Some areas you enjoy monopoly, some areas where it's going to be the pricing pressure cod EnzymesWhore ENZYME is Life Advanced Enzyme Technologies Limited May 15, 2024 and you need to evolve with the new ideas and new thoughts and with the R&D you need to improve your productivity

items.statement: Two EFSA food enzyme dossiers approved; two USFDA GRAS no-question letters received
items.quote: We have received approval of two food enzyme dossiers from EFSA. Over and above, we also received no-question letter for our two GRAS filings with USFDA.

items.statement: Logistics cost elevated due to Red Sea conflict but manageable
items.quote: Some areas, the logistic cost is still on a higher side because of all this red sea conflict, which is going on, but still it is okay, manageable, it's not really impacting to a very great level the way it used to be during the COVID time and other time.

items.statement: ₹500 crore cash on balance sheet; generating ~₹100 crore annually
items.quote: we have around ₹500 crores of cash on the balance sheet, and we generate around ₹100 crores of cash every year.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; using cash for dividends, capex, acquisitions
items.quote: last year we have declared interim dividend, this year we are continuing with the interim dividend, and apart from that, we are keeping the cash with us to make sure that whenever we have some opportunity, we use that money and to expand our business, and apart from that the normal capital expenditures and -

items.statement: Acquired 5.89% stake in JC Biotech for ₹56.07 million; now 95.72%
items.quote: During the year, we have also acquired an additional stake of 5.89% in JC Biotech for the total cash consideration of ₹56.07 million. Now, the shareholding of Advanced Enzymes, in JCB has increased to 95.72%.

items.statement: Actively seeking probiotic acquisitions; no specific target identified
items.quote: Well, we are always in search, but if you come across any good company, please let us know.

items.statement: Continuing interim dividend policy
items.quote: last year we have declared interim dividend, this year we are continuing with the interim dividend

items.statement: Building new R&D center in Nashik; 120,000 sq ft, 3x current capacity
items.quote: we have already taken a 15 -acre land during the COVID time in Nasik, in Pathardi areas, we are coming up with a new R&D center , right now we are building up about 120,000 sq uare feet building. I think it should be around three times of our current R&Ds what we are doing

items.statement: evoxx impaired ~₹18-19 crore; contract research didn't materialize
items.quote: we have taken an impairment as well this year into our balance sheets, impairment of about 18, 19 crores on the Advanced Enzymes balance sheet, if you look at it, we have taken impairment loss as well.

items.statement: R&D spend 4.58% of revenue (3.2% post-elimination)
items.quote: Our R&D expendi ture during the year is about ₹274 million as compared to ₹290 million in FY'23. Percentage of R&D expenditure on consolidated basis, we spend about 4.58% as compared to 5.06

items.statement: One-time ₹151 million court judgment impact in AST Enzymes
items.quote: During Q4, there is one-time impact of ₹151 million on profitability due to adverse judgment of the court in lawsuit in one of our US subsidiary, AST Enzymes.

items.statement: Business always carries risk; no other pending litigation seen
items.quote: Business is always full of risk. I can't comment on that, but as of now, like I don't see any other thing which is there in like but it's always a risk and what will pop up tomorrow, you never know, right.

items.statement: Management expects sugar crushing of 560-570 lakh quintals for season 2024-25, subject to monsoon.
items.quote: So, overall, we are thinking around, again, this is 544, 534 next year, we are anticipating around 560, 570, but it is very early to say because the whole period of monsoon is still pending.

items.statement: Management expects sugar inventory to be liquidated by November or December 2024.
items.quote: So, we are expecting whatever inventory build-up is there that is going to be liquidated the way it has been liquidated last year by November or December end.

items.statement: Management estimates all-India sugar production at 32-32.5 lakh tons net for next season.
items.quote: We are estimating the production is going to be similar to the current year level only. On a gross level basis, around 34, 35 and with allowing a diversion of again 1.7, 1.8. So, we have a net sugar in the position around 32, 32.5.

items.statement: Management expects average sugar realization in UP around Rs 39 per kg for next year.
items.quote: Our estimate is the average realizations in UP for the next year is going to be around INR39.

items.statement: Management states sustainable EBITDA of Rs 300 crores annually under current policies.
items.quote: This is a sustainable EBITDA. Yes, this is a sustainable EBITDA. Today's policies. 300 sustainable EBITDA, absolutely.

items.statement: Hargaon expansion capex of Rs 151 crores to increase crushing capacity from 10,000 to 13,000 TCD and reduce steam consumption from 42% to 31-32%, completion by 2025-26.
items.quote: The total capex at Hargaon is INR151 crores and it is to be completed in the first phase, partly in 2024, 2025 and it will be completed totally in 2025, 2026 and start giving benefit from November , 2025.

items.statement: Rosa multi-feed distillery capex of Rs 147 crores for 100 KLPD capacity, pending government approvals, expected completion by end of FY26.
items.quote: At Rosa, we are still awaiting from the government approval. We are hoping all the government approvals will come to us by September 2024 and the distillery will start operation by the end of financial year 2025, 2026. And the capital outgo for Rosa distillery is INR147 crores.

items.statement: Hargaon crushing capacity being increased from 10,000 to 13,000 TCD with steam consumption reduction from 42% to 31-32%.
items.quote: At Hargaon, we are going to increase our crushing capacity from 10,000 to 13,000 TCD. And along with that, we will bring down our steam consumption from 42% to 31% or 32%.

items.statement: Rosa multi-feed distillery of 100 KLPD will take total ethanol capacity from 325 to 425 KLPD, enabling ~14 crore litres annual production.
items.quote: Right now we have an ethanol capacity of 325 KLPD. We are considering a new plant, multi-feed plant at Rosa of 100 KLPD. It means our capacity will go up from 325 to 425 and our production capacity on 345 days if you convert into it will be around INR14 crores litre.

items.statement: Ethanol sales in Q4 FY24 were lower by 26% due to changes in government policies.
items.quote: However, ethanol sales during quarter 4 was lower by 26% at INR183 lakhs quintal compared to last year INR246 lakhs quintal due to changes in government policies.

items.statement: Ethanol order book of 3.64 crore litres each for Q1-Q2 and Q3-Q4 FY24, with 95% supplied in first half.
items.quote: In the quarter 1 and quarter 2, we have an order of 3 crores 64 lakh litres. Against that, they have taken from us 3 crores 42 lakh litres. It means around 95% we have supplied to them. And the balance they have diverted to the next quarter 3 and quarter 4. And in quarter 3 and quarter 4, we have an order in hand of 3 crores 64 lakh litres.

items.statement: Sugar inventory valued at Rs 3,441 per quintal as on March 31, 2024.
items.quote: The way I told you earlier, sugar inventory is INR37.99 lakhs quintal as on 31st March 2024. This was INR24.92 lakhs quintal as on 31st March 2023, and the sugar inventory is valued at INR3,441 per quintal.

items.statement: Government policy changes on ethanol procurement led to 52% higher ethanol inventory and higher short-term borrowing.
items.quote: Recent changes in government's ethanol procurement policy has burdened us to carry higher inventory by almost 52% as on 31 March 2024 compared to last year, resulting into higher short-term borrowing.

items.statement: Management expects government may allow B-molasses or syrup diversion given high opening stock of 85-91 lakh tons.
items.quote: And considering that there is an opening stop around 91, 80, 85 to 91, the government may again relook into the allowing B molasses or syrup.

items.statement: Total debt not expected to increase despite Rs 298 crores capex; Rs 95-111 crores annual repayment over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Our overall borrowing is not going to go up because every year we have a repayment of around INR95 to INR111 crores in the next 2 years, 3 years.

items.statement: Rosa distillery project of Rs 147 crores to be funded with ~Rs 100 crores borrowing, repaid over 2 years.
items.quote: Against this project we are hoping to borrow around INR100 crores against INR151 crores total project cost and INR100 crores borrowing on a new generation of around INR47, INR48 crores will be repaid over a period of 2 years time.

items.statement: Varietal shift from CO238 to CO118 and 15023; CO238 share to drop from 60-65% to 20-25% next season.
items.quote: '23-'24 we can say around or total C0238 was around 60%-65% and next year we are anticipating around 20% maximum, 20% to 25%.

items.statement: New varieties CO118 and 15023 have similar recovery but 5-10% lower yield than CO238.
items.quote: Recovery more or less same as 238 but yield slightly 5% to 10% less than 238.

items.statement: Sugar recovery expected to improve next season as new varieties outperform deteriorated CO238.
items.quote: Whatsoever recoveries we are getting last 2 years in 238 the upgraded new varieties will give better recovery than 238 is giving at the moment. We are expecting better recovery next year.

items.statement: Sugar inventory increased to 37.99 lakh quintals from 24.92 lakh quintals YoY as of March 31, 2024.
items.quote: The way I told you earlier, sugar inventory is INR37.99 lakhs quintal as on 31st March 2024. This was INR24.92 lakhs quintal as on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Narkatiaganj sugar plant crushing capacity to increase from 7,500 TCD to 10,000 TCD by November-December 2024
items.quote: We are going to complete all our capex plan during the current financial year. Both the capex which we have projected and announced to the exchanges, one is Narkatiaganj where we are increasing the capacity from 7,500 to 10,000. This will go on steam by November, December this year itself.

items.statement: Narkatiaganj expansion capex of Rs 141 crores expected to yield EBITDA margin of at least 25%
items.quote: The total invested capital cost is around Rs 141 crores, and this project is going to give us an EBITDA of not less than 25%.

items.statement: Sidhwalia distillery conversion to multi-feed with grain attachment at Rs 32 crores capex
items.quote: The capital cost involved in converting this distillery, this molasses-based distillery to this multi-feed is around Rs 32 crores only.

items.statement: Sidhwalia distillery capacity 150 KLPD, can run 340 days to achieve 5.50 crore litres annually with grain
items.quote: Our plan is that we have the capacity of 150 right now and we can easily run on 340 days. It means we can go up to 5.50 Cr litres.

items.statement: FY24 sugar crushing at 239.98 lakh quintals, up 10% YoY
items.quote: FY24 crushing was at Rs 239.98 lakh quintals as against Rs 219.13 last year an increase of almost 10%.

items.statement: FY24 sugar production at 25.09 lakh quintals, up 21% YoY
items.quote: Sugar production during FY24 was at Rs 25.09 lakh quintals as compared to Rs 20.69 lakh quintals in the previous year an increase of 21%.

items.statement: FY24 average sugar realization at Rs 3,796 per quintal, up 6% YoY
items.quote: The average realization during the year was Rs 3,796 per quintal as against Rs 3,572 per quintal an increase of 6% in the last year.

items.statement: FY24 ethanol production at 498 lakh litres, sales at 467 lakh litres, average realization Rs 60.14 per litre
items.quote: At the ethanol side, total production for the full year was Rs 498 lakh litres as against Rs 393 lakh litres and the total sales of ethanol was Rs 467 lakh litres as against Rs 399 lakh litres in the corresponding year last year. Average realisation stood at Rs 60.14 per litre as against Rs 60.76 per litre.

items.statement: Bihar cane availability ample, peak crushing potential 288 lakh quintals vs 237 lakh quintals last season
items.quote: Yes, Vikram. To answer your question, last year, sugar season, we have swept around 237. We can go right now up to 288 there.

items.statement: Maize availability of 1 lakh metric tons from Samastipur, Begusarai, Khagaria districts for multi-feed distillery
items.quote: The availability of maize will be about 1 lakh metric ton from Samastipur, Begusarai and Khagaria districts. And that is already available.

items.statement: Bagasse conversion to power preferred over sale; Bihar power tariff Rs 5.6-6.5 per unit vs bagasse sale Rs 3.5 per unit
items.quote: Yes, at the price of Rs 5.6 to Rs 6.5 it is always beneficial. Even I sell bagasse, it means I am realizing not more than Rs 3.50 per unit. It is better to convert bagasse into power.

items.statement: Ethanol mix flexible: last season 44% C-heavy, 56% B-heavy; prefer B-heavy and juice if policy permits
items.quote: No, we basically will go for the B heavy only if the government allows it to. Last year 44% was on C Heavy and 66% was on B heavy. Before that 93% was on B heavy and 7% on syrup. So if government permit, say next season gave complete freedom to us. We'll go back to our preference will be B and juice.

items.statement: C-molasses ethanol price increased 6.78% per litre; B-heavy and syrup prices not increased by government
items.quote: Now one has to look into only one thing because C, molasses, ethanol, they have increased the rate substantially. Whereas in B we have to look into the, after considering the cane cost and everything, whether it is beneficial to go for the syrup or do-little bit of C and B because C prices have increased by 6.78% per litre and syrup and B prices have not been increased by the government.

items.statement: Narkatiaganj expansion to reduce steam consumption from 44.7% to 34.8%, saving 4.5% bagasse
items.quote: By doing this we are going to crush more, we are going to get high recovery and our steam consumption, which is around 44.7%, it will come down to 34.8%.

items.statement: Cane variety 0238 red rot infestation caused lower recovery; replacement with CO0118 & CO9301 underway to keep variety share 30-40%
items.quote: Yes, basic reason for the low recovery was the infestation of the 238 with the red rot. So, we have a robust planning to replace this variety with the promising varieties like CO0118 & CO9301 and we have increased significantly in our units. Ideally any one particular variety should not be more than 40% and it should be in between 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Reducing debt to lower finance costs and increase financial flexibility for value-creating investments
items.quote: by reducing our debt, we are giving ourselves more financial MAGADH SUGAR SR ENERGY LTD Magadh Sugar & Energy Limited May 15, 2024 flexibility, with which we will be having lower finance costs, which gives us on the other hand to invest more into projects that create values

items.statement: Total advances growth target of 17-20% for next 2-3 years with deposit growth higher than advances growth
items.quote: For the bank, we are looking at for the next 2 to 3 years, roughly around 17% to 18% to 20% growth. And we will definitely like to look at deposit growth higher than the advances growth.

items.statement: Micro credit (EEB) growth target of 14-15% for FY25
items.quote: Within that, the EEB book, we are looking at around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Normalized credit cost expected at 2.5-2.6% for EEB book and 1.8-2% for total portfolio
items.quote: We expect normalized 2.5% for the EEB book. Bu t at the total portfolio level, it will be between 1.8% to 2

items.statement: Technical write-off of INR 3,852 crores in Q4 FY24, largely in micro banking portfolio from COVID period
items.quote: During the quarter 4, the bank has done a technical write-off amounting to INR3,852 crores, which is largely in the micro banking portfolio, which is the EEB portfolio and which meets this criteria pertaining to the COVID period and which has had a long vintage and meets the bank's policies in this particular regard.

items.statement: CGFMU portion of technical write-off was INR 3,053 crores, remaining INR 800 crores
items.quote: If we look at the total technical write -off that was done duri ng the quarter of INR3,852 crores. The CGFMU portfolio within that was INR3,053 crores and remaining was about INR800 crores

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 3.8% from 7% in Q3 FY24, net NPA reduced to 1.1% from 2.2%
items.quote: With the actions that have been done and the result of that we have seen that the gross NPA ratio improved at 3.8% as of the end of the quarter, as compared to 7% in Q3 FY 2024. And the net NPA levels also reduced substantially at 1.1% as of the end of the quarter, compared to 2.2% as of the end of December 2023.

items.statement: EEB SMA 0 reduced from INR 805 crores (1.4%) to INR 380 crores (0.6%), SMA 1 from INR 570 crores (1%) to INR 400 crores (0.6%), SMA 2 from INR 533 crores (0.9%) to INR 480 crores (0.8%)
items.quote: Overall, if we add up across these three buckets, the reduction has been quite substantial going down from around INR1,900 crores to roughly around INR1,260 crores.

items.statement: Gross slippages reduced to INR 1,017 crores in Q4 from INR 1,394 crores in Q3, EEB slippages down to INR 632 crores from INR 993 crores
items.quote: The gross slippages during the qua rter 4 was INR1,017 crores, which was substantially down from the INR1,394 crores that we saw in the Q3 2024. Slippages in the EEB book also significantly came down to INR632 crores as compared to INR993 crores in the previous quarter

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 99% excluding NPA portfolio
items.quote: The bank's overall collection efficiency, excluding the NPA portfolio, was very stable at 99% quarter ended March 2024.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio at 71.8% as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: The provision coverage ratio, also known as PCR, as of 31st March 2024, stood at 71.8%, so at a healthy level of coverage that we have got for our NPA portfolio.

items.statement: NIM improved to 7.6% in Q4 FY24 from 7.2% in Q3 FY24, full year NIM at 7.3% up 10 bps YoY
items.quote: The net interest margin improved to 7.6% in Q4 2024 compared to 7.2% in Q3 FY 2024. This is aided by the good improvement we have seen in reduction in slippage rates our NPA levels as well as the business focus in terms of improving our margins.

items.statement: NIM may face contained reduction as secured portfolio mix increases
items.quote: And as that portfolio increases, there is going to be some impact of reduction in the NIM in a contained manner.

items.statement: EEB disbursed INR 65,000 crores in FY24 with only INR 160 crores in NPA (0.11%)
items.quote: We have adapted the EEB book now this financial year '23, '24 we disbursed INR65,000 crores. And out of that, only INR160 crores is in NPA. So that is the one part.

items.statement: Opened 289 branches in FY24 (53 in Q4), added nearly 2,000 employees
items.quote: In the last quarter, we have opened 53 branches. In total, we have added 289 branches.

items.statement: Core banking migration completed, investing in digital lending platforms and surround systems
items.quote: We have just about completed our core banking migration. We have got state-of-the-art technology system. We have also upgraded some of the surround system. We are working aggressively on the digital lending platforms and digital sourcing.

items.statement: Total deposits grew 25% YoY to INR 135,202 crores, retail deposits up 22% YoY, CASA at 37.1% of total deposits
items.quote: As at 31 March 2024, the total deposits stood at INR135,202 crores as against INR108,069 crores in the previous financial year, which represents a growth of 25% and deposits grew on a quarter-on-quarter basis, 15%.

items.statement: CASA plus retail term deposits constitute 69% of total deposits, West Bengal deposit share reduced from 43% to 40% YoY
items.quote: CASA plus retail term deposits constitute 69% of the total deposits. The CASA deposits within this at the end of the year stood at INR50,151 crores and constituted 37.1% of the total deposits.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 18.3% with Tier 1 at 17.2%, liquidity coverage ratio at 172%
items.quote: Capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.3%, with Tier 1 capital of 17.2% with balance sheet remaining sufficiently capitalized.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 1.50 per equity share of INR 10 for FY24, same as previous year
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR1.50 per equity share of INR10 for the year ended March 31, 2024, which is at the same level as the previous year.

items.statement: MD & CEO Chandra Shekhar Ghosh to retire on July 9, 2024, search firm appointed for succession
items.quote: On April 5, 2024 I announced my decision to retire as MD & CEO of the Bank on completion of my current tenure on July 9, 2024. The Board in accordance with the Business Continuity Plan and the Succession Plan of the Bank has appointed a search firm to assist in identifying potential candidates to take on the role after which we will approach RBI for its approval.

items.statement: New senior leadership appointments: Rajinder Babbar (CBO), Rajeev Mantri (CFO), heads for Wholesale Banking and Housing & Retail Business
items.quote: Our new Executive Directors Rajinder Babbar who is also our Chief Business Officer joined us in March 2024. Ratan Kesh who is our Chief Operations Officer has been with us for over a year. Rajeev Mantri our Chief Financial Officer also joined us during the quarter. We also have appointed Heads for our Wholesale Banking and Housing & Retail Business.

items.statement: CGFMU audit at advanced stage, management confident of positive outcome, resolution expected in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We believe that we should be able to get a resolution in the next -- which is this particular quarter, which is quarter 1. Will it have any bearing? As of now, as I said, that management and all of us are extremely confident.

items.statement: EEB portfolio constitutes 50% of advances, housing 24%, commercial banking 22%, retail 4% as of March 2024
items.quote: EEB, also known as emerging entrepreneur business, it comprises about 50% of the advances. Housing is 24%, commercial banking at 22% and retail at 4%, respectively, as at 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Slippages primarily from Punjab, Manipur, Maharashtra, Gujarat; trajectory expected to remain similar
items.quote: we have got the slippages primarily coming in from states of Pu njab. And also some of that is being carried forward from Manipur. And apart from that, Maharashtra, Gujarat was two states where in terms of the other states where we are present, the numbers are slightly higher

items.statement: ARC recovery income of INR 60-80 crores expected per quarter including provision releases
items.quote: Jai, around INR60 crores to INR80 crores of income from the ARC recovery we could expect every quarter.

items.statement: Target 700 restaurants by FY27
items.quote: Our guidance for FY '24 for restaurants was 450. We've beaten that guidance. We have 455 as of March 31, and our outlook for FY '27 continues to remain the same. We are targeting to open 700 restaurants.

items.statement: Gross margin target 69% over next 3 years from 67% base
items.quote: For gross profit, we had given a guidance of 67%. We've achieved that for the full year. For FY '24, our gross profit is 67%. And over the next 3 years, we want to take this up by 2 percentage points to 69% approximately.

items.statement: India FY24 EBITDA 9.7%, doubled from prior year
items.quote: If you look at it from the perspective of EBITDA, our EBITDA for the full year was closer to 10%, 9.7%, to be pre cise for the year

items.statement: India FY24 gross margin 67%, Q4 67.7% with small one-off
items.quote: For the full year, now we reported 67% gross margins. Quarter 4 was marginally higher at 67.7%. It had a one-off, but we should be able to improve for the coming years.

items.statement: Indonesia gross margin dropped due to value strategy and delivery focus
items.quote: Our focus, again, like in India, is going to be value strategy, drive more traffic, focus on delivery, and that is also one of the reasons why we've seen a drop in gross margins as far as Indonesia is concerned.

items.statement: India positive SSSG 2.9% FY24 driven by traffic growth every quarter
items.quote: In this environment, I think our work in India at least continued to deliver positive same-store sales, every single quarter. Every single quarter, we delivered positive sales, and we ended up being 2.9% positive.

items.statement: India traffic positive all year and into current year, no dent seen since April
items.quote: We continue to -- on top of building new restaurants in existing markets, in many cases, we have continued to drive positive traffic into our restaurant. More people coming to our restaurant. More people coming through our delivery system, right? That we haven't seen a dent since we started into April, May and going into June next month.

items.statement: Indonesia Q1 up 10%, Q2 up 13%, Q3 hit by geopolitical crisis, Q4 bounced back 11% ADS growth
