items.quote: We started the year on a great note. The first 2 quarters, we delivered double-digit growth. In quarter 1, we were 10% higher. Quarter 2, we were 13% higher. But the third quarter actually has been quite challenging for us. Even in the month of October, as Sumit and Raj was mentioning, we were 17% higher in sales compared to same period last year, which is unfortunately, when the entire industry w

items.statement: India net restaurant growth 64 in FY24 (75 opened, 11 closed)
items.quote: We've built 75 restaurants last year with 11 closures. That's about 64 NRG, net resta urant growth

items.statement: Indonesia closed 26 non-performing BK restaurants, ADS improved from 18.5M to 19.3M IDR
items.quote: During the year, as Raj was also mentioning, we took some calls and closed some of the underperforming stores and as a result of which, our ADS also improved further by another 0.8 million. So the average has gone up from 18.5 million to 19.3 million.

items.statement: India growth funded by internal accruals and balance sheet cash, open to short-term debt if needed
items.quote: As far as India is concerned, we will continue to grow using the cash that we have on balance sheet plus internal accruals. As we've said in the past as well, that if there is a need to raise some short-term debt to fund any part of the growth, then we would be open to do that.

items.statement: Indonesia pausing new store openings for both BK and Popeyes in current financial year to focus on stabilization
items.quote: At the moment, as we've been saying that we are focused as far as Indonesia is concerned is goi ng to be really stabilizing the entire portfolio of -- both the portfolio as far as business is concerned. So the capital allocation on both the brands is going to be literally close to nothing. We are not going to put any capital allocation on expansion at least in the current financial year as far as

items.statement: India digital experience rolled out to ~100 stores, table service at ~250 stores
items.quote: As of today, we have almost 100 stores that offer 100% digital experience. So you can order on the kiosk or on the app or on the table, and your food will get served on the table. And we're expanding this as we speak, the table service is available at across almost 250 stores, which are all our dine-in locations now offer table service to our customers.

items.statement: India took price hikes on delivery offerings in line with industry while maintaining value
items.quote: Number two, we have recently taken some price hikes on our delivery offerings. These are keeping in line with where the industry is. And we are making sure that there are still value for money for our consumers.

items.statement: India launched India-specific nuggets, wraps, puffs, premium menu focus, Whopper recipe change, BK Cafe at 351 stores
items.quote: We launched the chicken snacking favorite nuggets. Now it's a crunchy nugget. It's got a twist on a typical nugget that we've seen in QSR. We also relaunched the BK chicken burger with 50% more chicken. So it's not just about new products, we go back and improve our existing products also based on customer feedback, right? And that's now available at 50% more chicken at the same price, so even bet

items.statement: India delivery traffic highest in industry, optimizing mix and entry pricing for profitability
items.quote: First of all, it drives the highest number of traffic numbers in delivery in India, right? We already shared that with you every single meeting that we get on the call. we are optimizing that, right? We are trying to make sure that, that is traffic that we are driving with profitable kind of margin numbers. So that optimization through product mix through entry-level pricing and through offers tha

items.statement: India non-current and other financial liabilities up ~INR100 cr due to late-year store openings, current in nature
items.quote: these are largely on account of the stores that we opened during -- towards the later part of the year. So those would kind of get pa id as they do, due to curren t in nature there. But that's something which is more like -- as you know, we are negative for the capital business. So we will always have business and expansion -related negative working capital cycles that we will continue to have

items.statement: India company EBITDA loss reduced from INR95 cr to INR55 cr, targeting breakeven in current financial year
items.quote: Last year, we were -- we had a loss of almost around INR95 crores. We brought that down by INR40 crores to INR54 crores or INR55 crores. Our endeavor is to make sure that if this improvement of journey that we are taking, we do believe that we should be able to achieve what we plan to achieve this year, in the coming financial year or the ongoing financial year.

items.statement: Prashant Desai stepping down as Head of Strategy and IR, Gaurav Ajjan appointed as replacement
items.quote: I have been moving on from Burger King or RBA, and in my absence, Gaurav Ajjan has now joined as the new Head of Strategy and Investor Relations.

items.statement: Indonesia geopolitical headwinds caused anti-US brand sentiment, dine-in dropped >30%, recovery expected over couple of quarters
items.quote: But what does that do is, it gave us a lot of headwinds in both Q3 and Q4. And instead of kind of gaining momentum, which we had reached ADS level in October as per plan to go over 20 million IDRs per restaurant, 20 million IDR per restaurant per day. But that got reverse d in the Q3 and Q4. It's not coming back, and we feel good about it moving forward. It might take another couple of quarters to

items.statement: India ADS fell from INR126k in Sep to INR105k in Mar due to seasonality, expected to improve in Q1
items.quote: There is seasonality. Quarter 4 Jan, Feb, March typically does have low seasonality. And we do see improvements coming through in April, May, June as seasonality kicks in, school holidays, malls -- mall events, all of that

items.statement: Indonesia ADS reached 19.5M IDR in Oct before geopolitical hit, Q4 bounced back to 11% YoY growth
items.quote: But right up to October, we got to an A DS of 19.5 million. And then with further investments that we had planned on chicken and all, we felt positive that we would have got to what we had been talking about to cash breakeven towards quarter 3, quarter 4 in Indonesia, but external factors really kind of pulled us back. We are back on track as far as Indonesia is concerned and we've started at leas

items.statement: FY25 store expansion target of 275-300 stores across core brands in India
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at a similar number, which is 275 to 300 stores.

items.statement: Opened 256 new stores in FY24 including 47 in Q4; total store count 1,782 as of March 31 including 283 KFC Thailand stores
items.quote: We opened 256 new stores, including 47 in the fourth quarter. As of March 31, our total store count has reached 1,782, including the 283 KFC stores we acquired in Thailand on January 18, 2024.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 70.3% for FY24 (+30 bps YoY); Q4 gross margin lower due to Thailand consolidation and Nigeria currency impact
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business including Thailand was 70.3% for the full year versus 70% for the previous year an improvement of 30 basis points on a full year basis.

items.statement: KFC India Q4 gross margin 69.9% (+50 bps QoQ); brand contribution 19%
items.quote: Gross margins for KFC during the quarter was 69.9% thereby reflecting an improvement of 50 basis points over the previous quarter. Brand contribution remained healthy at 19% for the current quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 gross margin 77.3% (+150 bps QoQ); brand contribution 4.4% (lower QoQ due to ADS deleverage)
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter came in at 77.3% versus 75.8% in the previous quarter. Brand contribution was INR 7 Crore for the quarter with margins at 4.4% which was slightly lower on a quarter-on-quarter basis mainly due to the ADS deleverage impact.

items.statement: Costa Coffee Q4 gross margin 76.7%; brand contribution 17.9% (+300 bps QoQ)
items.quote: The gross margin was 76.7% in quarter 4. Brand contribution in quarter 4 stood at 17.9% an improvement of 3% versus the previous quarter.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment weak throughout FY24 due to weak disposable income, tight liquidity, geopolitical issues; expect improvement post elections and West Asia stability
items.quote: Consumer sentiment continues to be weak throughout the year , w eak disposable income, tight liquidity position, local consumption, geopolitical situation were the major drivers for the weak consumer demand

items.statement: Seeing some green shoots on ground; Q1 seasonally better than Q4
items.quote: we are seeing some green shoots and we hope that they are kind of lived long.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement sustainable due to supply chain negotiations, menu optimization, and promotion refinement; not from dramatic cost reductions
items.quote: It is a sustainable trend, Devanshu. Since the hyperinflation we experienced, things have stabilized, they have not come down dramatically. However, with our negotiations, we are seeing good results. We've also done menu optimization.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Fun Flavour value pizza damaged premium positioning; KFC value layers (rolls/wraps) successful as side dishes; Pizza Hut recovery initiatives underway
items.quote: During the period of hyperinflation, we tried to experiment with Fun Flavour pizza, which lowered the overall pricing structure. In hindsight we can call ourselves wiser, but this move impacted the brand positioning.

items.statement: Food courts strategy targets travel, tourism, shopping channels; partnership with PVR INOX for mall food courts; existing food courts at highways, railways, airports
items.quote: DIL has entered into a strategic partnership with PVR INOX to develop and operate the business of food courts at shopping malls across the country to co-promote movies and food.

items.statement: Costa Coffee-PVR JV performing well with ~80 outlets; expanding collaboration
items.quote: We have already opened close to 80 Costa Coffees in the PVR, and it will be expanded and adding great value to our business.

items.statement: Entire QSR market facing negative SSSG including burger segment leader; competitive intensity exists but partly inflated by cloud kitchen multiplicities
items.quote: We've seen the market leader in the burger segment reporting a negative SSSG , as well as our peer competitor s were in similar situation . We are in similar situation and the entire market is facing these challenges

items.statement: Nigerian Naira depreciated ~200% vs USD in FY24; INR 236 crore forex loss on USD liabilities (INR 90 crore exceptional, INR 147 crore OCI); full impairment of INR 116 crore investment in Nigeria
items.quote: During the financial year Nigerian Naira has got depreciated by almost 200% versus the USD. As a result of this, the Nigeria business has recorded an impact of INR 236 crore forex loss on account of USD denominated liabilities.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR 910 crore (INR 470 crore international, INR 365 crore India); gearing below 1x; debt/EBITDA 1.28x
items.quote: The total debt in the books at a consolidated level is INR 910 crore as of March 31, 2024. Out of this, INR 835 crore in the bank debt consisting of INR 470 crore at international and INR 365 crore in India.

items.statement: Senior management exits (Rajat moving South for family); no disruption expected as strategy unchanged and Virag Joshi continues leadership
items.quote: Rajat has been with the Company for almost 13-14 years, and he wanted to move to South to be closer to his family. He gave his best to the Company in any case. So we don't expect any disruption or significant changes because the strategy remains the same.

items.statement: Nigeria business fully impaired; Thailand geopolitical impact on few southern stores; Pizza Hut brand recovery uncertain
items.quote: In view of the above, DIL has also taken a full impairment of its investment of INR 116 crore in Nigerian business through its subsidiary, RV Enterprises Pte. Ltd.

items.statement: Thailand KFC purchase price allocation provisional under IND AS for up to 12 months from acquisition date
items.quote: As per the IND AS, DIL has a measurement period of up to 12 months from the date of acquisition and hence to that extent, this is subject to final adjustments.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth >60% YoY and operational EBITDA margin improvement >100 bps
items.value: >60% revenue growth; >100 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: For the year 2025, we expect to clock a similar rate of growth in revenue greater than 60% and an improvement in operational EBITDA margin of more than 100 basis points.

items.statement: FY25 guidance excludes OSAT/PCB revenue; those will start in 1-2 years and reach full form in 3-5 years
items.quote: This year guidance OF 60% up is just on EMS and not based on activities in the OSAT and PCB. OSAT and PCB will take one to two years’ time to start the initial capac ity utilization and you can see them in full form maybe in a span of about three to five

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration of $1 billion revenue by FY28 (75% EMS, 25% other) remains on track
items.quote: We are very confident that we will be achieving this number in year 2028 because the tailwinds are very good and then entire globe is looking at India.

items.statement: Order book rose to Rs 41,152 million at end of Q4 FY24 from Rs 37,890 million at end of Q3 FY24; average monthly inflow increased to Rs 3,212 million in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The order book surged from Rs.37,890 million at the end of Q3 FY'2024 to 41,152 million at the en d of Q4 FY'24. The average order inflow per month increased from 2,788 million per month in Q3 FY'24 to 3,212 million during Q4 FY'2023

items.statement: Smart meter orders (concluded April-May) not yet in Q4 order book; will add next quarter; CDAC server order already included
items.quote: So these smart meter orders are actually not part of your 4,152 crores. Smart meter orders have been concluded, especially the large orders been concluded in April and May. So in the next quarter we will add these orders and show you.

items.statement: Strong demand across all verticals, notably Industrial & EV, Aerospace/Outer Space/Strategic Electronics, Railways
items.quote: Our growth was led by strong demand across all the verticals, more notably. Industrial and EV Aerospace, Outer Space and Strategic Electronics and Railways vertical.

items.statement: 100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY25 driven by operating leverage, not gross margin expansion; further operating leverage possible
items.quote: So the numbers are clear. Obviously, the gross margins have come a tad down. So we have done operating leverage. And like I said, we still have fair amount of ope rating leverage possibility because we still have middle line which can be leveraged better

items.statement: FY25 capex funded from internal accruals; expect ~Rs 200-250 crore from operating cash flow (EBITDA >50-60% growth + 100 bps margin) at 7-8x asset turnover
items.quote: So it will give about 200 to 250 crores of money which can be invested into CAPEX and that will be sufficient taking a seven or eight times asset turnover eventually.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of Rs 1,400 crore earmarked only for OSAT and HDI PCB projects; no deleveraging
items.quote: We raise the funds for specific two p rojects, one is OSAT and the other is high density interconnection PCB and they will be used for only that

items.statement: Chamarajanagar facility becoming truly integrated; Pune facility now operational; preliminary construction started in Telangana; new regions in India and overseas planned
items.quote: continue to make serious progress in our expansion and con tinuously adding newer lines across various facilities, especially Chamarajanagar which is in line to become truly integrated facility. Our Pune facility which was acquired recently also now is opera tional. Also, we have plan to expand the new regions in India and outside India as well

items.statement: Bare board (PCB) manufacturing approval received; supplier orders being finalised, recruitment and construction starting; expect shipments in FY25
items.quote: We have got approval for that already. We are in the advanc ed stages of finalizing the orders with all the suppliers, recruitments are going on, and construction is also just starting. Indrajit Agarwal: So we can see some shipments this year

items.statement: OSAT/PCB government approvals expected soon after model code of conduct ends; 2-3 month delay absorbed in plan; preparatory work underway
items.quote: We are in the final stages of obtaining government approvals for ou r new investments and expected the approval soon after the model code of conduct is concluded. We feel even there is a delay of 2-3 months, we will be well within the expected plan a nd we will catch up with the timelines for these projects implementation through preparatory steps, wh ich are already underway

items.statement: EMS exports currently ~10% of revenue; expected to rise modestly in aerospace/defence/railways; OSAT/PCB will be export-driven and significantly increase export share in 4 years
items.quote: However, when we come to something like semiconductor assembly that is OSAT or PC board, HDI PC board, they are all export-driven and so another four years’ time you will see significant increase in the exports th rough the new businesses

items.statement: Portfolio rebalancing toward 50:50 high-volume (auto/industrial/EV) vs high-margin (aerospace/defence/medical/railways) by FY25
items.quote: this year, we have seen the orders of the financial year FY'25 and we find that the portfolio balance is coming back to our original expectation, which is like 60:40 and may be eventually it will be 5 0:50, so 50 of high volume and 50 of high profit making the products will be there in our portfolio

items.statement: OSAT/PCB subsidies pending government approval; model code of conduct delay of 2-3 months; approvals expected soon after elections
items.quote: We are in the final stages of obtaining government approvals for ou r new investments and expected the approval soon after the model code of conduct is concluded

items.statement: OSAT partner Globetronics facing issues (Apple contract cancelled); Kaynes says agreements intact, backup partners lined up, no impact on timeline
items.quote: The issue is once we get the government approval, we have severa l partnerships lined up and there are several backup also available. One of these can be consumm ated till we get the government's approval for the subsidy scheme, correct. So there is nothing cancelled, etc., We are in touch with

items.statement: Medical segment revenue expected to reach triple digits (Rs 100+ crore) in FY25 after long qualification cycles
items.quote: So this year you will see at least medical segment will go to triple digits, at least 100 crores plus will be there in the medical sector in FY'525 for sure.

items.statement: Management targets fee-based income to grow to 75% of EBITDA from current 55% over coming years
items.quote: I see that to continue or even grow slightly every year to become a 75% fee based earning business.

items.statement: AUM grew from Rs 1,665 cr to Rs 2,500 cr in FY24 driven by global arbitrage fund, AIFs and SATCO PMS acquisition
items.quote: The highlight of the results is the assets under management, which have increased from Rs. 1,665 crores in March'23 to approximately Rs. 2,500 crores in March'24 primarily due to our remarkable performance in our global arbitrage fund housed in Mauritius, our alternative investment funds and the acquisition of a renowned PMS called SATCO Growth & Momentum portfolio during this year.

items.statement: Global arbitrage fund AUM grew ~80% from $455M to ~$800M in FY24; similar trajectory expected in FY25 absent geopolitical issues
items.quote: So from a trajectory point of view, we have grown from 455 to approximately 800 this year. That in terms of percentages, I think we've grown almost 80%, and the way the inflows are coming in this year, I think the same trajectory should continue as long as there are no new geopolitical issues happening

items.statement: Received SEBI approval to operate as Investment Manager for AIFs in India, transforming Abans Holdings into an operational entity
items.quote: We have received approval from SEBI to operate as an Investment Manager for our alternative investment funds in India. This approval enables us to transform from a holding entity at Abans Holdings Limited level into an Operational Entity.

items.statement: Applied for US commodity pool operator license to access US investors for global arbitrage fund; approvals awaited
items.quote: We are in the process of getting the regulatory approval both from a commodity pool operator perspective and from a regulation perspective. So once we have those, I mean regulatory approvals in place, we shall be able to access U.S. investor funds.

items.statement: Applied for mutual fund license to launch own commodity ETF; approval timeline uncertain
items.quote: As soon as the approvals are in place, we will initiate that business. We've already made the applications to the relevant authorities both for sponsorship as well as the license, but they're still awaited and there is no, a deal given by them as to when they will accord us the approval.

items.statement: Focus shifting to fee-based income (subscription, performance, advisory fees) targeting 75% of EBITDA vs 55% currently
items.quote: Finally, the focus is always going to be on fee based income, either through inorganic growth, through strategic alliances, keep focusing on fee based income and keep building the lending book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~11% in FY24, up 3.5% YoY; agency business EBIT grew from Rs 21 cr to Rs 59 cr YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins are at approximately 11% with the growth 3.5% increase year-on -year.

items.statement: Borrowings at Rs 929 cr; 70% asset-backed, 30% non-asset-backed; comfortable on interest coverage and debt-equity; no equity dilution planned in next 12 months
items.quote: So, the Gearing ratio of the company is still low and also out of the borrowings, at least 70% of them are asset backed borrowing, so 30% are non-asset backed borrowing, so yes, we are in a comfortable place both in terms of interest coverage ratio as well as debt equity ratio, but no, there are no plans to dilute equity in the next 12 months because the group is in a comfortable place for growth.

items.statement: Employee cost rose from Rs 14 cr to Rs 40 cr due to global hiring and ESOPs/performance incentives; future increases only inflation-linked
items.quote: Absolutely, so the employee costs have gone up because of new hiring in different parts of the world, one, and two is due to the ESOPs and the performance incentives that have been given to the people who have been working in this company for a longer duration, so that's why the employee cost looks on the higher side and it shall, if not increase in this way and this will increase on an inflation

items.statement: Strategic tie-up with SMC Global Taurus Wealth for distribution; Abans manufactures products, partners provide sales reach
items.quote: So we have such strategic tie-up in nature whereby we understand the product and they become our sales team and they approach the audience that they already have available or new audience who is looking for wealth options and that's what this tie-up actually means.

items.statement: Remittance business in UK subsidiary (FCA regulated) generated Rs 5 cr income in FY24; plans to replicate license in other countries
items.quote: if you've seen that about 5 crores of income this year has come from that entity and that is new income that we found in the group, and I think that can continue if we keep looking at different industries across the globe and try to understand the regulatory requirements of different regions, so that we can replicate this license in different countries.

items.statement: Lending focus remains on agri-commodities; gold lending not planned for current year pending RBI approvals
items.quote: Not as of now. Our understanding of Agri-commodities lending has grown over the years. For gold lending, we need certain approvals -- in place for RBI, so we are not looking at it in the current year, but if we do eventually we can look at gold lending in the future but not for the current year only.

items.statement: Global arbitrage fund growth dependent on no new geopolitical issues; US fund registration approvals uncertain
items.quote: I think the same trajectory should continue as long as there are no new geopolitical issues happening

items.statement: Standalone loss of Rs 6.72 cr due to ESOPs for 16 long-tenure employees; expected to turn positive in FY25 from AIF management fees and cost reimbursements
items.quote: However, in the current year Abans Holding has received the license both from SEBI and from IFSC to act as an investment manager for both AIFs, which has assets under management of approximately Rs. 300 crores. So, during the current year, you will see incomes booked from the performance of AIF and their redemptions, so they will, the P&L will turn positive

items.statement: FY2024 will be an elevated and peak level of capex; clear moderation expected in FY2025
items.quote: we have always mentioned that FY2024 will be an elevated and peak level of capex and I expect to see clear moderation going into FY2025.

items.statement: Wireless capex to moderate meaningfully in FY2025; transport, enterprise, data center, and homes capex to continue
items.quote: wireless capex which accounts by the way for a large part of the capex so to that extent we do see moderation going ahead into next year.

items.statement: B2B capex lumpy due to fiber purchase, data center build, and submarine cable milestones; otherwise steady state
items.quote: our B2B business had a bit of one -off this quarter which is primarily related to fiberi zation so we bought some fibers and some spends o n the data center business

items.statement: Rolled out ~43,100 network sites and ~55,982 km of fiber in FY2024; 5G available across the country
items.quote: We rolled out about 43,100 network sites and 55,982 kilometers of fiber.

items.statement: Plan to rollout over 25,000 sites in next couple of quarters, lower than last year, focused on rural coverage gaps
items.quote: We expect to rollout over 25000 sites lower than last year in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Smartphone shipments grew in FY2024 after price shock absorption; 70-80% of shipments now 5G-enabled
items.quote: 70% to 80% of the shipments that are happening on smart phones are now 5G enabled so to that extent as people upgrade their devices they will naturally move to 5G.

items.statement: Industry customer additions in low single digits annually over last 12 quarters; Q4 was an aberration
items.quote: You are seei ng that customer addition in the low single digits at the aggregate level

items.statement: India RoCE 9.5% in Q4, extremely low; tariff repair needed to improve returns
items.quote: our RoCE for India is 9.5%, which is extremely low for a business that is so essential to the digital spine of this country.

items.statement: Tariffs at absurdly low level globally; substantial repair needed; ARPU at Rs.209, right level ~Rs.300 still among lowest worldwide
items.quote: tariffs are at an absurdly low level relative to any other part of the world so tariff repair is solely needed for return ratios to improve.

items.statement: Two rounds of tariff repair in last couple of years led to modest SIM consolidation; digital mobility essential so customers will adjust spends
items.quote: Every time there is some increase there is some SIM consolidation that happens I would say at best it is modest.

items.statement: 5G base ~72 million as of March 2024, growing 2-2.5 million monthly; free 5G doubles data usage vs 4G
items.quote: We have roughly 72 million 5G customers as of March 2024. This is growing currently at the rate of 2 to 2.5 million every month.

items.statement: Broadband net adds moderated to 3.6 lakh in Q4; added 2.2 million fiber home passes, expanded to 23 cities; 43% of adds on converge plans
items.quote: However, there was some moderation in net additions to 3.6 lakhs in the quarter.

items.statement: FWA live in 25 cities on SA; scaling in 8 weeks; will complement FTTH in weak fiber areas using 3.5 GHz spectrum
items.quote: We are live in 25 cities and currently streamlining the customer journeys. We will be at scale in the coming eight weeks.

items.statement: DTH customer base grew 9,000 in Q4 and 200,000+ in FY2024, only operator to grow; moderate price hike due to broadcaster increases
items.quote: On an annual basis after two years of decline we grew our customer base by over 200,000 net adds the only operator in the industry to grow customers during this year.

items.statement: Postpaid net adds steady at 0.8 million; over 80 million credit-scored customers identified for postpaid upgrade
items.quote: Postpaid net adds was steady at 0.8 million.

items.statement: Mobile churn reduced from 2.9% in Q3 to 2.4% in Q4 via structural grid-based experience program
items.quote: mobile churn reducing from 2.9% in Q3 to 2.4% in Q4.

items.statement: Welcome VI fundraising; India well served with three strong private operators; market brutally competitive, execution key
items.quote: I am glad to see that VI has raised money a nd I really wish them well. I think India will be we ll served if it has three good private operators working there

items.statement: Rights issue guidance three years; six to eight months left; will provide revised guidance in 3-5 months based on free cash flow outlook
items.quote: the guidance was three years and we have about six to eight months left to that guidance. Our understanding is more a guidance and we will have to chew on what is the outlook for the free cash flows so maybe by the next three to five months we will come out with a more formal either a revised guidance or whatever commentary that we have to provide for the rest of the calls.

items.statement: Paid Rs.16,350 Crores debt in FY2024; India net debt/EBITDA at 2.86x; expect further reduction
items.quote: We paid 16,350 Crores of debt. India net debt to EBITDA is n ow at a comfortable level of 2.86. We expect further debt reduction going forward

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom repaid Rs.1,500 Crores debt in Q4; net debt/EBITDA 2.14x at year-end
items.quote: I am happy to report we have repaid about Rs. 1500 Crores of debt in Q4 and ended the year with a net debt to EBITDA of about 2.14.

items.statement: Dividend increased significantly (effectively 1.5 to 4 post-split); Hexacom dividend policy after debt repayment and spectrum commitments
items.quote: the dividend has increased a lot whilst on the face of it, it may seem that it has moved from Rs. 3 to Rs. 4 last year to this year you must remember that there has been a stock split so effectively it has moved from 1.5 to 4 so there has been a significant improvement in dividend.

items.statement: All 20,000 employees spent a day with frontline staff in March; ongoing ritual to improve customer experience
items.quote: We think of Airtel as having only two types of people those who serve customers and those who serve those who serve customers. It is with this in mind that we had every one of our 20,000 people get out into the market and spend a whole day with our frontline people in March.

items.statement: Airtel Business domestic revenue growing 18-20% annually; global wholesale business under pressure from OTT cutbacks
items.quote: the domestic business is on a strong footing and continues to grow at 18 to 20%.

items.statement: Payments Bank MTU 67 million; annualized revenue run rate >Rs.2,100 Crores; deposits ~Rs.2,800 Crores, up ~50% YoY
items.quote: Monthly transacting users under 67 million. The annualized revenue run rate is now over 2100 Crores; deposits remain robust at around 2,800 Crores growing nearly 50% year-on-year.

items.statement: Digital businesses annualized run rate ~Rs.1,900 Crores; 50% revenue growth in FY2024; Airtel Finance disbursed Rs.2,000 Crores loans to 4 lakh customers
items.quote: saw 50% revenue growth in the last fiscal . Airtel Finance is scaling up well and served four lakh custome rs across loan and car products in FY2024. We disbursed loans worth 2,000 Crores

items.statement: Expects domestic auto market volume growth of 6-8% in FY25 and aims to outgrow market through domestic, export and aftermarket growth
items.quote: We expect the market to grow, as you would have seen last year. We expect similarly this, current year as well as next year. If, of course, post the elections, we are hoping that everything goes well. We are hoping that the markets will rebound very strongly and we will be looking at a figure of around close to 6% to 8% growth in the market as far as the volumes are concerned.

items.statement: Targets to continue outgrowing domestic market growth rate of 6-8% in FY25
items.quote: And we have a fairly good position with all our customers and we expect that our growth should be better than that, primarily not only the improved sales coming from the domestic busine ss, but also with the focus that we have with regards to penetrating newer markets in the aftermarket and exports. So, we expect to still continue to outgrow that figure of 6% to 8

items.statement: Sees excellent pull in passenger vehicle and two-wheeler segments; commercial vehicle flattish but expected to pick up post-elections
items.quote: What is happening is we see excellent pull in both the passenger vehicle as well as the two-wheeler industry. And except for the cyclical changes that happens normally in the month of April we are seeing excellent scheduling coming in from most of our customers, especially for the passenger vehicles as well as the two-wheeler markets.

items.statement: Export markets badly affected by geopolitical issues; grew 7% vs <1% market growth in FY24
items.quote: And when we grow in our components 7%, it means we have outgrown the market by 7 times. it's really a huge outgrowth for the ki nd of markets that we are catering to because the export markets are very badly affected

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 421 bps to 23.4% in FY24; PAT margin expanded to 14.7%
items.quote: Our EBITDA expanded to INR7,114 million, witnessing a growth of 39.6% on a year-on-year basis. The EBITDA margin improved 421 basis points from 19.2% in FY '23 to 23.4% in FY '24.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 222 bps to 23.7%; PAT margin improved 203 bps to 15%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin expanded by 222 basis points to 23.7% for the quarter from 21.5% in Q4 FY '23. Further, profit after tax for the quarter was at INR1,206 million against INR926 million in Q4 FY '23, reporting a significant growth of 30.2% year-on-year. We reported a PAT margin at 15% for the quarter, which has improved by 203 basis points from 13% in Q4 FY '23.

items.statement: Pithampur plant capacities backed by awarded customer business; expects plant to get booked up soon
items.quote: All the capacities that have been put up is backed by forward-looking customer businesses that have been awarded already to us. So we expect that plant to get booked up very soon.

items.statement: INR70 crore capex for Coimbatore EV plant mostly to be spent in FY25
items.quote: The INR70 crores will be mostly spent in FY25, as I see.

items.statement: Invested close to INR80 crore in Pithampur plant
items.quote: We have put in almost close to, with regards to the overall business, we have put in almost close to INR80 crores of rupees in terms of building the new plant.

items.statement: Commenced manufacturing operations at Pithampur plant in March 2024; ramping up production
items.quote: I am really happy to share with you al l that during this quarter, we have commenced the manufacturing operations at our plant in Pithampur in Madhya Pradesh

items.statement: Building new EV-focused facility in Coimbatore for electric motors and controllers
items.quote: Further, the process of building a state-of-art manufacturing facility near to our existing facility in Coimbatore is also on track. This facility will be focused on growing our EV portfolio, including electric moto rs controllers, for passenger vehicles, two -wheelers, three-wheelers, as well as the commercial vehicles

items.statement: EV motor lines cover 250W to 30kW hub motors and 7kW to 300kW mid-drive motors catering to all vehicle segments
items.quote: we have p ut in lines which will make hub motors right from 250 watts right up to 30 kilowatts and mid-drive motor lines which can make right from 7 kilowatt right up to 300 kilowatts

items.statement: Content per vehicle increases with emission norm changes (ethanol, hydrogen); expects higher content growth vs Euro 6 transition
items.quote: But at the same time, but from a product perspective single prod uct, because of the technology that goes into it with regards to coating and other requirements, the content for the vehicle always goes up and we are expecting it to continue to grow up as we go along

items.statement: Developing solutions for E85 ethanol blending; requires different ring coatings and higher technology content
items.quote: The government is already working on E85. In other parts of the globe, in Brazil, people have blended 85%. And so we have, we already have solutions for that and we are already Shriram Pistons & working on, it requires different kind of coatings on our rings and others

items.statement: Aftermarket growth driven by brand pull (USHA, SPR brands) and 1,200+ touchpoints with daily field servicing
items.quote: Basically, there are two major brands within our portfolio. One is called the USHA brand and the second one is called the SPR brand. And both the brands in different segments of the markets are actually doing very, very well and they have been able to create a huge pull from the customers.

items.statement: EV motor controller supply for both existing and new OEM models; customers seeking alternate sources for volume growth
items.quote: Yes, for both, for existing as well as for the new models. New models have to as per the new requirements of the government and the new rules that have been put in, every sub-product has to be validated and tested and ARAI certified.

items.statement: Market share improved as company grew 14.5% vs 7% market growth in FY24; added new applications (marine, snowmobile)
items.quote: When you outgrow the market, especially when the market has grown by 7% and we have grown by 14.5%, it's but natural that we have actually improved our market share.

items.statement: Actively pursuing M&A; hopes to close a couple of deals soon; focus on auto segment agnostic to IC engines
items.quote: Well, we are looking at it like a hawk and I'm hoping that we will be able to close a couple of deals soon.

items.statement: Acquired majority stakes in SPR EMFI and SPR Takahata Precision India for EV and plastic injection moulded parts
items.quote: With the acquisitions of majorit y stakes in SPR EMFI and SPR Takahata Precision India , we are positioning ourselves to capitalise on the growing market for electric vehicles, EV mobility solutions, and plastic injection moulded parts

items.statement: Takahata annualized revenue ~INR270 crore; EMFI ~INR15-20 crore; expects vertical revenue growth from EMFI
items.quote: based on the last year's performance to be somewhere close to INR270 crores for Takahata, and I NR15 crores or INR20 odd crores for EMFI. But going forward, as I said, EMFI is just it is the volume of business that we are doing, and the kind of capacity that we are setting up is huge. The increase in revenue is going to be quite vertical

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR5 per share for FY24 plus INR5 interim dividend (post 1:1 bonus)
items.quote: I am really happy to share with you all that our esteemed Board has recommended a final dividend of INR5 per equity share for FY '24 in addition to the interim dividend of INR5 per equity share already paid. This is post the 1:1 bonus issue that was given in FY '24.

items.statement: Maintains robust credit profile with AA stable rating; generated INR4,742 million operating cash flow in FY24
items.quote: The company is generating positive cash from operations with tune of INR4,742 million during FY '24. We have been maintaining a robust credit profile with the credit rating of AA stable.

items.statement: Board approved BSE listing subject to approvals
items.quote: I am also delighted t o announce that our Board has recommended and approved the listing of the company's equity shares at the Bombay Stock Exchange, which is subject to necessary approvals and clearances

items.statement: Export market outlook remains challenging due to geopolitical issues (Ukraine war, Israel-Gaza); Europe and UK markets badly affected
items.quote: Next year, the current situation in the market still continues to be bad as far as the export market is concerned. So our focus is to see how we can still outgrow the market.

items.statement: Technology center in Ghaziabad developing in-house design capabilities for CNG, ethanol (up to 85%), hydrogen pistons
items.quote: This design center is presently working on forward-looking technologies for CNG requirements for ethanol blending right up to 85% and also hydrogen pistons. We have delivered some samples. We have already worked with our customers and we are working with them for further developing the same.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target INR450 crores with PAT margin around 25%
items.quote: My plan for the next year is that if we take our occupancy at 55%, which we have just closed at 37%, then our revenue will be around INR450 crores. And my target for the PAT will be around 25% because all our basic expenses are getting completed.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR600-650 crores with 85% occupancy on existing beds
items.quote: No, no. I have planned only 600. If I add 500 beds, then it will be around 650. Deepak Poddar: 600, 650. Manish Grover: So, I will take 35 occupancy for 500 beds. I will take 85 occupancy for old

items.statement: 3-year target of 3,000 beds and 5-year target above 4,000 beds
items.quote: In the next 3 years we will do 3,000 beds. In 5 years, we will be above 4,000 beds.

items.statement: Add 500 beds by March 31, 2025, including 100 for infertility and 300 for heart/liver
items.quote: Yes, by 31st March 2025, we will add 500 beds. The 1300 beds, there are 1270 beds now. We will add 500 new beds in that.

items.statement: Capex ~INR3-3.25 lakh per bed; 500 beds max INR15 crores; hospitals taken on rent, only interiors funded
items.quote: Sir, as I told you, the capex that we add for each bed, it will be around INR3 lakh per bed on average. Sometimes it will be INR4 lakh, sometimes it will be INR2 lakh. So, on average, we add one bed for INR3, INR3.25 lakh

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 29%, PAT margin 21%; medicine gross margin ~85%, net margin 22%
items.quote: The EBITDA during FY24 grew by 102% year-over-year basis to INR93, implying EBITDA margin of 29%. The FY24 PAT grew by 105% year-over-year basis to INR69 crores.

items.statement: Revenue FY24 INR324 crores (59% YoY); hospital services INR139 crores (122% YoY); products INR186 crores (32% YoY)
items.quote: FY24 results, revenue from the operation grew by 59% year-over-year basis to INR234 crores. Mainly driven by the hospital services, which grew by 1.22% year-over-year basis to INR139 crores, while production grew by 32% up to INR186 crores.

items.statement: Acquired 7 products from Gujarat company Arshar; sales to reflect from next month
items.quote: By chance, we found a company in the middle. We took their 7 products and made them. Already, their market is going on. From next month, their sale will reflect in our company.

items.statement: No direct peer in Ayurveda treatment model; others focus on wellness; 10% share of NABH centres (24 of 240)
items.quote: No, sir. We do not see anyone working like us. People are working on wellness. We are working on treatment. We are going to start the wellness sector now. We are also going to start wellness together. So there is no one now, sir.

items.statement: Overseas expansion: Nepal centre inaugurated, planning Vietnam, Dubai, Mauritius, Canada, UK; Ayurveda approved in 112 countries via MSME
items.quote: Yes, sir. Within two months, we have a plan to open a center in at least three countries. On the 15th, I have been inaugurated in Nepal. Harish Kumar Gupta: Very good. Manish Grover: And now we are talking about Vietnam. We are talking about Dubai in the Middle East. And we are planning clinics and hospitals

items.statement: Trade receivables increased from INR22 to INR42 crores due to 60% revenue growth; government billing cycle 3-6 months
items.quote: Sir, our trade receivables have increased, the reason is our revenue has increased from 60%. So our revenue has increased in proportion to 42-46 days. The reason behind this is the government Billing Receivable cycle is 3-6 months.

items.statement: Net cash position INR62 crores at FY24 end; ROE ex-cash 36%, ex-ROC 80%
items.quote: We attained the healthy balance sheet with net cash in equivalent of INR62 crores by the year-end of FY24 and the ROE on the ex-cash ROC is 36% and ex-ROC is 80% respectively.

items.statement: Appointed E&Y for management performance review FY25; migrating from SME to main board in FY25 (April 2025)
items.quote: And from SME, we will come to the main board in the financial year 2025 and for management assurance, we have started Big 4. And we have appointed E&Y for the management performance review for financial review 2024-25.

items.statement: Declared 15% dividend
items.quote: I think we did dividend yesterday. How much percent did you take 15% dividend...15% dividend has been announced.

items.statement: ESOP granted 130,000 shares to 738 employees (5-year vesting); 3 cars given, 21 more planned for Diwali; hired OTC head from Dr Ortho maker
items.quote: And for the well-being of doctors on 16th March 2024 we have done ESOP. We have divided 1,30,000 shares in ESOP for doctors and old staff. We have done ESOP for about 738 employees on 16th March whoever stays with us for 5 years, they will get ESOP.

items.statement: Phasing out franchisees: reduced from 70 to 50 in 6 months, target zero in 2-3 years; 55 of 70 clinics franchised, all hospitals company-owned
items.quote: We don't give a new franchisee. We have reduced 16 of our old franchisees in the last 6 months. Now we are running the company only. Viraj Mahadevia: But how many were there earlier? Manish Grover: Earlier it was around 70, now it is around 50. And this will go to 0 in 50 in the next 2-3 years

items.statement: FY25 sales guidance of at least Rs 8,500 crore on a base case, aiming higher if new launches and inventory release perform well
items.quote: If we continue on the path of at least 20% plus, SOB H we should be at least doing Rs. 8,500 crores. And if we can achieve anything more than that, based on the new launches that we are seeing and based on how the release of inventory, if it continues to do well, then definitely we should be aiming towards it

items.statement: FY25 launch target of 9 million square feet, up ~30% from 7 million square feet in FY24
items.quote: Of the remaining unlaunched inventory of 16.85 million, we plan to launch about 9 million square feet in FY '25 and the remaining subsequently, that would be an increase of about 30% from the previous year of 7 million square feet launches.

items.statement: Robust inventory visibility of 24.4 million sq ft comprising 16.85 million sq ft potential new launches and 7.55 million sq ft existing inventory
items.quote: At the end of this quarter, we have potential new launches of 16.85 million square feet and an existing inventory of 7.55 million square feet, making a robust inventory visibility of 24.4 million II square feet

The biggest spurt of growth in new business was in Indonesia, particularly with the Taman Safari Group, which is the large group that we acquired wi th revenues to the tune of roughly about INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores.

items.statement: Expect outbound travel revenue to recover to FY20 level of INR2,400 crores in FY25 from INR1,400 crores in FY24
items.quote: And our expectation is that we will see that number coming back in FY '25. That's the point we are making, yes. And that comprises of your short haul as well as long haul.

items.statement: Expect MICE business to grow at high double-digit 15-20% in FY25 and beyond
items.quote: So we expect this growth to be in the, as I said, high double digit, in the range of about 15% to 20%. That's the kind of expectation we have for FY '25 and beyond.

items.statement: Expect DMS business to repeat similar strong growth trend next year
items.quote: And our expectation next year is that we should be rather repeating a similar growth trend.

items.statement: Expect travel segment EBIT margin to improve from current 3.5% towards 5% range
items.quote: Our ambition is to move our EBIT margin to close to that 5% range. We are currently about 3.5%.

items.statement: Expect overall travel segment recovery to be almost closer to pre-pandemic level in 2025
items.quote: we expect the recovery in 2025 on the travel segment to be almost closer to the pre-pandemic level.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin improvement driven by volume growth and cost transformation benefits
items.quote: So clearly, we expect a lot of flow-through of the increased revenue to come to the bottom line. And hence, it's reasonable to estimate that our EBIT margins will improve from where we are currently based on the higher volumes that will come through.

items.statement: DMS business is currently very profitable
items.quote: But I can assure you one thing. But then if you look at DMS as a whole, it is certainly very profitable right now.

items.statement: Strong demand for MICE from corporates expanding distribution networks in Tier 2-4 markets
items.quote: So clearly, each one trying to expand their volumes will either go and get new set of distributors or piggy bank on the existing network. And there is this race to be better than the other.

items.statement: Inbound travel expected to grow 18-20% in current year
items.quote: Dipak, during his conversation, spoke about inbound businesses and s aid how he expects the recovery to happen and expecting an 18%- 20% growth in the current year

items.quote: DMS now contributed 41% of the turnover for the travel segment, which used to be about 30% pre-COVID. The business has grown about 27% during the year.

items.statement: Deploying technology to reduce transaction time by 70% and enable instant mobile downloads for Digiphoto
items.quote: the entire mode of transaction is going to reduce some time by at least 70%. So if average transaction time if we assume is 3 minutes, it can be done and lessened in about 40-50 seconds.

items.statement: Full benefit of Digiphoto technology deployment expected next year
items.quote: we see a full blown benefit of this in the next year, precisely.

items.statement: Prepaid card portfolio grew 20% last quarter and 14% YoY; floats typically 4-5% of portfolio; expect $20-30M addition YoY
items.quote: Typically, in a model like this, floats account for about anywhere between 4% to 5% of your overall portfolio. And we expect that this addition year-on-year will be anywhere between $20 million to $30 million.

items.statement: Forex floats managed through swaps and forwards, not deployed into working capital
items.quote: We actually do swaps, yes, because what happens is you will appreciate that when I sell a prepaid card to a customer, I sell in foreign currency and he pays me in rupee and there is a delay from the time that I raised an invoice for the corporate to process the invoice and take the payment back to me.

items.statement: Finance charges INR26 crores in current quarter vs INR23 crores YoY; real interest INR5.5 crores vs INR8 crores YoY
items.quote: our total finance charges, as I would like to put it, is about INR26 crores as against INR23 crores last year, same quarter last year. Out of the INR26 crores, about INR5.5 crores is the real interest. items.statement: Going forward, overall finance cost will keep going up but indicates volume improvement rather than working capital charges
items.quote: So at the overall level, yes, the overall finance cost will keep on going up, but it really ind icates the improvement in volumes rather than charges for working capital

items.statement: RBI discussion paper on money changers proposes FX correspondents concept; expect consolidation in space
items.quote: One of those things that they have spoken about is they want to introduce this concept of FxCs, which is FX correspondents. We believe it will bring us a lot of consolidation in that space because we have about, give or take, 1,500, 1,600 money changers who operate in this country.

items.statement: Prepaid forex card represents 26% market share, growing at 40% YoY and 15% 10-year CAGR
items.quote: our prepaid card today, we represent about 26% of the market, and it's been growing at about 40%. And if I look at the 10-year CAGR on this, we've been growing at about 15% on a 10-year period.

items.statement: Digiphoto differentiated by emotional experience, augmented reality, video elements, auto edits not replicable by smartphones
items.quote: We are selling a video part of it. We are doing a lot of stuff. We're adding a lot of enhancements on it. We're doing augmented reality on it. So it's way a lot more than just another complete picture.

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; focus on building cash on balance sheet after pandemic hit
items.quote: We don't have anything in the horizon, neither are we in any conversation with anyone at this point in time.

items.statement: No buyback plans; focus on showing gratitude to investors who stayed through pandemic period
items.quote: I think the word reward depends on how you perceive it. In our case, it's not a question of reward, but it is our way of showing gratitude to our investors who stayed with us through this period.

items.statement: Continuous innovation and adaptation across distribution channels and customer interactions over past couple of years
items.quote: That entire exercise has been going on for a couple of years. So it's not a question of whether our model works or not. It's our ability to adapt to the requirements of the market, and that's something that we have done.

items.statement: Sterling ROCE for FY24 close to 20%, ahead of peer comparison
items.quote: It's 20% and it's ahead of the peer comparison.

items.statement: Focus on getting business completely back to normal across all segments and geographies; reviewing AI implementation opportunities
items.quote: But right now, our focus is to get our business completely back to normal across all the segments that we operate in. And the reality is we operate in multiple geographies as well as multiple segments.

items.statement: Targets 18-20% EBITDA margin by FY26
items.quote: Our visibility and confidence in our performance in FY25, and our ability to achieve the long-term aspiration of 18-20% EBITDA by FY26, has further bolstered.

items.statement: Expects meaningful profitability improvement in FY25 from Q2
items.quote: On the back of margin improvement action plan initiated, prudent cost management and narrowing losses in Zee5, we are hopeful of seeing a meaningful improvement in overall profitability in

items.statement: FMCG ad spending recovery driving ad revenue growth
items.quote: The FMCG sector has been recovering with the rural sentiment witnessing an uptick, leading to a healthy increase in advertisement revenue for the Company, both, on a quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Industry ad and subscription revenue expected to grow high single digits in FY25
items.quote: I think the industry itself will see healthy growth in the high single digits for both subscription and advertising.

items.statement: Q4 operating costs steady YoY, up QoQ due to Zee5 and sports
items.quote: In Q4FY24 our YoY operating cost base has remain steady, while it has seen some uptick QoQ due to Zee5 and sports.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiated, one-time costs in Q1 FY25, margin improvement from Q2 FY25
items.quote: While these interventions will have some one-time costs coming in Q1 FY25, we are well setup for driving a healthy margin improvement beginning Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Zee5 EBITDA loss flat in FY24, costs at peak, will trend down after streamlining
items.quote: In FY24, Zee5 EBITDA loss remained flat. As part of our overall performance enhancement plan, we are revisiting and optimising the overall Zee5 cost structure in line with our strategic priorities.

items.statement: Ad revenue grew 8.1% QoQ and 10.4% YoY in Q4 FY24
items.quote: These factors enabled us to post healthy 8.1% QoQ growth on a festive quarter base, and 10.4% YoY growth.

items.statement: Subscription revenue grew 12% YoY and 3.1% QoQ in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Similarly, Q4 FY24 Subscription revenues are up at a healthy rate of 12% YoY and 3.1% QoQ.

items.statement: Other sales and services grew 31.5% YoY in FY24 driven by movie performance
items.quote: This strong movie performance across theatrical and syndication, aided the other sales and services, which grew at 31.5% YoY in FY24.

items.statement: Zee5 revenue grew 24.1% in FY24
items.quote: Zee5 revenues were up 24.1% in FY24.

items.statement: Q4 viewership share at 16.8%, up 30 bps QoQ
items.quote: Encouragingly in Q4 FY24, Zee Marathi and Zee TV have both shown uptick, and our Q4 viewership share performance has increased by 30 bps QoQ, coming in at 16.8%.

items.statement: Zee Music Company #2 music channel with 149M YouTube subscribers and 165B video views in FY24
items.quote: Zee Music Company (ZMC) continues to be the #2 music channel with over 149 Mn subscribers on YouTube and over 165 Bn total video views during FY24.

items.statement: Content inventory declined by Rs 5.4 Bn YoY to Rs 74.2 Bn in Mar'24
items.quote: Mar'24 Content inventory, advances, and deposits were at Rs 74.2 Bn, lower by Rs 5.4 Bn on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Generated strong FCF in Q4 driven by working capital optimization
items.quote: During the quarter, we generated strong FCF driven by optimization of working capital.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments at Rs 11.9 Bn as of Mar'24 (Rs 5.7 Bn cash, Rs 6.2 Bn FDs)
items.quote: The cash & treasury investments increased duri ng the quarter and as of Mar’24 stood at Rs 11.9 Bn, which includes a Cash balance of Rs 5.7 Bn and FDs of Rs 6.2 Bn

items.statement: Withdrew merger implementation application from NCLT, continuing SIAC arbitration
items.quote: the Company has withdrawn its merger implementation application from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). This decisi on will enable the Company to sharply focus on growth and strategic opportunities, in order to generate higher value for all shareholders

items.statement: Expects NTO 3.0 and tariff forbearance to strengthen pay-TV ecosystem
items.quote: We remain hopeful that NTO 3.0 implementation and tariff forbearance will strengthen the pay-TV ecosystem and pave way for sustained growth in subscription revenues.

items.statement: Being cautious on content acquisition pricing, may slow down buying
items.quote: We have been aggressive already Pankaj in terms of buying movies, but there are times when in situations like today, where we have to become a bit frugal to make sure that we are buying the right content at the right pricing.

items.statement: Zee5 pricing competitive, room for pricing to go up across industry
items.quote: We are competing in the market on pricing with everybody, and we have pretty competitive or even equal to whatever the pricing may be, maybe a little bit lower than them, but that is for the reasons for the content that we do not offer, whether it be sports or the English language content.

items.statement: Zee5 pivoting to balanced cost structure, expects short-term financial aberration
items.quote: We have been over-indexing on the growth and investments in the past, but the need of the hour is to pivot the business to achieve a balanced cost structure, in order to sustain long-term growth.

items.statement: Focus on quality content over big-budget films for movie business
items.quote: If you look at most of our successes in the last 2 years, have not been high -cost content. T hey have been reasonable cost or even low cost that has worked for

And if you look at the content offering that ZEE5 has, that's what we have always maintained that we are a holistic family entertainment

And now we truly believe that our pla tform is stable, and our platform has been built up to compete in the market in the best form that we can

items.statement: Merger arbitration sub-judice, will safeguard stakeholder interests
items.quote: Sameer, these things are very sub-judice, so I would not like to comment on those things, but we will do everything that's possible to safeguard the interest of our stakeholders and the company. That is our prime objective.

items.statement: Full repayment of USD 314.4 million debt at Maamba Collieries completed during FY24 ahead of schedule.
items.quote: Our commitment to financial prudence and operational excellence has resulted in significant milestones including the full debt repayment of USD314.4 million during the financial year at Maamba Collieries ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Stand-alone profit increased 55% quarter-on-quarter in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue and profit reached highest ever levels in FY24.

items.quote: Our Energy division has particularly excelled with Nava Bharat Energy's 150 megawatts power plant, witnessing a turnaround in its financial performance marked by substantial increase in PLF in the current financial year.

items.quote: Similarly, our mining division in Zambia has reported healthy growth in sales and profitability, driven by improved coal sales and operational efficiencies.

items.quote: We use only about 10% of MOIL's ore in the overall blend. Having said that, as a company, we are quite well insulated from these increased prices because when prices were low, we had accumulated large stocks. So, our current inventory would serve us for the next couple of quarters, so we are fairly insulated from these increased prices in the market.

items.quote: Right now, it's $110 million. It's not 5 to 6 months. I think it's $ 5 million for the next 1 or 2 months and then the number increases. So altogether for 6 months, it's $110 million.

items.statement: Raw material inventory secured at lower prices will last next couple of quarters, keeping cost structure linear.
items.quote: And as a Company, we have secured raw material pricing, which are also in the rise …. early on at reduced prices. So we have an inventory, which will last for the next couple of quarters, which essentially means that the cost structure is going to be more or less of a linear one going forward.

items.statement: No interest cost in FY25 as zero debt at standalone and consolidated levels; only minimal working capital borrowings.
items.quote: There is no interest cost for FY '25 as of now because there is no debt either at a stand -alone level or at a consolidated level. It's only normal working capital, which is very minimal.

items.statement: Avocado plantation on 1,100 hectares; full production expected at 22,000-25,000 metric tons yielding $50-60 million revenue.
items.quote: Avocados, the total area where we have the plant is about 1100 hectares. And once the entire 1,100 hectares come into full scale production, we anticipate a production of somewhere about 22,000 to 25,000 metric tons. Going by the present values of Avocado, we anticipate revenue of $50 million to $60 million.

items.quote: First, magnetite is very new. We are yet to start on the exploration. Once we get to the reserves, that time we'll be able to envisage what's going to be the investment on the magnetite mining site, etc.

items.statement: African expansions structured under separate subsidiaries: Maamba Collieries for power (Phase 2 under same), agri business in separate 100% subsidiary.
items.quote: There are different subsidiaries. Whereas Maamba Collieries is a different subsidiary under which we have the Phase 1 power plant, and the Phase 2 could be under that. And agri business is anyway 100% in a different subsidiary.

items.statement: Zambia Phase 2 equity to be funded by Nava Bharat Singapore using dividends and shareholder loan repayments from MCL.
items.quote: Yes. So with regards to the Phase 2 , the equity would need to be financed by NBS. But at the end of the day, MCL will declare dividends and repay the shareholder loan to NBS. So NBS will be utilizing some of that cash flow to fund its equity.

items.statement: ZESCO arrears collection uncertain; management doing best but cannot guarantee 100% recovery by calendar 2024.
items.quote: Yes. So I don't think we can be 100% sure of anything in life. So what we can assure you is we are doing our level best to discuss with ZESCO. ZESCO has been honouring a lot of its commitments. We are working with ZESCO times are tough in Zambia, and we definitely wish and hope to recoup the entire amount, but it will all depend on discussions that we have with ZESCO as we move forward.

items.statement: Aspirational target of $100 million revenue by FY26 maintained, dependent on execution and hiring
items.quote: We believe we have an amazing opportunity. We've always said $100 million was the dream, was aspirational target. And we still believe that these opportunities exist.

items.statement: No formal projections given for FY25; goal is to beat previous quarter and improve EBITDA margin
items.quote: We don't give projections. But as I said, my simple goal that I work with since the day I got this job and I think as long as I will be here is to beat the previous quarter and that's what we aspire to do.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 11%+, first time double-digit; Q4 EBITDA 8.2% due to one-off expenses; target 35% gross margin vs current ~29%
items.quote: We have delivered strong double digit EBDITA of 11%+ for the first time with phenomenal performance from entire team.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 8.2% lower than expected due to several one-time expenses; expect bounce back to double-digit
items.quote: And our EBITDA margin was at 8.2%, it was a bit lower than we expected because of several onetime expenses that we had in the quarter.

items.statement: Strong demand across all three verticals; pipeline better than ever; re-signed three lost customers; old customers returning
items.quote: So, V.P, our whole world has changed from April 1 because we all are fresh. There's nothing for us to move away from anymore. It's better and bigger than we've ever seen, I continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Active client roster reduced to 84 from 250; exited bottom 10-15 customers; target 75 clients for INR 800 cr revenue
items.quote: And while we added a lot of new customers, we also exited the bottom 10 - 15 customers. And now, our active client roster is down to a healthy 84.

items.statement: Just signed a Fortune 50 company as new healthcare customer; healthcare domestic and Europe revenue to go to zero, US/Canada to grow
items.quote: And as we speak, we have just signed a Fortune 50 company as a new customer. I'll get to that later.

items.statement: DSO improved from 86 days to 72 days; further improvement opportunity exists
items.quote: In terms of DSO, which I already touch base upon, we had a huge improvement from 86 days to 72 days, and we still see a lot of opportunity for us to improve.

items.statement: New office opening in Bangalore Whitefield in July; upgrading to A-grade tech parks for data security and amenities
items.quote: In addition to this, we strengthened our offshore infrastructure, whether it is Pune, Chennai and then very soon coming in July, we have a new office in Bangalore in Whitefield opening up

items.statement: Global headcount 2,529, down ~200 YoY due to exit of domestic volume business; target 2,700-2,800 with majority outside India
items.quote: I want to acknowledge my entire team, which is now at 2,529 employees globally. So, if you see this compared from a year ago, we've gone down by about 200-odd people.

items.statement: Key managers moved to USA and UK for global roles; hiring local talent and transferring employees from India; trend to continue 3 years
items.quote: Now, under each of these leaders, we are hiring local people and in parallel, we are transferring many more employees from our various India offices. I expect this trend to continue for next 3 years as we build our global presence and account management capabilities.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 5 per equity share, highest ever, 9th consecutive year, subject to AGM approval in July
items.quote: Based on the performance, our Board has recommended this morning a dividend of INR 5 per equity share, the highest ever in our history and marking the ninth consecutive year of dividend payout, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming 33rd Annual General Meeting in July.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Industrial Equipment 52%, Transportation & Mobility 37%, Healthcare 8%; 98% from three verticals, 2% ITS to go away
items.quote: Industrial Equipment & Heavy Machinery continues to be our largest vertical and growing very well, and we see amazing potential is at 52%; Transportation & Mobility, which is where automotive is predominantly the largest vertical and now rail is where we are investing, contributed 37% of our revenues; and Healthcare, which is our new vertical, contributed about 8% of our revenue.

items.statement: Pivoted from pure-play mechanical to software (embedded, digital, AI, ML, cybersecurity, data analytics); largest RFPs and deals in software
items.quote: The other side of the story, which is a real ga me changer for us for the last three years, has been when we pivoted from just a pure -play mechanical and engineering services company to software, both on the embedded side and digital side.

items.statement: Sales team fully relocated to US (Michigan) and Europe (London); no sales team in India from April 1; lead gen and presales remain offshore
items.quote: Our entire sales team led by Vignesh, who's Executive Vice President and part of my global management team, he has moved to Michigan. He's building a team around there. Pramod Patil, who's again Executive Vice President, part of the management team; has moved to London. He's building a whole team in Europe.

items.statement: US immigration opened up; Canada visa processing down to 3-4 months from 6-12; Germany 3-6 months, targeting 1 month
items.quote: US was shut for us till about last year. And now, US is open. So, we have people going to US. Canada, which was taking 6, 9 months, 12 months is now taking 3 to 4 months only. Germany is still 3 to 6 months, and we hope it goes down to 1 month.

items.statement: No active M&A discussions; open to acquisitions with cash and PE partner Convergent; priority is finding company supporting existing clients
items.quote: Shriram, on the M&A side, nothing concrete as of today. We haven't , there is nothing that we are actively discussing. But as I always said, we are very open. We have the cash. We have very strong PE partner in Convergent.

items.statement: Exited large Indian healthcare customer end of April (~130 engineers at USD 4.5-5/hr); domestic healthcare revenue to become zero
items.quote: So, for example, we exited a large Indian customer end of April where about 120 engineers moved away, and we transitioned them to some other pay roll the customer chose. So that significant number of headcounts will come down.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 440 cr to INR 470+ cr (7%+ YoY); PAT grew 194% (3x) from INR 11+ cr to INR 34+ cr; cash from INR 48 cr to INR 93 cr
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we have grown from INR 440 crores to INR 470 + crores, which is a 7%+ growth. I think we could have done much better if it wasn't for all the clients that we were exiting during our transition phase.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 307 cr to INR 472 cr over last 8 quarters; Q4 revenue INR 118 cr after Q3 dip from furloughs/holidays
items.quote: And the exact number from INR 307 crores in the last 8 quarters we have gone to INR 472 crores in quarters. So huge growth for a company of our size and I'm very excited and very happy where we are.

items.statement: Moving engineers from India billing (USD 5-10/hr) to onsite global billing (USD 18-75/hr) drives margin improvement; not headcount-driven growth
items.quote: Let us say we are invoicing at USD 5, USD 6, USD 7, USD 8, USD 10 an hour. And they are moving to my international business where we are invoicing from USD 18 an hour to USD 75 an hour if they are on site.
