items.statement: Free cash flows largely consumed by project sizes, only 10% available for land acquisitions
items.quote: Majorly free cash flows would get utilized in the self-projects as a possessor of bigger site. Though the cash flows also has increased up in YoY basis and we would see up the same type of 30% growth in terms of collections also. But the project sizes would consume the free cash flows also or the increased cash flows. There may be 10% of cash flows of the total cash flows it can be utilized for la

items.statement: Company culture of spending right and not spending high drives capital efficiency
items.quote: And this is all put together in terms of monitoring, in terms of hard work, et cetera, that we have been able to generate better margins, better profits, even given an average selling price of INR 6,500 as on this year also. And going forward also, we would be able to do it because that is the culture. The whole of the office is under that culture of spending right and not spending high.

items.statement: Land bank mix: 75% owned land, 20-25% joint development asset-light model
items.quote: So, we are open to it. And going forward as on today, we see that at least a mix of 75% places is where we own the land as an owner of 100%, and 20-25% of the projects are into asset-light model which is called as joint developments.

items.statement: Unutilized land bank only 15-20 acres
items.quote: Most of them are already done, not unutilized or unplanned lands or something to a size of 15-20 acres only.

items.statement: FY25 footfall growth expected at max 5% for existing parks; ARPU growth 10-12%
items.quote: But having said that, I think at a company level we are not expecting more than 5% footfall growth for FY'25. But the footfall growth and ARPU growth will be about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Odisha park targeting 4 lakh footfalls at ARPU Rs 800-1,000 in first year
items.quote: We are expecting about 4 lakh visitors at an ARPU of roughly Rs.800-1,000. So that's the way we are looking at it. This is our conservative estimate.

items.statement: Existing parks ARPU growth ~10% in FY25; marginal footfall growth
items.quote: We are expecting an ARPU growth in our existing parks of around double digits, 10% this year because we've had huge ARPU growth in the last two years.

items.statement: Odisha park EBITDA positive from year 1; PAT positive from year 2-3
items.quote: We are expecting it will be EBITDA positive from first year itself, and at the PAT level, it should be positive from year two or three.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin may shrink 3-4 percentage points due to Bhubaneswar park
items.quote: In the next FY , Bhubaneswar Park into our k itty, there could be some little shrinkage in the margin percentage of about some three to four percentage.

items.statement: Chennai park revised budget Rs 515 crore including land; Rs 194 crore committed/paid by Mar 2024
items.quote: In Chennai Park, we had a revised budget expense of somewhere close to 515 crore s and including the orders what we committed, we have about 194 crores has been committed or paid till 31st of March 2024.

items.statement: Odisha park budget ~Rs 190 crore; nearly complete
items.quote: And then in Odisha Park, we had a budget of about 189 crores and we are at the last leg of completing it. So probably , we'll be finishing it up for maybe around 190 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~10% of park top line annually for new rides
items.quote: We typically spend 10% of our top line from a particular park as we earmark with and keep it for adding new rides to the park.

items.statement: IT/digital transformation investment ~Rs 4-5 crore in next year
items.quote: In fact, we have a new IT head has joined and so in the next one year, we will be investing I think about 4-5 crores in new tech for our parks.

items.statement: Odisha park soft launch 24 May 2024; full opening next week
items.quote: We are actually soft launching from 24th onwards. I'm taking this call from Bhubaneswar. We just finished the press launch of the park. Tomorrow and day after we having a preview meet for some well-wishers and influencers and all that. And then the next week the park is opening.

items.statement: Chennai park commissioning likely Q3 FY26; targeting late Q2 if no rain delays
items.quote: We will be commissioning most likely in the third quarter. We are trying to finish in second quarter because we would like to be ready before the third quarter. There could be some delays because of unseasonal rains plays havoc in Chennai sometime.

items.statement: Plan to open ~1 new park per year; 5 more locations targeted by FY30
items.quote: We are looking at another five more locations in addition to what we already have. One or two of them will get closed and before the end of this financial year and the rest we will announce as and when they are ready.

items.statement: Bangalore & Kochi parks at capacity in peak season; headroom in Q2/Q4
items.quote: There is a limit, for example, on a summer season, our parks are already running pretty full. So it's hard for us to justify higher footfalls. But there are like for example Q2 and Q4, we do feel that there is some more headroom for us to grow.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 footfall hit by exam prepone & elections (Kochi group -37%); heat wave impacted Bangalore
items.quote: Normally, our Cochin park has a high contribution from group sales in January . That did not happen this year. Now the reason we are told is because of change in exam dates and also preponing of exams because of elections. So these are the two reasons that we were given. The other two parks I've not seen this issue. Only Cochin, I think the group footfalls degrew by 37%.

items.statement: Hyderabad park at 70% of Bangalore/Kochi footfalls; expanding marketing to Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: If you look at footfalls in Hyderabad compared to like for example, Kochi or Bangalore, it's only 70% of the other two parks, whereas we feel that it should be at par with the other parks. So we still feel there is a headroom for us to grow foot falls in Hyderabad.

items.statement: ARPU grew 15% in FY24 driven by non-ticket revenue (F&B, retail)
items.quote: ARPU for the quarter s tood at Rs.1,349, an increase of 14% , and for F Y'24 at Rs.1,430, registering a growth of 15%. Our increase in ARPU was driven by a healthy growth in non-ticket Wonderla Holidays Limited May 17, 2024 revenue along with encouraging response from walk-in groups and all aspects of our customer base

items.statement: Employee cost up 16% YoY in FY24 due to salary revision & headcount increase (+54 for year)
items.quote: There is actually 16% revision in the salary cost as compared to the previous year, and at the same time we had a headcount increase for this quarter as well as for the year, there was about some 16 number has added to the corporate team in the current year and even to the parks as well and then 38 numbers have been added during the full year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 38.7% (-28pp YoY) due to lower footfall, higher payroll, lower other income
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter reached Rs.40.5 crores, degrew by 28 percentage on year-on-year basis. This was due to reduction in our footfall, increase in our payroll expenses and reduction in other income. EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 38.7%.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 49.4% (adj. 49.7%); PAT margin 31.2%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stood at Rs.250.1 crores as againstRs.234.6 crores same period last year, showing a 6.6 % year-on-year increase. EBITDA margin for the year was 49.4% . Adjusted EBITDA for FY'24 was at Rs.251 crores as against Rs.235 crores for the same period last year with the margin of 49.7 percentage.

items.statement: Will raise funds (debt/equity combo) for new projects; Chennai capex large
items.quote: We will be looking at some fundraise. Some amount of debt depending on how many projects we sign in the next year or so, we'll take a call on that. We will be definitely doing some fundraise in the form of either debt or equity or most likely a combination of both.

items.statement: Reorganising sales, marketing, IT teams; new IT head hired; beefing up projects team for parallel execution
items.quote: We are reorganizing our sales team and our marketing team is going through a bit of a reorganization. Because of the way we are also going through a digital transformation , our IT team is also going through a substantial change. items.statement: Government talks on hold due to election code of conduct; will resume after elections
items.quote: Nothing as of now, because this is election season. I think all of those conversations have been put on hold as of now because of code of conduct . We are waiting for normal government functioning to resume, then we will take up.

items.statement: Resort occupancy fell to 55% in FY24 due to loss of long-stay industrial guests
items.quote: In the current year, there were no major long stays. So that's the reason why the occupancy has reduced to 55% in the current FY.

items.statement: Footfall volatile due to exams, elections, heat waves; seasonality limits peak-season growth
items.quote: Every year the story tends to be little different. For us, the best way to mitigate this is to be in more locations and I have always some projects in the pipeline.

items.statement: Depreciation policy: rides & machinery over 10 years; consistent across parks
items.quote: Asset side for the plant and machinery like these rides and things like that we are depreciating over a period of 10 years.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected around Rs 4,000 million, similar to FY24
items.quote: Next year, the figure should be similar to about Rs. 4,000 million, unless there are other new opportunities.

items.statement: Europe FY25 capex budget approx €40 million to complete EV capacity installation
items.quote: Speaking about FY 25, the budget is to implement the total production capacity with an effort of approx. 40 million euro as gross amount.

items.statement: Target four-wheeler share of consolidated business 45% by FY30 from 25% now
items.quote: Increase our four-wheeler share of consolidated business from 25% now to 45% by FY 30.

items.statement: Target aftermarket sales 10% of India sales by FY28
items.quote: Our focus also is to reach 10% of India sales in our aftermarket business in India by FY28.

items.statement: Carbon neutral target >50% by FY30 from 35% in FY24
items.quote: the aspiration is to reach a carbon-neutral percentage of more than 50 % by FY30

items.statement: AURIC non-auto/4W plant capex Rs 4,009 million through March 2028, SOP Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total CAPEX is expected to be Rs. 4,009 million which should be spent in stages from now to March 2028, with the sales expectation of more than Rs. 5,000 million per annum.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated capex Rs 3,833 million, 81% for growth
items.quote: We have done Capex of about Rs. 3,833 million in FY24, which was 81% for growth, which included building, plant machinery and dies.

items.quote: In FY24, we booked capex of €62 million of investment in order to install this production capacity.

items.quote: We are further planning to increase this capacity to 1.2 million single and dual channel ABS assemblies per annum in the second half of FY26.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity expanded to 5.5m wheels/yr from 4.5m
items.quote: we are now expanding to supply 5.5 million wheels per annum and the SO P has already started for April 24

items.statement: Disc brake assembly run rate 6.2m/yr, brake disc 8.1m/yr
items.quote: With this new plant, we have reached a run rate of 6.2 million numbers per annum of disc brake assembly volumes, and 8.1 million numbers per annum of brake disc volume.

items.statement: EV aluminum castings ramp to 240k sets/yr (Rs 1,000m/yr) peak Q3 FY25
items.quote: For EV Scooters, we are ramping up our sales to 240,000 sets per annum of aluminum castings, which are required for electric vehicle battery packs and motor housings. The total value will be Rs. 1,000 million per annum, which has already started and will reach peak sales value in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Four-wheeler order wins Rs 2,810m in FY24 (23% of total)
items.quote: The total four-wheeler business win in FY24 is Rs. 2,810 million, which is 23% of our total order wins in FY24.

items.statement: Active RFQ pipeline Rs 18,440m from OEMs
items.quote: we are in discussion for Rs. 18,440 million worth of request for quotes from OEMs.

items.statement: Europe FY24 order wins €30.8m (VW Group, Mercedes); 24-month total €115m (€61m BEV, €35m hybrid)
items.quote: In FY 24, we have won €3 0.8 million business , mainly from the V olkswagen Group including Porsche & Audi, and Mercedes Benz. In the last 24 months, out of €115 million orders, €61 million orders are for the growing battery EV business and €35 million are for hybrids.

items.statement: Aluminum alloy prices trending down; driven by scrap availability and sea freight
items.quote: The price trend appears to be downwards.

items.statement: Focus on structural castings (swing arms, subframes, crank cases) and machining for higher value add
items.quote: We are also getting into structural castings like swing arms and subframes and structural fairings which are complex, which need technology and where pricing is better.

items.statement: Aluminum forging expanding beyond backward integration; orders from JLR, Harley-Davidson
items.quote: We have also got orders from Harley-Davidson, and we are talking to other OEMs. We learn from Jaguar Land Rover that aluminum forgings will be a very important part in 4 wheelers.

items.statement: New 4W customers: Tata Punch Powertrain, JLR, Hyundai, Mahindra, Tata Motors
items.quote: These orders are mainly from Tata Punch Powertrain, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Jaguar Land Rover, and Hyundai.

items.statement: ABS market ~3.5m/yr in India; competing with Bosch, Continental; now supplying dual-channel from July 2024
items.quote: the competition is mainly from Bosch and Continental, which controls the major market share in the Indian ABS two-wheeler market of approximately 3.5 million per annum. We are now in the process of supplying our dual channel ABS from July 24, 2024.

items.statement: FAME II subsidy withdrawal impacted 2W EV OEM order flow in India
items.quote: Definitely, the withdrawal of FAME II subsidy in India has affected a lot of 2-wheeler EV OEMs who were market leaders.

items.statement: India standalone exports grew 4.4% to Rs 2,210m FY24; aftermarket exports to 34 countries
items.quote: In FY24, the export sales for India standalone business grew by 4.43% from Rs. 2,116.23 million in FY23 to Rs. 2,210.06 million in FY24.

items.statement: Net debt zero; consolidated cash Rs 5.044 billion
items.quote: There was no net debt and there was a consolidated positive cash available which has crossed the Rs.5 billion mark and it stood at Rs.5.044 billion.

items.statement: Europe considering acquisitions due to supplier bankruptcies in EV transition
items.quote: Unfortunately, there are a lot of companies in bankruptcy due to the fact that the OEM's strategy in the last few years was to focus only on a few suppliers like us for the electric development. We are considering possible acquisition in order to grow.

items.statement: Expects e-commerce industry growth of 15-20% and plans internal operations for that range
items.quote: See, I think industry growth, at least as far as we've been able to gather from our clients as well and their appetite, remains in that 15% to 20% range.

items.statement: Expects FY25 capex to decline to 6.6-6.9% of revenue from 7.4% in FY24
items.quote: We expect this to decline in fiscal '25 to somewhere between 6.6% and 6.9% of revenue overall.

items.statement: Sufficient capacity to grow through FY25; only major addition is Bangalore mega facility; Tauru gateway capacity expanded 10-15% via process improvements
items.quote: we have sufficient capacity available to grow through fiscal '25. We will need to build our Bangalore mega facility. And there may be some smaller hubs that are planned here and there, but there's nothing major outside of this

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA at 18.4% for FY24, in line with long-term 18-20% target; PTL incremental margins 40-50%; SCS service EBITDA doubled to 6.8%
items.quote: Total service EBITDA from the Express Parcel business has grown from Rs. 636 crores in fiscal '23 to Rs. 934 crores in fiscal '24, which represents 18.4% of revenue and is in line with our long-term targets for this business.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes grew 12% YoY to 740M in FY24; PTL freight grew 30% YoY to 1.4M metric tons; Truckload grew 40% YoY
items.quote: We delivered 740 million Express Parcels in our Express Parcel business in fiscal '24, which is a growth of nearly 12% year-on-year and 1.4 million metric tons of Part Truckload freight, which is a growth of nearly 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: No significant pricing movements needed or anticipated; will pass cost efficiencies to customers; yields up 6% YoY due to mix, weight increases, and some account repricing
items.quote: We haven't seen any significant sort of pricing movements being necessary in the market so far, and we don't anticipate that there will be significant pricing movements at this point going forward.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 38 to 31; receivable days down from 77 to 66; expects further improvement in FY25
items.quote: We are now closing fiscal '24 with a net working capital position of 31 days. Receivable days have declined consistently over the last 5 financial years and especially between '23 and '24 from 77 days to 66 days, and we expect to see further improvements to this financial year.

items.statement: Sandeep Barasia (ED & CBO) leaving after 9 years to pursue personal interests
items.quote: Mr. Sandeep Barasia has announced his decision to move on from Delhivery to pursue personal interests. On behalf of the employees, the Board of Directors and the shareholders of Delhivery, I'd like to place on record our gratitude to Mr. Barasia for his service as an Executive Director and Chief Business Officer of Delhivery for 9 years.

items.statement: Delhivery >100% of Express Parcel profit pool (ex-captives); PTL growth driven by service quality not discounting; pricing comparable to market
items.quote: We are fairly certain that if you take the third-party players put together and our Express business, we are materially over 100% of the profit pool of this industry.

items.statement: PTL truck utilization ~65% on trailer network, 55-60% on secondary line haul; room for improvement
items.quote: Broadly across the trailer network, if I break it in half, I think truck utilization on the trailer network would have been in the range of about 65% or thereabouts. Broadly speaking, on the secondary line haul, we would have been closer to about 55% to 60% utilized.

items.statement: Express Parcel 62% of revenue, PTL 19%, Supply Chain ~10%, Truckload & Cross Border ~9%; PTL share up from 16%
items.quote: Express Parcel continues to be the largest part of our business overall at 62% of revenue. The PTL business has grown significantly between fiscal' 23 and fiscal '24 from 16% of revenue to 19% of revenue.

items.statement: Active multi-service customers increased to 33,278; Meesho volume impact stabilized; new SCS customers ramped in Q3-Q4
items.quote: We have expanded the overall number of active customers who access multiple services of Delhivery with 33,278 customers as of the end of Q4.

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 8,142 crores (+12.7% YoY); EBITDA Rs 127 crores (1.6% margin) vs loss of Rs 452 crores; PAT loss narrowed 75% to ~Rs 250 crores
items.quote: We've delivered Rs. 8,142 crores of revenue in fiscal '24, which is a growth of 12.7% compared to fiscal '23 with an EBITDA profit of Rs. 127 crores and an adjusted EBITDA profit of Rs. 76 crores as opposed to an EBITDA loss of Rs. 452 crores.

items.statement: Targets INR 100 crore revenue for FY25, with 80-100 crore range considered exceptionally well
items.quote: Top line our internal target is INR100 crores, but to be very honest we are like I said an internal target is INR100 crores, but anything between 80 to 100 I think, so w e wo uld be doing exceptionally well because 80 would be close to 100% over FY24

items.statement: Targets INR 200 crore revenue for FY26
items.quote: For FY'26, that is correct.

items.statement: Targets $25 million revenue within two years (by FY26)
items.quote: Our immediate goals over the next t wo years is to grab $25 million out of that which on a very logical sense for a company who is approved by Disney, Warner, Paramount , Sony, and all of the majors, to grab $25 million pie out of a $10 billion market is not very difficult

items.statement: Maintains 25% PAT margin guidance for FY25
items.quote: As of now we haven't moved out from there. So as of now we are. It's too early for the full financial year to comment on it. items.quote: We are right now, I would say very conservatively, very, on a very conservative level. We are in talks with productions which have VFX, total VFX budgets of over $50 million. Like I said, we've already started getting work from Star Trek, which is one of the biggest wins for us this year.

items.quote: The EBITDA margin also saw a substantial rise, improving by 1127 bps to 32.30.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 13.92% in FY24

items.quote: But the projections for 2024-2025, we've set the base now. And we are looking at very healthy double-digit crores numbers for 2024-2025 from our OTT business.

items.quote: See, I think you have a lot of capital work in progress now from INR2 crores to it is now INR6 crores. Intangible assets, I can understand you have created this platform. Abhishek More: That's right

items.quote: So it's not only Canada. It's U.S. and Canada. So we have a total of 4 senior people and 7 artist level people.

items.quote: But we also -- it didn't make sense in January, February for us to, when we saw after the strike. So we did reduce some manpower and that's why you see the effect out there. items.quote: We have launched, I'm really happy to inform that we have launched the beta version of vpsets.com, i.e. www.vpsets.com. items.quote: and thanks to her efforts, we've already started working on the Star Trek U niverse, which is a huge breakthrough for Digikore and it should lead to substantial revenue for many, many years for

items.quote: Let me give you an example of Tippet Studio. Tippet Studio is a debtor of more than 18 months to us just now. They have just declared bankruptcy after being taking over by Phantom. So you can't -- we actually have certain debtors which are even older than six months.

items.quote: So, we got an increase from our bank on the CC limits that we enjoyed. So, that is the long-term borrowing that you are talking about.

items.quote: Historically, Digikore has seen H2 weaker than H1, but I'll tell you how it goes now. Let's say in H2, I get a - you see we are project based. items.statement: Revised operating EBITDA margin guidance to 26-28% for FY25 from previous 25-27%
items.quote: With this outlook, I'm pleased to revise our operating EBITDA margin guidance in the range of 26% to 28% as against our previous guidance of 25% to 27%.

items.statement: Domestic business to outperform IPM by 200 bps; domestic and CDMO to reach 75-80% of revenue in midterm
items.quote: Concluding, I would like to state that the domestic business will continue to outperform the IPM by 200 basis points. The domestic business share in the overall business will continue to increase while CDMO business will continue to gain traction. We expect both domestic and CDMO to cumulate the account for 75% to 80% of overall business in midterm.

items.statement: CDMO business to grow 12-14% in FY25 with high teens growth from Q3 onwards
items.quote: This business should grow between 12% to 14% a nd you should see probably high teens growth happening quarter 3 onwards that is October onwards

items.statement: India, CDMO and emerging markets to grow 12-14%; US, Russia, South Africa to grow 8-9%
items.quote: India, CDMO and our emerging market, which is ROW, should grow between 12% to 14%. US, Russia, South Africa should grow at around high single digit, around 8%, 9%.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA to grow 16-18% in short to midterm; gross margins near 65% for next 2 years
items.quote: Overall business growing at around 12% to 14%; EBITDA growing it around 16% to 18%; and EBITDA margins -- operating EBITDA margins between 26% to 28%. That is where we stand. And both India and CDMO will contribute overall to the growth of the company. And overall generating gross margins closer to 65% for the coming 2 years.

items.statement: CDMO lozenges capacity at 2 billion annually, currently running at 1 billion; only maintenance capex needed

items.statement: Complex generics share fell from 76% to 64% YoY due to new clients starting with simple products; existing clients' complex share stable
items.quote: So typically, maybe when a new client is added, they start off with playing single ingredient products and then move on to complex. Since there has been a lot of addition of new customers, probably it might be the impact of that.

items.statement: Top 10 client revenue stable in absolute terms but composition changing as new clients graduate into top 10
items.quote: We are basically saying that in the top 10 this year there are one or two or three new names. We don't give out those new names but the composition of those top 10 clients is differing.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 15 in Q4 from ~33 in September; management expects to stay in 15-33 day range
items.quote: So, if you remember, our September working capital days were around 33 and right now we are at 15. So, this is the range that we expect to continue. One quarter could can be here or there but this is basically the range in which we should stay.

items.statement: Proposed dividend of Rs 11.4 cr (Rs 5.5 per share) for FY24
items.quote: In line with our dividend policy, the Company proposed a dividend of 11.4 crores that is Rs. 5.5 per share related to FY24.

items.statement: Capital allocation mix of organic (oral solids) and inorganic (other dosage forms); injectables to be built organically
items.quote: Mixed, surely as we just mentioned that we want to…So our strategy has been that for organic oral solid business is what we want to build on our own. And for other dosage forms, we would be interested to do acquisitions other than injectables that we have now already put in place.

items.statement: Employee cost ~14% of sales; management views it as strategic investment with ESOPs and variable incentives driving growth; expects operating leverage over time
items.quote: We cannot really comment on the comparison versus competitors. However, what we have been, the money that we spend on employees is what we consider as an investment as a strategy we expect. So, we have brought ESOP schemes, two ESOP schemes we have in place. We also have a variable model of extra incentive limit on achievement of various growth percentages for the critical employees.

items.statement: CDMO operates on cost-plus model with transparent cost sheets; margins stable 11-12.5% regardless of input price volatility
items.quote: I think the primary reason is that it is because the CDMO space, it is a cost-plus business. So, we work with the transparent and open cost sheets with our customers. So, what that does is, it allows us to even like if you have seen during the COVID and just tail end of COVID, there was a huge supply chain problem. The price increases for Metformin, Paracetamol, they went to 3x of those prices. Bu

items.statement: Injectable facility breakeven utilization uncertain due to product mix variability; management will evaluate at FY25 end
items.quote: That really depends on the product mix and eventually many other factors. So, very hard to say on that. That's why we were saying that we should evaluate at the end of the year where we stand on this.

items.statement: Exports vertical revenue Rs 27.4 cr in FY24 (38% YoY); Rs 8.9 cr in Q4 (27% YoY); exhibit batches for export markets being prepared at injectable facility
items.quote: Our exports vertical demonstrated revenue of 27.4 crores in FY24 with YoY growth rate of 38% and 8.9 Cr in Q4 recording YoY growth rate of 27%.

items.statement: Trade generics & institutional growth driven by both distributor expansion and government tenders; Jan Aushadhi stores to grow 2.5x to 25,000 by FY26
items.quote: Government is targeting to increase Jan Aushadhi Store count by 2.5x to 25,000 by end of FY26. This will provide added impetus to our trade generics and institutional business.

items.statement: Structural shift toward quality driving consolidation of supplier base toward organized players like Windlas; non-compliant smaller players losing clients
items.quote: These conversations have been happening in the last couple of years in fact but it takes time for supply chains to change and so we see a continuation on this. Also of course, the new regulator has been very strict on companies who are not complying. And so, clients who are impacted because they have sourced from a small player who has been found non-compliant, then these clients they look for a s

items.statement: Revenue target INR 800-1,200 crore by FY28 including all exclusive brands and Baldus
items.quote: Regarding the guidance I had given was INR800 crores to INR1,200 crores of turnover by FY28. This is the guidance. And this definitely includes all the exclusive brand IOPs we do across the world. And that also includes the Baldus segmentation system.

items.statement: Expect at least 70-75% revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Sir, we are expecting at least 70%, 75% growth this year.

items.statement: Baldus revenue expected in double digits in FY25
items.quote: Sir, we expect a double-digit number this year.

items.statement: Target under 48-hour average TAT nationwide in FY25
items.quote: Within 48 hours we are optimistic that within the next financial year we'll be able to achieve an under 48-hour average TAT within the whole country. That is our vision.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 11.82% in FY24, up 303 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 11.82%, an increase of 303 bps, year -on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin growth expected long-term as own brand share rises, but not large growth in short run
items.quote: So we don't see a large growth on EBITDA margins in the short run, but in the long run definitely if 70% of the sales comes from our own brands and a lot of exclusive brands, we see a good EBITDA numbers in the future.

items.statement: Monthly active users grew 93.8% YoY to 440,000 in FY24
items.quote: Our average monthly active users have grown to 4,40,000 users in FY '24, as against 2,27,000 users in FY '23. This is an increase of 93.83% year-on-year.

items.statement: Total orders grew 36% YoY to 430,574 in FY24
items.quote: The total order growth was 4,30,574 in FY '24, compared to 3,16,748 in FY '23, a year-on-year 36% increase.

items.statement: Customer retention improved from 68% to 76% YoY
items.quote: Our customer retention has increased from 68% to 76% year -on-year, and this is really something important for a company to increase the customer retention going ahead.

items.statement: 90,000 unique customers ordered in FY24; 76% retained
items.quote: 90,000 people are those who have ordered from us in the last financial year. Amit Mehta: Last year? Vikas Agarwal: Yes. And 76% of them are retained customers, rest of them are new customers

items.statement: Addressable market ~320,000 registered dentists, 100,000+ unregistered, 100,000+ dental students, 352 colleges, 5,000+ labs
items.quote: Sir, currently, there are around 3,20,000 approx. registered dentists in the country. Apart from that, we expect more than 1,00,000 unregistered dentists in the country. There are more than 1,00,000 dental students in the country. And then, there are 352 dental colleges, more than 5,000 dental laboratories. These all are the addressable markets.

items.statement: Revenue INR 173.32 crore in FY24, up 40% YoY
items.quote: the revenue from operations in FY '24 was INR173.32 crores, as against INR123.8 crores in FY '23, year -on-year increase of 40%.

items.statement: Own brand revenue 54% of total (INR ~93 crore) from 21% of SKUs
items.quote: So, regarding the percentage of revenue, it is close to 54%. And regarding the percentage of the total SKUs we sell, it is only 21%. 21% of our own branded products contribute to 54% sales.

items.statement: Exclusive distribution brands revenue not significant yet
items.quote: Okay. That number is not significant currently. We are trying to grow that. So, overall, the companies, which we are doing exclusively in India, we count them as our own brands for the country, because we can have a better margin on them.

items.statement: Baldus revenue under INR 2 crore in FY24, initial stage
items.quote: Last year, I th ink it was under INR2 crores sales from Baldus overall. So, there is not much significant contribution from that.

items.statement: 24-hour delivery live in parts of Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore; testing phase
items.quote: We are currently able to deliver products within 24 hours within Delhi, Bombay, and some parts of Bangalore, b ut not all the products and not all the orders. This is under testing.

items.statement: In-house price monitoring tool enables competitive pricing
items.quote: Our in -house price monitoring tool empowers us to offer competitive pricing, ensuring our customers will get the best possible value.

items.statement: Own brands sourced from ~30 countries, mostly China, also South Korea, Brazil, Germany, USA
items.quote: Sir, Mostly in China, but not only China. We have brands from South Korea. We have products from Brazil, Germany, America, and close to 30 countries. We are importing our white label products.

items.statement: 98% online sales from individual dental practitioners; 2% hospitals
items.quote: From the total online sales we do, 98% of that sale comes from the individual dental practitioners and 2% comes from the hospitals.

items.statement: Overall revenue mix: 92% online (B2C), 8% offline (B2B+B2G)
items.quote: I said that from the total online orders we get, 98% is B2C. So overall, if we see the business 92% is coming from online and 8% of the business is coming from offline as far as the last financial year is concerned.

items.statement: Majority revenue from Tier-2/3 cities where DentalKart is secondary source; Tier-1 limited by strong traditional supply chain
items.quote: is coming from Tier -2 and tier -3. Tier -4, we have a problem because we are not delivering faster. We are on the way to deliver faster. Tier -1 because there is a very strong traditional supply chain established in those cities

items.statement: Most revenue from customers using DentalKart as secondary source for hard-to-find products
items.quote: Secondary source. Majority of the revenue is coming from a large number of customers who are keeping us as a secondary source because they are not able to find the products locally or they are able to find a lot of new products on our website which they wa nt to buy again and again.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 76 from 70; turnover ratio 4.8x; unoptimized due to rapid warehouse expansion
items.quote: the current inventory has gone up to 76 days from 70 days in the last financial year. And the turnover ratio is 4.8, which we will make better with time. But currently it is un-optimized because of rapid expansion in the warehousing section.

items.statement: Inventory mostly own brands due to MOQs and multi-warehouse distribution
items.quote: It is mostly our own brands. Because we have to follow MOPs when we buy products from international markets. And we also have to distribute our own branded products in the other warehouses. So, we have to increase the inventory.

items.statement: Dead inventory policy: liquidate non-moving >1 year at cost or below; clearance sales for near-expiry items
items.quote: Sir, an inventory which is beyond one year and it has not been sold beyond one year. And even if it is non -expiring, we have a policy to liquidate that in the open market. At maybe our cost rate or maybe below that. For perishable goods, for the products which are expirable, we run a sale before they become short expiring.

items.statement: M&A for manufacturing possible but nothing to announce
items.quote: There is a possibility to do that. It is likely, but currently we don't have anything to inform the market about.

items.statement: Trading volumes declined due to international companies unable to register under new drug license policy; expected to recover in FY25
items.quote: the trading volumes have gone down because a lot of international companies have not been able to register themselves in the new drug license policy in India. So, this will subside this year and we expect those revenues to come back in this financial year.

items.statement: International expansion not in next 2-3 years; focus remains on India
items.quote: Yes, in the long term, we are looking to go beyond India, but in the short term next 2 years, 3 years our focus is only India because it's a big market and we have a long way to go.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 30-33% for FY25 despite new facility ramp-up
items.quote: So, on a consolidated basis, we still are confident enough that we will be able to maintain a 30% to 33% EBITDA margin on the overall business.

items.statement: Plan to add 150-250 beds in Tanzania and India by end of FY25; manufacturing unit in Mwanza, Tanzania
items.quote: Moreover, plans are in place to augment the commission bed capacity by about 150 to 250 beds through the establishment of UMC Hospital facilities in Tanzania and India before the end of fiscal year '2025. Additionally, the forthcoming commissioning of a manufacturing unit in Mwanza, Tanzania underscores UniHealth' dedication to providing top-tier healthcare services on a global scale.

items.statement: Target 150-250 commission beds in India by end FY25 across 2-3 facilities in western India
items.quote: The company targets to achieve a commission bed capacity of 150 to 250 beds by the end of Fiscal '2025, which will be spread across two to three facilities, primarily in the western part of India.

items.statement: Consultancy projects with combined 1,250 beds under execution across India, Asia, Africa
items.quote: Under our unique design, build, and operate model, UniHealth provides healthcare consultancy services and presently has projects with a combined bed capacity of 1,250 beds under various stages of execution, spread across India and multiple countries in Asia and Africa.

items.statement: Consultancy vertical EBITDA margin nearly double hospital vertical due to low incremental manpower cost
items.quote: That is why the overall EBITDA margins and profit margins for that vertical are significantly higher, almost twice that of the margins that we have from the medical centers and hospitals vertical.

items.statement: Nigeria local currency revenue grew ~40% YoY but 40% Naira depreciation muted INR consolidation
items.quote: If we look at a consolidated basis, this year though the revenue upstream has just been around 9% to 10%, in a local currency format, the growth has been much higher. This was a year where in Nigeria we witnessed a 40% depreciation of the currency compared to the previous financial year. So, though the revenue growth for Nigeria was 40%, because of the depreciation in the currency, we were not abl

items.statement: Nigeria cash-pay patients 65-75%; Uganda corporate/insurance cycles 2-7 months; Tanzania NHIF ~90-100 days; India govt schemes 4-9 months
items.quote: For example, in Nigeria, the cash patient base, the patients who pay upfront or immediately on delivery of the treatment services, that forms almost 65% to 75% of the patient base because insurance or credit market is not a big portion of the healthcare services model in Nigeria. Now compared to this, when we come to a country like Uganda where there are, though the insurance market is not as big,

items.statement: Working capital days: Nigeria ~55-60 days; Uganda ~4-4.5 months; Tanzania ~90-100 days; India govt schemes 4-9 months
items.quote: So, going from country to country, that model keeps varying and accordingly, our working capital requirement keeps changing where in Nigeria working capital requirement is significantly lower. It is just about I think 55 to 60 days. In Uganda, that goes up to almost four, four-and-a-half months. So, it keeps changing. In India, there may be facilities where we are catering to the requirements of a

items.statement: Long-term borrowings reduced from Rs 36 cr to Rs 12 cr; debt-equity from 1.45x to 0.18x; operating cash flow Rs 4.56 cr vs Rs 1.33 cr
items.quote: Our long-term borrowings reduced from 36 crores to 12 crores accompanied by a decrease in the debt-equity ratio from 1.45x in fiscal year '23 to 0.18x in fiscal year '24. Our operating cash flow has increased to 4.56 crores from 1.33 crores in the previous fiscal year, reflecting enhanced operational efficiency of the company.

items.statement: Adding IVF, ophthalmology, cardiology at existing Uganda and Nigeria hospitals; IVF revenue $4,500-6,000 per patient, cash-pay
items.quote: We are looking at an average revenue per patient in the range of $4,500 to $6,000. And these kind of treatments are usually paid for in cash by the patient. There is no credit. There are no insurance coverages. There are no corporates which are actually paying for these.

items.statement: Target: no single geography >25-30% of consolidated revenue by FY26 (Uganda currently 60%)
items.quote: The target for us is that by fiscal year '25-'26, the contribution from a single geography does not exceed 25% to 30% to the consolidated financials of the company. So, with that particular target in mind, the expansion strategy of the company is being structured and formulated.

items.statement: Navneet Learning LLP divested 5.12% stake in K12 Techno Services to Venturi Partners for INR225 crores, reducing stake to 14.92% from cumulative investment of INR118 crores
items.quote: our subsidiary, Navneet Learning LLP, where Navneet Education Limited holds 93% stake , has entered into a definitive agreement with Venturi Partners, P fund from Singapore, to divest a small fraction, which is 5.12% stake of the company, which is valued at INR225-odd crores.

items.statement: NCLT approved merger of Genext Students and demerger of edtech business from Navneet Futuretech into Navneet Education, effective in FY24 accounts with FY23 comparatives restated
items.quote: Further, in the month of May, Navneet has received final order from NCLT regarding the merger proposal. In this regard, we have given merger effective in present accounts for FY '24 and reinstated the comparative numbers for FY '23 as well.

items.statement: Publishing segment expected to have nominal growth in FY25 with no major growth due to no syllabus change in Maharashtra and Gujarat
items.quote: So in the current year, that is FY '24, '25, we are not looking at major growth in publishing segment. Whatever new introduction of titles on our own that we have done and also revision of certain titles that we have done for -- particularly for the higher grades, that is, 8th, 9th and 10th grade, we will see a little upward.

items.statement: Stationery exports guided to grow 10-15% in FY25 including recovery of INR40 crore loss from US restrictions in FY24
items.quote: As far as exports stationery is concerned, as I just explained over the call that we had a loss of production. But this year, we are very definitive of growing between 10% and 15% for sure.

items.statement: Domestic stationery guided to grow 12-15% in FY25 with new non-paper categories being introduced
items.quote: Yes. Again, here, we had mentioned between 12% and 15% for the domestic business growth.

items.statement: Indiannica Learning expected to return to FY23 revenue levels and grow 5-7% volume in FY25, implying 12-13% overall growth
items.quote: So for FY '25, as far as revenues are concerned, we'll come back to FY '23 numbers, that is for sure. And over and above that, we should be growing by around between 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Stationery margins expected to improve by ~100 basis points in FY25 vs FY24 due to lower paper prices
items.quote: It will be around 100 basis points better than FY'24 because part of the year last year, we had to face the higher prices of paper, which is not the case.

items.statement: Capex guidance: FY25 land/building INR30 cr, machinery INR40-45 cr; FY26 land/building INR60 cr, machinery INR70-80 cr; plus INR40 cr advance capitalization in FY25
items.value: INR30-odd crores in FY'25 and around INR60-odd crores in FY'26
items.quote: So FY'25 in -- see, as far as -- I will split that between two, land and building and the machineries. So as far as land and building is concerned, part of that advanced money were already paid, which is shown in current asset and which will get capitalized in the current year. So around INR40-odd crores will be capitalized in the current year for which payments have already been made in the previ

items.statement: Capacity constraints limit stationery growth to 10-15% in FY25; new capacity being built for future growth with 3x asset turnover on machinery investment
items.quote: So you're right that capacity constraint is one reason that we will not be able to grow better -- more than what I just mentioned. And secondly, whenever we introduce new product or product categories, the benefit of that is achieved in the second and third year.

items.statement: Stationery demand driven by shift from unorganized to organized sector (22-23% organized share in paper stationery) and China+1 export opportunity as preferred vendor to US retailers
items.quote: So overall aspiration levels in the country are going up for a branded product. And therefore, the segment, which was largely dominated by the unorganized sector, is moving to organized sector. And therefore, there itself is a big opportunity for the organ ized player, a branded company, to sell its

items.statement: Introducing AI-designed stationery in Q4 FY24; launching 2 non-paper stationery categories in FY25 (tested in exports); blending edtech with publishing for CBSE and SSC schools
items.quote: During Q4 FY '24, we introduced designs created through AI technology, and the market response to these launches were quite satisfactory. Also, the company is exploring phased introduction of various products in non-paper stationery segment in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Paper prices stable for last 4-5 months; publishing prices not increased in FY25, some higher-grade titles reduced in size and price due to lower costs
items.quote: It is broadly same. Sonaal Kohli: Last 4 months, 5 months, no major change

items.statement: Stationery is seasonal back-to-school business with major sales in two quarters; quarter-on-quarter comparisons not meaningful due to order timing shifts between March and April
items.quote: Now this -- again, I will suggest all my dear investors or analysts if you try comparing quarter-on-quarter for a, a seasonal business, it will always -- you will have questions. So my request would be to look at yearly basis because here, it is -- we are in the midst of season.

items.statement: K12 stake sale proceeds (INR225 cr) to be reinvested in stationery capacity over 2-3 years instead of using balance sheet cash or raising debt
items.quote: So for last couple of quarters, I've been talking our major focus on stationery business. Publishing business is otherwise quite well set. But the opportunity in stationery business domestically or in exports are humongous. And not only with the product ca tegory that we are in, we need to add a couple of more categories. So for all that, company will have to make reasonable investments continuous

items.statement: Edtech business loss INR9.5 cr in Q4 FY24 and INR44-45 cr for full FY24 (including severance costs); expected to reduce to INR25-30 cr in FY25 and breakeven in 2 years
items.quote: net, for FY '24, we would have lost around INR9.5 crores in the current quarter -- in the last quarter, that is, FY -- Q4 '24. Mohammed Patel: And full year? Sunil Gala: Full year loss was, including the both businesses, around INR44 crores

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR1,693 cr (+3.5% YoY), EBITDA INR299 cr (17.6% margin), PAT INR189 cr; domestic stationery INR407 cr (+7%), exports +4%
items.quote: Our FY '24 revenue experienced a meagre growth of 3.5%, reaching to INR1,693 crores compared to INR1,636 crores in the same period last year. EBITDA of FY '24 amounted to INR299 crores, with EBITDA margin of 17.6%. And our profit after tax was INR189 crores.

items.statement: Publishing volume declined ~2% in FY24 vs FY23; edtech revenue INR21.5 cr in FY24 vs INR15 cr in FY23
items.quote: But for FY -- there was no volume growth in FY '25. It would be around 2% lower volume. I mean we could sell lesser quantity in FY '24 over '23, so around 2%, we had reduction in sales volume.

items.statement: US market restrictions caused INR40 cr opportunity loss in stationery exports in FY24 (8-10% of export revenue); Red Sea crisis disrupted export operations
items.quote: Also, as you may recall, due to restriction imposed in the US market for some of our product categories, there was an opportunity loss of around INR40 crores during FY '24. This product actually contributes 8% to 10% of our export revenue.

items.statement: Indiannica Learning faced higher sales returns and lost schools wanting integrated tech+textbook solutions (Indiannica lacks tech offering)
items.quote: Coupled with that, FY'24, we did see a higher percentage of returns, which is normally a case in the industry. So it was beyond our expectations, some higher percentage of returns that we received.

items.statement: Rationalizing sales teams across book and technology businesses; technology facility now shared across publishing and stationery
items.quote: We are in the process of reducing sales teams, which were there for both book business and technology business. So we have started rationalizing there as well.

items.statement: K12 stake sale aimed at unlocking shareholder value; balance 14.92% stake (carrying cost ~INR60-65 cr) to be held for 2-3 years until strategic holders exit
items.quote: So carrying cost of the balance cost would be -- I have not seen the accounting effects of this, but around INR60 crores to INR 65-odd crores would be the cost for the balance in equity that we are owning.

items.statement: NEP implementation not happening in FY25; publishing growth dependent on government curriculum decisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat
items.quote: We will, of course, await for the decision from respective governments. And as soon as that comes, we'll start publishing for the subsequent year.

items.statement: Publishing faces competition from second-hand books (no curriculum change in 6 years) and schools creating own content; stationery benefits from organized shift
items.quote: Couple of schools have started creating their own content as well. And there is a bit of confusion among the school users that what all products to be used.

items.statement: Stationery exports directly to US retailers (not distributors or branded); 4 major CBSE schools currently using blended print-digital offering; SSC schools starting to demand digital solutions
items.quote: We have none neither of that. So, we export to the end customer, that is, the retailers of the developed country that is majorly to the U.S. So, we export directly to the retailers.

items.statement: SFA (Sports For All) championships expanded to 15 cities in FY25 with 20,000-30,000 students per event; strong IP creation attracting brand sponsorships but not yet monetized
items.quote: But now that they have created -- they did around 9 SFA championships in '23, '24. And that also has attracted many, many brand companies to look at the opportunity to either sponsor or give advertisement. So this year, for the '24, '25, they have planned in 15 cities, and number of students are rising in every event, so between 20,000 to 30,000 students are participating in each event.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA positive in the coming year but declines to give forward-looking revenue or PAT targets
items.quote: We think we will stay EBITDA positive. But beyond that, we don't think we can really give any forward-looking statements.

items.statement: Company turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY24 after focusing on cost reduction
items.quote: In the past few quarters, we've been indicating that we'll take all our efforts to get the company back to EBITDA positive and consistently improve the bottom line from there. And we're happy to say that in this quarter, we have done EBITDA positive

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at USD 188 million providing healthy visibility
items.quote: Our unexecuted order book stood at a healthy USD 188 million, giving us a good start to the next year.

items.statement: Q4 order bookings grew 19% year-over-year to USD 27.9 million
items.quote: Q4 witnessed a 19% year-over-year increase in order bookings from USD23.4 million to USD 27.9 million this year Q4.

items.statement: Recurring revenue grew 13% year-over-year in FY24 versus 5% last year
items.quote: Despite challenges and headwinds, our recurring revenue grew at a healthy pace of 13% year-over-year compared to 5% last year.

items.statement: Cloud/SaaS orders constitute 60% of revenue and continue to grow at a healthy pace
items.quote: Our cloud orders that are primarily subscription-based SaaS solutions continue to grow at a healthy pace with a 60% revenue recorded from the cloud or SaaS customers.

items.statement: Signed Korean Air deal worth north of USD 10 million, one of the largest in company history
items.quote: Korean Air the largest order and it is to the north of $10 million. We don't want to give an exact number.

items.statement: Onboarded Deloitte and BDO as strategic partners to redefine payroll landscape
items.quote: On partnership on alliance front, this year witnessed the onboarding of Deloitte and BDO as a key strategic partner to redefine the payroll landscape and we continue to work with them very closely on getting into the market.

items.statement: Launched Ramco Payce SaaS payroll platform; 13+ roadshows completed with high demo requests
items.quote: One of the significant milestones this quarter earlier was the launch of Ramco Payce. It's a modern SaaS-based platform, which is giving good traction and showing promise in various markets. Till date, we had over 13 events across India, Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Middle East, where Ramco Payce has been demoed to several customers and prospects, and we've received tremendous response and a lot

items.statement: Payce demo-to-order conversion expected in 2-3 quarters; revenue impact post-H2 FY25
items.quote: These conversations, given that we deal with mid to large-scale enterprises, typically take 2 to 3 quarters before these transition from demo to possibly orders and then revenue is there. So we'll only start to see this post-H2.

items.statement: Korean Air deal execution timeline 5-7 years including AMCs; revenue recognition front-loaded
items.quote: Typically, our execution timelines, including the AMCs would be looking at 5 to 7 years. That would be the indicated timeline.

items.statement: Recurring revenue at INR 320 crores out of INR 526 crores total revenue for FY24
items.quote: Out of INR526 crores, INR320 crores is recurring revenue.

items.statement: Expense run rate around INR 130 crores considered a baseline guideline for coming quarters
items.quote: I think you can take that as a guideline. There is a baseline run rate for the expenses; if you're asking, yes, you can consider that.

items.statement: MRO market niche with few operators but active interest; Korean Air win provides credibility
items.quote: Whereas the airline MRO, particularly engine MRO and airframe MRO are very niche fields. There are not too many operators there, but we have seen a lot of active interest. It is based on the solution that we have at this point of time. So we do see an active interest and the market potential is pretty good.

items.statement: Defence opportunities have 18-24 month gestation; currently more bullish on MRO side
items.quote: Defence, it usually takes a very long gestation period. That time also, it's around 18 to 24 months, what we are seeing. And right now, MRO has moved faster than others because this is in the non-defence area.

items.statement: Sales force expansion selective; focus on existing markets first for 12-18 months before new territories
items.quote: We'll also be very selective in terms of which markets we'll add more sales folks as well. We don't want to expand too aggressively into new areas because we think the depth is quite large in our existing markets itself.

items.statement: Accelerated growth expected only after 12-18 months; current focus on EBITDA and cash control
items.quote: Since we're are in the turnaround journey as well right now, I would say it will still take another 12 to 18 months to expect any accelerated growth. Right now, it's all about EBITDA and cash control, making sure that we remain profitable as a company.

items.statement: Signed 11 deals above $1 million in FY24 including Korean Air
items.quote: We signed 11 deals over the year above $1 million and in Q4, we added, as we mentioned before, the Korean Air, which is a very large deal for us.

General Atomics deal gone live as planned

Mr. Balaji, currently Deputy CFO, will take over the role of Chief Financial Officer with effect from 1st June 2024

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance reverse merger back on track; expected to complete in a couple of quarters; exploring third-party investment in Hinduja Housing Finance
items.quote: The reverse merger process is back on track. It had some procedural issues more than anything else. So, otherwise what was envisaged as the original merger strategy continues. So, we expect that this may take a couple of more quarters.

items.quote: And that was because of OBD-II norms that had forced some prebuy. So, we have to just keep in perspective that if we exclude that period of high base number because of which the industry degrew, industry has been growing before that by 8%-9%.

items.statement: Dedicated Freight Corridor impact not expected in short run; TCO model not working yet, fundamental issues to be resolved over few years

items.statement: Switch India turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY24; expected to remain EBITDA positive in FY25; no major investment needed in H1 FY25

items.statement: Market share gains to come from product superiority and expanding reach, not discounting; confident of increasing share in trucks and buses

items.statement: Strong interest in eLCV from e-commerce and logistics multinationals for green last-mile; order book building since March launch
items.quote: There is a lot of interest from e-commerce and logistic companies, especially many multinationals who are looking for the last mile to be green as well. So, I would say that it is early days, but a lot of strong interest.

items.quote: No, this mission, actually this is mission 4, - Mission 4+ rather, and the effort is to try and attempt to do it in the current year or max next year.

items.quote: No. The mission that we have outlined for ourselves is from domestic production only. This doesn't include anything from Mozambique.

items.statement: Maharatna status conferred August 2023; Vision 2040 aims to double revenue by 2040 via E&P, downstream, alternative energy
items.quote: OIL's vision to become an integrated energy player is backed by aggressive growth plans aiming to double its revenue by 2040. The growth plans are underpinned by substantial Capex investments, spanning exploration, production, downstream and alternative energy ventures.

items.statement: Management expects MRR potential of INR 14-16 crore from current CAPEX over next couple of months
items.quote: we believe that like the MRR potential with the current CAPEX that we have already done would be of the order of anywhere between like 14 to 16 crores from the current MRR number like we should be able to achieve over like next couple of months.

items.statement: Management targets INR 800 crore CAPEX over next 12 months in ideal scenario
items.quote: In an ideal world, like we would like to end another $100 million or about Rs.800 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: CAPEX funding to combine bank financing, leasing, vendor financing and equity raise
items.quote: It's will have to be a combination of things including like financing from banks and leasing partners and vendor financing and some equity raise.

items.statement: Demand for cloud GPU workloads expected to increase as industry shifts to GPU-centric computing
items.quote: The demand is only going to increase as the industry shifts to more cloud GPU centric workloads. That demand is only going to increase in the industry.

items.statement: Differentiation through software capabilities and workload understanding creates long-term value
items.quote: that insight into the workload, that ability to understand the need for the workloads and implementing those in the software. That product differentiation is what creates long-term value for our customers.

items.statement: Customer base includes SMEs, higher education, research, startups and partner ecosystem; no migration imperative observed
items.quote: The nature of our customers like primarily is the four different buckets today. So one is of course, like we have the SME segment, which continues to be our main the bulk of our customers, then we have the higher education and research category, then we are back with a bang with working with a lot of startups today.

items.statement: Revenue primarily from India; focus on EMEA and US markets for international expansion
items.quote: currently, like our focus continues to be in India, although we would obviously not refuse any customers coming from outside as well. So from a focus outside your perspective, like majorly we are focused on the EMEA market and the US market.

items.statement: Team size approximately 140-150; organic hiring continues across technology, marketing and operations
items.quote: Broadly, we have claim to somewhere between 140 to 150 people in the team. So approximately about 150 and we continue to grow the team organically.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA INR 48 crore with 45% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 EBITDA INR 15 crore with 68% YoY growth
items.quote: EBITDA is 48 crore, representing a growth of 45% on year-on-year basis

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR 95 crore with 43% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 revenue INR 29 crore with 67% YoY growth
items.quote: revenue from operations stood at INR 95 crore representing a growth of around 43% year-on-year basis

items.statement: GPU supply constraints easing; normal integration lead times expected going forward
items.quote: There is always going to be some queue. But it's not going to be the longest queue that we have seen in the past of that type okay, like we are looking at 52 weeks, 56 weeks, 60 weeks and so on. That is not going to be the future.

items.statement: InfiniBand 3.2 Tbps deployed to handle unstructured data at scale for AI/ML workloads
items.quote: the overall idea is that , what is difference between the old world o f the CPU and the storage and the new world of CPU plus GPU plus very high speed panel file system kind of storage and so on

items.statement: Management sees no risk of GPU investment obsolescence; GPU compute shift is irrevocable
items.quote: I don't see there is any risk, the process of going to the GPU is irrevocable. The kind of exponential computing offered by GPU is kind of like really changes the era in which we are operating.

items.statement: Services purchased (data center, power, bandwidth, software licenses) scale with revenue; percentage decreases incrementally with volume
items.quote: So the services would be like in the same proportion as the revenue or a way that they will increase with the revenue in a certain incremental percentage fashion.

items.statement: Right-of-use assets relate to lease-to-own equipment; data center services rented not leased under IndAS 116
items.quote: leasing relate to the equipment and this is all lease to own kind of equipment.

items.statement: Government AI announcements indicate exponential data center capacity growth over next five years
items.quote: one of course that the data center capacity required for artificial intelligence is going to kind of, exponentially grow over next five years or so.

items.statement: Expecting 30% revenue increase in FY25 with PAT margin of 6-6.5%
items.quote: Considering the overall growth in the spice market and our future plans we are expecting a 30% increase in our revenue in FY '25. This strategy is focusing on increasing our brand and PAT margin would be in range of 6% to 6.5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Acquired Vita Green Products for INR7.75 crore including plant, machinery and brand
items.quote: I'm very happy to announce that to cater above both sectors, we recently signed a terms sheet with Vita Green Products Private Limited, which are located at Rajkot, Gujarat.

items.statement: Vita Green peak revenue was INR30 crore in 2021, FY23 revenue INR20 crore, profit INR65 lakh
items.quote: The top peak of the company was in 2021 and that was around INR30 crores. And this company was 100% acquisition base and we have acquired it at INR7.75 crores, including the plant and machinery and brand.

items.statement: 50% of acquisition consideration paid; balance to be paid after fixed assets removed from Vita Green
items.quote: We have paid almost 50% to the company and as I mentioned earlier that we have acquired the plant and machinery and the brand itself, while some fixed assets like land, building are in the name of Vitagreen.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Vita Green manufacturing capacity; can utilize 70-80% in FY25
items.quote: Yeah, in FY '25, we can utilize more than 70 -80% of Vitagreen. Because Vitagreen has production line of only blended and instant mix. While ground spices are acquired by some vendors, which we are currently providing by Madhusudan Masala. So, I don't think any more capex to be utilized in manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Blended spices EBITDA margin expected to improve significantly in FY25; current blended margins below 20% vs established players at 20-25%
items.quote: Yeah, it is a fair. So, because after adding the blended spices and instant mix, our EBITDA margin must be improved.

items.statement: Powder/blended spices margins almost double whole spices margins
items.quote: Second question of the margins in whole spices and powder spices is margins were almost double for the powder spices.

items.statement: Spice industry valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY24 growing at 10% CAGR; only 35% branded share
items.quote: The spiciest industry is valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY '24 and is growing at a CAGR of 10%. And the noticeable thing in this industry is that only 35% market share is hold by branded companies.

items.statement: Branded sales share increased to 56% from 47% driving margin expansion
items.quote: The PAT margin was increased because our market share of branded sales in total revenue was increased to 56% from 47%.

items.statement: Vita Green adds 228 SKUs (mostly small INR5/10 packets) taking combined portfolio to 500+ SKUs
items.quote: They have 228 SKUs in their product portfolio and we at Madhusudan Masala have 272 SKUs. So our SKUs portfolio will be more than 500 after this acquisition.

items.statement: Vita Green distribution network covers Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir; 19 million small SKUs sold annually
items.quote: The main strong factor of this company is that their super scopes and distributed network are widely spreaded in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, and Jammu, Kashmir.

items.statement: Targeting HoReCa segment for whole spices with consistent quality supply
items.quote: So, the main concern for that is to quality that lose whole spices are not coming in consistent quality and we are supplying them consistent quality to all these HoReCa business.

items.statement: Working capital requirement 40-45% of turnover; inventory INR40-45 crore at INR160 crore revenue; debt sufficient for INR160-250 crore turnover
items.quote: If you're going to see our balance sheet, in the financial year '26, there is almost INR20 crores to INR25 crores stock is maintained on an average. But as of now, we have reached to the turnover of the 160, we have to maintain at least INR40 to INR45 crores of stock.

items.statement: 70% of raw material procured in season to ensure consistent quality year-round
items.quote: So, we procure our required procurement was 70% procurement was done in respected season only.

items.statement: Current debt level sufficient for INR160-250 crore turnover; will increase if turnover grows beyond
items.quote: No, no. For this type of INR160 crores to INR250 crores is enough. But in the near future, if turnover is going to be increased indefinitely, that will also increase.

items.statement: Balance 50% acquisition payment from internal accruals and promoter unsecured loans
items.quote: Yeah. Also, some amount from internal actuals and some will be coming by way of unsecured loan from promoters.

items.statement: Installed capacity 2400 metric tons; chili powder at 62% utilization; turmeric/coriander have sufficient capacity
items.quote: No, as of now, I don't think we have to increase our capacity, production capacity, because we have almost 2400 metric ton capacity installed in our unit. And turmeric coriander has more than sufficient capacity we have.

items.statement: Turmeric sourced from Maharashtra; sometimes procure semi-finished powder instead of raw dry turmeric for cost reasons
items.quote: No, because turmeric, we are sourcing turmeric from Maharashtra. So, sometimes it happens that if we procure raw, dry turmeric instead of powdered turmeric, it costs more than a powder product.

items.statement: Only papad, soya chunks and asafoetida procured from vendors; all other products manufactured in-house
items.quote: No. We have all products manufactured in -house, but except three products, like papad, soya chunks, and Asafoetida. Three products are procured directly from vendors and we repaid the change.

items.statement: Products listed on Amazon and JioMart; own e-commerce website generating good numbers; margins similar to offline after returns
items.quote: Yeah, Disha, we have already placed our products in Amazon and JioMart and already started this selling from these two platforms and also trying to place our products in more e-commerce platforms and quick commerce.

items.statement: Targeting unorganized market (65% share) not competing with established brands; using consumer/retail schemes for retention
items.quote: As of now, you see the spices industry has very big numbers in India, like powder spices has INR1 lakh crores in FY '24. But you can see only 35% market share was acquired by branded companies. So, our main concern was not to compete with existing established players. We are targeting unorganized market, which are not any good brand or loose sales.

items.statement: Retail prices lower than established players; offer good trade margins and schemes instead of price cuts
items.quote: No, we are offering good margins to our sales channels and our retail price for consumers are also lower from established players. So, to affect the retail consumers also.

items.statement: Marketing plan includes August 2024 Mumbai exhibition, shop signage, social media, local cable ads, product blend localization
items.quote: We have planned one exhibition in August 24 at Mumbai called [Anugapur 21:22] for acquiring new distributors, super stockists to our western region. And another step is to deploy a shop Asia to our retailers and some social media marketing are also planned.

items.statement: Northern expansion using Vita Green's existing distributors in UP, Bihar, Jharkhand; Madhya Pradesh/Rajasthan need new channels
items.quote: Because these regions were already sold by Vitagreen earlier from last 10 years. So we appointed the same distributors of Vitagreen to Madhusudan. That's why these states are covered because middle states like Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan are left because Vitagreen do not have sales channels in this part.
