items.statement: Targets 30% top-line growth over next 12 months on recruitment and manpower front
items.quote: We have already have had a few contracts that have come our way at the beginning of the year. And that in itself will add to the top line of the organisation. So, I don't see that a 30% upside should be a problem, over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Targets ~3% operating margin in FY25, definitely by FY26
items.quote: We can expect a range of about 3 odd percent in FY'25. That's what we are targeting. But if not '25, '26, definitely.

items.statement: Historical PAT margin ~4%; current dip due to recruitment/IT staffing slowdown and senior hiring
items.quote: We've typically been working with a 4% sort of a PAT margin in the past. It's not just been the past, it's not just been FY'23, but before that also, if you look at it, we were always in the 4 odd percent sort of a range as an organisation.

items.statement: Recruitment and IT staffing revenue declined ~40-42% YoY in FY24
items.quote: So, it's been about a 40%, 42% sort of a decline, Jatin. In terms of absolute numbers in the recruitment and the IT Staffing business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA fell from ₹23.6 cr to ₹9.4 cr in FY24
items.quote: The revenue overall was ₹1,018 crores as compared to ₹768 crores in the previous year, where the EBITDA was ₹23.6 crores to ₹9.4 crores for FY'24.

items.statement: Seeing pickup in IT recruitment mandates from IT services companies and US clients; RFPs and vendor renewals increasing
items.quote: We started getting demand, Jatin. The science for us is the number of open mandates that we are receiving from our customers. And this usually starts with IT services company.

items.statement: Global HR business grew 15-20% in FY24 vs 100% in FY23; US market opening up now
items.quote: year, it's 15%, 20%. Rahil Dasani: Got it. Vidur Gupta: Last financial year, we had grown 100% FY'23

items.statement: New contracts bagged at start of year will contribute ~12-13% top-line growth
items.quote: The contracts that we have bagged will not help us reach a 30% mark, but they will contribute around a 12% to 13 % odd growth in the top line of the organisation.

items.statement: ~₹15 cr deployed for under-construction office premises (short-term loans & advances)
items.quote: So around ₹15 odd crores, Rahil.

items.statement: ₹55 cr of IPO proceeds still unutilised; used for working capital in staffing/engineering contracts
items.quote: So, Rahil we have around ₹55 odd crores of the IPO funds still lying with us.

items.statement: Added sales headcount: Peush Saproo hired as Head of Sales (21 yrs exp) + ~10 member team for RPO/IT staffing
items.quote: We had Mr. Peush Saproo, who's joined us as the Head of Sales for this business. He came in with over 21 years of experience and was with competition heading sale [inaudible ] [0:02:53] grew this team by about 10 members

items.statement: Core team grew to 490 (from 480 in Sep'23); managed headcount 18,875 + 8,279 apprentices
items.quote: Our core headcount was 490 at the end of March '24 as compared to September '23 where the internal headcount was 480 numbers.

items.statement: Electronics trading (mobiles only) to be wound down within FY25; not long-term focus
items.quote: We want to shut it by the end of within this year, not by the end of the year. I'm hoping that we are able to get the other businesses up, and hopefully we'll be able to shut it as soon as possible.

items.statement: Electronics trading grew due to faster capital rotation (3x/month vs usual 2x) in H2
items.quote: There was a lot of turnaround and quick turnaround that happened in the shipments in this H2, where usually, we used to be able to rotate capital twice in the month. However, a number of times, we were able to do it thrice in the last H2.

items.statement: Candidate salary hike expectations dropped from 30-40% to 20-25%, causing offer shopping and lower joining ratios
items.quote: At the moment, the industry is offering more in the range of about 20%, 22%, 25%, which is resulting in a fair amount of retention as well. And a lot of offer shopping, which is why it's not yet corresponding into performance from an organisational standpoint, it will come.

items.statement: Trade receivables ₹78.5 cr includes ~₹10 cr from electronics trading; similar to last year
items.quote: So, trading has some bit of it, Rahi l. I believe it is to the tune of ₹10 odd crores roughly

items.statement: Annual salary cost rose from ~₹14 cr to ~₹22.2 cr (Mar'23 to Mar'24) due to senior hires
items.quote: Annual number, just a second. So, our salary cost has gone up from a ₹14 odd crores to a ₹22.2 odd crores.

items.statement: Achieved Great Place to Work certification in May'24 to attract talent
items.quote: If you did notice, we achieved the great place to work certification also. This came in May this year. We've added it in the presentation.

items.statement: Productivity (managed headcount per core employee) improved from 280 to 348
items.quote: We used, it was previously 280 for the second half of the financial year '23, which is now 348.

items.statement: Manpower supply EBITDA margin 1.1% in H2 vs 1% in H1; electronics trading 0.7% vs 0.9%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the manpower supply was 1.1% in the second half of the year as compared to a 1% in the previous half. And the electronic goods, it was 0.7% as compared to 0.9% in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Added 70 new logos in H2; client attrition routine, no significant losses
items.quote: We added 70 new logos in the H2.

items.statement: Client attrition routine; market consolidating as formalisation drives growth across competitors
items.quote: Nothing significant. So, if we are getting, see there are two ways to look at this, Rahil. One, if you look at it, all the firms are growing in terms of size.

items.statement: Industry-wide slowdown in recruitment/IT staffing; peers also seeing margin pressure
items.quote: If you look at the performance of our competition as well, while we don't like to comment on competition, but in general, the industry, there has been a massive slowdown in the Recruitment and the IT Staffing business, which is starting to come up now.

items.statement: RPO contracts take 3 months to close + 2 months implementation; revenue starts month 4-5
items.quote: Agreement takes about three months to close. Post the agreement about two odd months to usually set up and place the team in place. And at the end of those two months, revenue starts to come.

items.statement: Other operating expenses rose from ₹4.4 cr to ₹11.48 cr due to professional staffing fees and job board costs (₹35 lakh)
items.quote: So, Jatin, what has happened is we have been able to bag a contract, which is not a contract staffing assignment, but it is a professional staffing assignment. So, the fee to those professionals has been put in the other operating expenses.
